entities.name: Eplear
entities.description:
Eplear Camoran was a Bosmer king remembered as the founder of the Camoran Dynasty in year zero of the First Era (1E 0).

The establishment of the Camoran Dynasty marked both the beginning of the First Era and the official recording of historical time in Tamriel. His success in uniting the often divided Bosmeri clans is celebrated as one of the greatest political and military achievements in the history of Tamriel.

Prior to Eplear’s reign, the Bosmer lived in disparate tribal groups with little central organization. Legends hold that Eplear brought these clans together, forming the first unified kingdom of Valenwood. His dynasty would endure in various forms throughout the eras, even after Valenwood came under the influence of external powers such as the Second Empire.

Bosmeri tradition preserves several mythic accounts of Eplear’s rise. One tale claims he was once an ox-herd who vowed to win the hand of a merchant’s daughter by turning the plains of Valen into forest. He is said to have bought her acorns and planted them wherever his oxen grazed, causing the forests of Valenwood to spread.

entities.name: Ezhmaar Sul
entities.description:
Ezhmaar Sul was a male Dunmer, and one of the people directly responsible for the events of the Red Year. He is only called Ezhmaar Sul by his wife, Ilzheven, whereas everyone else calls him Sul.

Sul was the husband of Ilzheven, a female Dunmer who was selected by Vuhon, a friend of Sul, to power Vuhon's Ingenium. The device served to keep the Ministry of Truth aloft, after Vivec disappeared during the events of the Oblivion Crisis, and was powered by souls. Sul attempted to free his wife, but damaged it when Vuhon attempted to stop him. This caused the Ministry to resume its course and crash into Vivec City.

Sul and Vuhon were propelled into Oblivion, specifically the realm of Clavicus Vile. There, they encountered a being called Umbra, who was technically part of Vile, which threw the Umbra Sword into Mundus through the rift the Ingenium created. Vuhon made a deal with Umbra for his life: in exchange, he would build a new Ingenium to allow Umbra to escape Vile's realm. Sul was kept prisoner and tortured for years, but was soon forgotten about. Sul escaped into Azura's realm, who offered him to settle problems for her in exchange of letting him go. Yet, she decided to keep him, so Sul had to escape from her as he had escaped from Vile's realm.

Sul was able to escape Oblivion after decades and return to Mundus. Azura still sent him visions, though of a more helpful nature, so he could get his revenge on Vuhon. While he was sleeping in the Lank Fellow Inn in Chorrol, he received a vision of Umbriel flying over the sea. Sul realized it had to be Vuhon, but he didn't know where to start from. He discovered a book in an otherwise empty shelf: The Most Current and High Adventures of Prince Attrebus.

entities.name: Failed Incarnate
entities.description:
A Failed Incarnate is someone who was the intended Nerevarine, the reincarnation of Indoril Nerevar, as dictated by the Nerevarine Prophecy of Azura. All of these people were thought to be "possessed" by the spirit of the warlord, but had critical flaws that made them destined to fail the fulfillment of the prophecy, and as such were revealed to be false Nerevarines. Many failed incarnates have come and gone since the First Era, but came to an end when the true Nerevarine fulfilled the Prophecy in 3E 427.

The first known intended Nerevarine was Ane Teria, who was a holy crusader of the Tribunal Temple during the Tribunal's golden age in the early First Era, some time after the Battle of Red Mountain in 1E 700. She wrote writings, later known as Apographa, that were suppressed by the Tribunal Temple. She followed the false gods unquestionably, and only began to believe the Nerevarine Prophecy when it was too late.

In the late years of the Tribunate, Idrenie Nerothan was an incarnate who demoralized and repelled the Akaviri invaders during the First Akaviri Invasion in 1E 2703. She knew nothing of Dagoth Ur and the Nerevarine Prophecy until she took refuge with the Ashlanders. She died trying to loot Kogoruhn, the Sixth House capital in the northern Ashlands, considering her actions foolish.

Erur-Dan, another incarnate, saw Morrowind make a treaty with either the Reman Empire during the Four Score War, or the Septim Empire during the Tiber War. Humiliated by the surrender, he swore vengeance against the Empire and Tribunal alike. In later years, he despaired, and died fighting the Blight creatures at Red Mountain.

During the war, she wrote a diary about her experiences, noting her recollections about what it was like when there was peace between the Snow Elves and the Nords, and how the Snow Elves will never be the same again due to the devastation the Atmorans unleashed upon the Elves.

Far-Sighted Uche was an Atmoran warrior who lived during the Merethic Era. He was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

On Atmora Uche was among the students of wise war-teacher Adrimk. He did not have earned his name as a warrior yet.

Along with Adrimk herself and bunch of other war-students Uche joined Ysgramor's cause to slay the savage elves who were to blame for the Night of Tears. On the Day of Final Passage he had become a crewmember of the Darumzu, longboat under command of Captain Ylgar.

During the voyage to Skyrim, known to Nedes as Mereth, the Darumzu was caught in Storm of Separation and was separated from the rest of the fleet. However, the boat sailed out safely, arriving at Hsaarik Head just a bit late. Uche finally earned his warrior name, Far-Sighted Uche, in Tamriel. However, no further details on how it happened have been recorded.

He built the city of Wayrest from the ground up, and continued to found the Gardner Dynasty, which ended in the Second Era during the Interregnum as a result of the Knahaten Flu which whipped every remaining family member of the dynasty.

He authored an unpublished series of poems which can be read in King Farangel's Ode to Wayrest.

entities.name: Fervidius Tharn
entities.description:
Fervidius Tharn was a well known member of the Tharn Family who lived during the middle years of the First Era. Fervidius was, at one point, the highest-ranking member of the Alessian Order and was even said to be the Arch-Prelate of the Alessian secret sect known as the Marukhati Selective, being given the title in the year 1E 1188. Fervidius was best known for writing the book Sermons Denouncing the Seventeen Leniencies.

It is said that Fervidius Tharn began his role in the Alessian Order as a humble oblate, but quickly rose through the ranks of the order, becoming the Arch-Prelate of the Order with power rivaling even the Emperors. During this time, the Marukhati Selective, a split sect and internal threat to the Alessian Order, was formed, which was said to have been an enemy of Fervidius. Fervidius then apparently sent members of his order to find the missing pieces of the staff of towers to prevent the Selectives from getting their hands on them, but was eventually betrayed and killed by one of his own. However, other sources heavily imply that Fervidius Tharn was, in fact, the secret-master of the Selective responsible for the Middle Dawn Dragon Break which occurred in 1E 1200.

entities.name: Finna
entities.description:
Finna was a Nord who lived during the late Merethic Era. Finna was instrumental to the Nord's victory during the last battle against the the Snow Elves as she killed their commander.

At the age of twelve, when she was a squire to her mother, she played a brief but important role during the Battle of the Moesring, in Solstheim.

During this battle between the Nords and the Snow Elves, Finna's mother, Jofrior, was slain in front of her by the Snow Prince. In her rage Finna took her mother's sword and threw it at the Snow Prince, killing him while he was still on his horse. By this act Finna, still just a child, sealed the fate of the last remaining bastion of Snow Elves in Skyrim.

entities.name: Fjokki the Bard
entities.description:
Fjokki the Bard is a mentioned-only famous Nord warrior-poet. Rigurt the Brash compared poetry of the warrior-poet Vivec with Fjokki's poetry and found it is "not at all as interesting or bawdy."

"Art of Love and Swordplay" is a mentioned-only book of Fjokki. The Vestige will bring the original edition of this book (unreadable quest item) to Adras Sarethi during the quest "Cultural Exchange."

In the judgment of Adras Sarethi "It details, in epic balladry, the carnal exploits and adventurous deeds of warrior-poet Fjokki. The author claims the work is a true history, but many of the exploits it recounts are highly unlikely. It's lurid trash, and common as guar."

According to catalog of Library of Dusk it is "The popular autobiography of the frisky Nord, Fjokki, whose exploits are unbelievable but strangely compelling. Not rare, but a perennial favorite here at the Library."

entities.name: Flinthild Demon-Hunter
entities.description:
Flinthild Demon-Hunter was a Merethic Era hero and the second member of Khunzar-ri's kra'jun – his company of heroes – who fought against the dragons of Elsweyr along with Nurarion the Perfect, Anequina Sharp-Tongue, and Cadwell, after being convinced to leave her castle in Skyrim.

During the Merethic Era, the Khajiit hero Khunzar-ri, recruiting heroes to fight against the dragons of Elsweyr, traveled to Skyrim to recruit Flinthild after hearing of her might. Finding her at a great feast in the Old Hold of Eastmarch where she had drunk and gorged herself on horker for two weeks, Khunzar-ri duelled her whilst drunk for three continuous days. As they duelled, Flinthild "saw the majesty of Khunzar-ri's graceful form" and took him captive to force him to be her groom. After recovering from her drunken episode, she released Khunzar-ri instead of marrying him.

Sometime later, Khunzar-ri rescued Flinthild from the "Ayleid lair of creeping ebony plants," Black Vine Ruins in the Malabal Tor region of Valenwood, after which she joined his kra'jun. With him, she battled against the dragons until they were sealed away in the Halls of Colossus. After deciding to trap the dragons in the Halls, it was Flinthild and Anequina Sharp-Tongue who devised the plan to siphon the dragon's lifeforce into Jode. Flinthild then took an urn with a sliver of moonlight containting the dragons' lifeforce from Anequina Sharp-Tongue to the Halls of Colossus for the dragons to follow.

Folbert the Wide was a king of Daggerfall during the Second Era, around the 6th century. He took the throne after King Bergamot and many other nobles were killed by the Knahaten Flu around 2E 560. He assisted King Ranser in King Ranser's War in 2E 566 and the subsequent Daggerfall Covenant in 2E 567. He was replaced by King Casimir in the same year.

entities.name: Four Ambitions
entities.description:
The Four Ambitions are four powerful beings associated with Mehrunes Dagon. They were created through a pact between the Longhouse Emperors and the Prince of Destruction, intended to serve as weapons to merge Nirn with the Deadlands.

The Reach chieftain Durcorach the Black Drake made a deal with Mehrunes Dagon. In exchange for aid in conquering Cyrodiil, Durcorach agreed to bring forth the Four Ambitions under the signs and circumstances laid out in the sacred book.

After Durcorach's death in 2E 541, his son Moricar inherited not only the conquests but also the obligations to Dagon. Moricar continued his father's work and performed the ritual that resulted in the creation of the Four Ambitions.

The next emperor, Leovic, inherited the pact and hid the ambitions across Tamriel so that no one could use them prematurely. However, after Leovic's death without naming an heir, the contract was broken and the codicils described in the sacred book were activated. From that point on, anyone who sacrifices the Ambitions in the propper manner could claim the reward once promised to Durcorach and his heirs.

entities.name: Frandar Hunding
entities.description:
Frandar do Hunding Hel Ansei No Shira, commonly known as Frandar Hunding, was a Redguard hero. He was born in 1E 720, in the region of High Desert, on the continent of Yokuda. He grew up in a period of constant turmoil, the civil war in Yokuda, and led his people from the annihilation they faced to their new home in Hammerfell. He is also famous as being the father of his son, Divad.

Frandar belonged to the Sword-Singers. This faction, initially loyal to the Yokudan Empire, originally came from the high-class members of society. They devised training called "The Hall of the Virtues of War." Frandar was a master Ansei (the most skillful of the Sword-Singers) at the height of the turmoil of Torn's death. Many Ansei had hung up their swords and became master artisans instead. Some, however, like Hunding, sought true enlightenment through the dark times.

In 1E 734, Hunding's father died in one of the many uprisings in revolt of the death of Randic Torn, leaving him to look after his four brothers and mother, which he did through his knowledge of the sword. He was in great demand as a guardian and escort, but his reputation preceded him, and multitudes awaited to face him in battle, as they would gain instant fame through defeating him.

By 1E 750, Frandar has fought and won more than ninety duels. Nearly invincible with the sword, he gained such prestige and mastery that he eventually stopped needing to use real swords. He created, and began to use, the Shehai, or "Way of the Spirit Sword." He started using this around his ninetieth duel. During this duel, he had fought the evil Lord Janic and his seven Liches in the process.

entities.description:
Freydis was High Queen of Eastern Skyrim during the Second Era. She was said to have ruled over Windhelm. She was the daughter of High King Logrolf, however, Jarl Svartr of Solitude claimed she was an illegitimate child and thus that she had no claim to the throne. Having ownership over the Crown of Verity, Freydis was named High Queen in the city of Windhelm, and her successors would rule there for years to come.

entities.name: Friar Lylim
entities.description:
Friar Lylim was an Altmeri Trebbite Monk who led an army against Queen Morgiah of Firsthold during the Third Era. As a Trebbite Monk, he valued tradition above every other virtue. Lylim would later flee from battle after his revolt failed.

The revolt was planned by Lady Gialene, daughter of the King of Skywatch, who used her father's gold to pay for a horde of mercenaries. Their army was defeated at the gates of Firsthold, and ended in a panicked, unorganized retreat. He would later send furious notes to Lady Gialene, but they were returned, and even his best secret agents within the Firsthold palace were unable to find her whereabouts.

entities.name: Friga Shatter-Shield
entities.description:
Friga Shatter-Shield was a Nord and the daughter of Tova Shatter-Shield and Torbjorn Shatter-Shield of Clan Shatter-Shield in the city of Windhelm.

Friga was murdered by a serial killer known as The Butcher, and she was also the previous owner of Hjerim, until her mother eventually condemned the estate. Her twin sister, Nilsine Shatter-Shield, and her mother grew heavily depressed after her death, the latter becoming dependent upon alcohol to cope with her death.

Muiri, a shopkeeper in Markarth, knew Friga and the other Shatter-Shields very well. She visited the family after Friga's death, to offer her condolences. Drinking to ease the pain, Muiri met Alain Dufont, who romanced her, hoping to get closer to the Shatter-Shields and exploit their grief for Friga. He succeeded, robbing them and taking their family warhammer and framing Muiri causing the family to resent her and throw her out.

Friga is never actually encountered due to her being the Butcher's first victim. Her murder will always occur before the Dragonborn has first arrived in Windhelm.

entities.name: Froa
entities.description:
Froa was an Atmoran warrior. She was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

Froa was one of the war-teacher Adrimk's students. She earned her name as a warrior on Tamriel and was very close to her Shield-Sister Grosta. They were said to have thought and spoken as one.

Froa joined Ysgramor's cause to slay the savage elves who were to blame for the Night of Tears. On the Day of Final Passage she became a crewmember of the Darumzu, a Atmoran longboat under the command of Captain Ylgar. Joining here were her teacher and her fellow students, most of whom hadn't earned their names yet.

During the voyage to the Tamriel, known to Atmoran as Mereth, Darumzu was caught in the Storm of Separation and became lost. The boat sailed out of the storm safely, however, arriving at Hsaarik Head just a bit late. Unfortunately, there are no further records concerning what happened to Froa after landing.

He patrolled the roads the Black Marsh with his partner-in-crime, Drawing-Flame. They attempted to rob and kill Decumus Scotti, but were interrupted by Archein Right-Foot-Rock, an Argonian trader and plantation owner.

entities.name: Gaiden Shinji
entities.description:
Blademaster Gaiden Shinji was the leader of the Order of Diagna who lived some time during the early-to-mid First Era in a point known as the "Classical Period". The Order of Diagna, with the joint forces of Daggerfall and Sentinel, attacked the Orcish kingdom of Orsinium during Gaiden's leadership. The war is known as the Siege of Orsinium. In 1E 948, King Joile of Daggerfall sent a letter to Shinji saying "The orcs have been much plaguing the Wayresters and impeding traffic to the heart of the land." It took thirty years for the joint armies to breach and destroy Orsinium.

During his lifetime, he was also the founder and original Blademaster of the Imperial City Arena, which was completed shortly before the siege began. Gaiden Shinji was one of the many casualties of the Siege of Orsinium.

After going to Honor's Rest, the archaeological historians, Lozruth and Sharela will be arguing about who is buried inside the tomb. Lozruth argues that it is Orcish hero Baloth Bloodtusk, while Sharela argues that it is Blademaster Gaiden Shinji. They cannot fully confirm their speculations, however, as the tomb doors are currently sealed. Sharela sends the Vestige to the Honor's Rest Catacombs to obtain more information.

Once there, the burial chamber of one of Shinji's disciples, Tamahl, is found. It contains a Memorial Pool, imbued with his memory of Shinji speaking to Lord Trystan, the leader of the Knights of the Dragon during the First Era. After drinking from the pool, you are transported to the memory as Tamahl. There, you can find Shinji arguing with Trystan:

entities.name: Galana Septim
entities.description:
Galana Septim is the daughter of Emperor Uriel Septim II, and is sister to Pelagius Septim II.

Originally, the promise of marriage between Emperor Uriel Septim II and King Mantiarco of Solitude confirmed that she was to marry Mantiarco. But in 3E 80, during a visit from the Nordic ambassador to claim King Mantiarco's promised bride, young Potema, daughter of Pelagius, overheard a discussion of the promise.

She knew Galana was preparing for her wedding with the Duke of Narsis in Morrowind; thinking quickly, Potema crept into the Hall of Records and stole the Promise, leaving no evidence of its existence. Unfortunately for Potema, a replacement bride for the King had to be found or millions in gold were forfeit to King Mantiarco, and so it happened that two years later, at age 14, she herself was wed to the aged Mantiarco. Of Galana, no further records have been found.

entities.name: Gallivere Lariat
entities.description:
Gallivere Lariat or Lariate was a Breton noble from the Kingdom of Shornhelm that served as the royal consort of Empress Katariah after it was apparent that Pelagius Septim III would pass away. He is the biological father of Uriel Septim IV, who was the first indirect descendant to Tiber Septim.

Gallivere Lariat was a noble from the city-state of Shornhelm who garnered the attention of Empress Katariah Septim, who ruled from the Imperial City while her husband, Pelagius Septim III was being treated for his infamous insanity. While he was recovering in his personal cell, Katariah had a relationship with Gallivere, which resulted in the birth of Uriel Septim IV. The relationship was publicly acknowledged, even when Pelagius Septim III was still recovering some time before his death in Betony. Gallivere Lariat derives from a noble family of Shornhelm known as the House Lariat, who are considered distant relatives to Tiber Septim. What happened to Gallivere Lariat is unknown.

Gallivere Lariat's lineage would reside in the Imperial Palace for quite some time, beginning with Uriel Lariat IV. It was difficult for Uriel IV to gain acceptance from the Elder Council, considering his very distant relation to Tiber Septim, and despite the Lariat Family's immense influence, it was still a challenge to be fully recognized as the Emperor. But, Uriel IV managed to hold his own and became a substantial leader of the Third Empire, although the Emperor and the Elder Council would be at odds with each other. Uriel IV's son, Andorak Septim was denied the throne by a vote of the Elder Council, so the throne was given to more closer relative to Tiber Septim, with that relative being Cephorus Septim II. It was not a total loss for Andorak. However, the Elder Council had instead given Andorak his ancestral domain, the Kingdom of Shornhelm was given to Andorak Septim.

entities.name: Garnag
entities.description:
Garnag was an Orsimer assassin for the Dark Brotherhood, residing in the Cheydinhal Sanctuary at the time of the Great War. He hauled the Night Mother's crypt from Bravil after it was raided, and was one of the last surviving members of the Brotherhood in Cyrodiil.

Garnag was sent to aid Listener Alisanne Dupre and others in the defense of the Night Mother's Crypt in Bravil in Sun's Dusk of 4E 188. It was overrun later that month, with Dupre and Andronica perishing while defending it, and Garnag alone surviving. He was gravely injured and lost his right eye, but managed to transport the Night Mother back to Cheydinhal.

In the aftermath of Alisanne's death, Garnag murdered their Sanctuary leader Rasha at the request of Cicero, when Rasha falsely claimed to be the new Listener in 4E 189. Garnag, Cicero, and Pontius were the only surviving members in the sanctuary, and Cicero went mad shortly after. Garnag later left the sanctuary in 4E 191 to look for food, but failed to return after three months. His fate is unknown, with Cicero still receiving no contact of him by 4E 192. but if he still lives, he is likely the only surviving member of the Dark Brotherhood outside of Skyrim.

entities.name: Garridan Stalrous
entities.description:
Garridan Stalrous was a lord and knight of Cyrodiil. He was said to have been a fair and kind ruler.

Garridan Stalrous was the ruler of the settlement known as Farmantle Glens, a community consisting largely of farmers. He lived in a stone keep, alongside the rest of his people, in the northern Jerall Mountains. When a great drought hit the community the twenty-seven families who lived there were starving. Garridan's own grain supply was also in low supply, only being able to sustain himself for a few months before the crisis would also affect him. Searching for a solution to the problem Garridan hired the best sages he could find, and with the gold that remained he bought as much grain from the surrounding communities to sustain his own people.

A month had passed, and winter came closer to Garridan's lands. Garridan's patience was coming close to a breaking point, and the lord had considered selling his keep and belongings if it meant the survival of his people.

After days of travel, the three had come to the cave known as Garridan used Refined Frost Salts to go through a special door, coming to the Frostfire Glade. The sage had spoken truly, in the middle of an enclove, surrounded by rocks, the ewer stood, with water filled to the top. Garridan, who was eager to return with the ewer and end the hunger at Farmantle Glens, took the ewer. After Garridan had taken the ewer, the ground began to shake, the trees appeared to be bending away from the altar, and the sky, which was blue at first, turned gray. Then, suddenly, one of the standing stones near the altar exploded, and a Frost Atronach appeared. Garridan, being a knight, told his squire to run while he himself drew his sword. Still holding the ewer, Garridan tried to damage the creature, but only barely damaged it. Garridan kept swinging at the creature, hoping to damage it, but his attacks were futile. Then, in one hit, the atronach punched the lord, resulting in Garridan falling down and dropping his blade. Being unarmed, Garridan looked at the atronach, which was raising its arm to kill the lord. In a reflex, Garridan kneeled and held the ewer in his hands in a defensive position, resulting in the atronach hitting the ewer.

entities.description:
Gellir was a Nordic High King of Skyrim in the First Era.

Historians have attributed him as a master tactician in his wars against the Dwemer, during which several Dwemer cities, which had been able to held fast against Nords for hundread of years across Skyrim, fell to his armies. It is believed by Nord chroniclers that Gellir's talents were a blessing of the God Shor. While the Dwarves were fighting for the power of the Aetherium, causing internal conflicts, Gellir took the opportunity to conquer the Dwarven Cities within 3 years.

His assault failed and got defeated by Umbriel, after which the General retreated.

entities.description:
King Golkarr gro-Igrun, colloquially known as the "Orc of Wiles," was the ruler of the First Orsinium during the mid-to-late 10th century of the First Era after he succeeded Torug gro-Igron. His reign ended in 1E 980, when he was slain at the hands of his enemies, marking the end of the 30-year Siege of Orsinium.

Golkarr belonged to Clan Igrun, and was crowned the King of Orsinium after Torug gro-Igron's reign ended. Golkarr publicly praised the raids that occurred along the Bjoulsae River, committed by Clan Bagrakh.

The Siege of Orsinium began in 1E 950, with the armies of Daggerfall and Sentinel, as well as the Order of Diagna and Knights of the Dragon, allied against Orsinium. Golkarr was allied with the Orcish clans of Igrun, Bagrakh, Morkul, Tumnosh, Shatul, Fharun, and later the Savage Sons, who defended Orsinium.

The Siege lasted for thirty years, with the three gates designed by Torug to defend the city

After this, he fled to an ancient and abandoned fortress outside the city, Stonekeep. This piece of parchment was eventually returned by the Eternal Champion.

entities.name: Gortwog gro-Nagorm
entities.description:
Gortwog gro-Nagorm was an orc King of the Wrothgarian Mountains, who was involved in both the Warp in the West and the formation of Orsinium.

In 3E 399, Gortwog made a claim to the land of Orsinium, having equal claim to the land as his opponent, the Breton Lord Bowyn. The two were stuck in a deadlock, and as such, by Imperial custom, it was decided that a duel had to be held. Gortwog was granted the right to decide the arms and armor, whereas Lord Bowyn had the right to choose the location. While both also had the right to choose a Champion to fight in their stead, both chose to fight themselves. Despite some training in the armor, Lord Bowyn stood no chance against Gortwog, and was beaten in combat, providing Gortwog with the legal rights to the land.

While the Orsimer were originally not involved in the War of Betony in 3E 402, they were involved in clashes with Wayrest over access to the Bjoulsae River.

Later on during the War of Betony, the Orcs of King Gortwog were said to have been sent out to block a group of Wayrest Scouts from reaching the encamptment of King Lysandus of Daggerfall. While most of the scouts were blocked by the Orcs, some made it through, and are implied to have murdered the King in his tent. Specifically Lord Woodborne was stated to have murdered King Lysandus. Likewise, Gortwog's forces were slain by the Wayrest assassins. Other reports attribute the Orsimer for the death of Lysandus, however.

entities.name: Gothryd
entities.description:
King Gothryd (3E 381 – ???) was the King of Daggerfall. His father, Lysandus of Daggerfall, was killed at the end of the War for Betony in 3E 403, Gothryd was crowned to replace him. His wife is Aubk-i, former princess of Sentinel, who he married in 3E 404. His mother is Mynisera and his grandmother is Nulfaga.

While his father was said to have been very loyal of the Third Empire, it is implied Gothryd himself was not, as a Blades operative declared that if Gothryd obtained both the Mantella and the Totem of Tiber Septim, Tamriel would be thrown into a civil war. In spite of this, in the timeline where Gothryd obtains both items, Daggerfall only destroys Wayrest and Sentinel to gain control over the Iliac Bay.

Lysandus perished one year later, in 3E 403, with official accounts claiming an arrow shot by a Sentinel archer slew him. Upon his slaying, Daggerfall did not waste time and crowned Gothryd as the new king of Daggerfall. In reality Lysandus had made a deal with Gothryd, which Gothryd accepted due to a desire for his father to be happy. They agreed that an impersonator would ride into battle wearing the royal armor of Daggerfall and feign death while Lysandus would escape to join his lover Medora Direnni on the Isle of Balfiera.

While the plan went relatively as planned, the imposter was shot dead by Gothryd instead of merely feigning death, and was then buried under the full royal funeral. Lord Woodborne of Wayrest was tasked with getting the real Lysandus away from the battle, and had asked Lysandus what he would do if he grew bored on Balfiera. Lysandus' answer was that he would sneak back to Daggerfall to give his son advice. This debate would become heated, as Lord Woodborne drew a dagger and stabbed Lysandus - killing him, though he was almost saved by the Orcs of Gortwog gro-Nagorm,

entities.name: Graddock
entities.description:
Lord Graddock was the Redguard ruler of Reich Gradkeep during the War of Betony.

He acted as conciliator between Sentinel and Daggerfall, and eventually convinced both monarchs to meet and make peace. The Treaty of Gradkeep began civilly; the terms of peace were discussed, agreed on, and set to paper. The terms were excessively generous. Camaron had agreed to give up some of his rights to Betony in order to placate the madness of Lysandus and bring peace back to the Iliac Bay. However, it turned out that it was a trick; the treaty was miswritten on purpose, so the Camaron would sign the terms he had not agreed upon. Thus the castle of Reich Gradkeep erupted into bloodbath, and the war continued.

entities.name: Gratian Caerellius
entities.description:
Gratian Caerellius was an Imperial colonial and archeaologist that worked under the East Empire Company during the third era. Gratian was present during the construction of Raven Rock and served his part in the town's growth.

Gratian Caerellius was serving the East Empire Company as a miner for the Raven Rock Mine, which primarily excavates Ebony Ore from the ground. He had helped build the Imperial-Charter township, making it what it is today. With the establishment of Raven Rock, the town was in need of guards and Caerellius decided to join the first regiment of the Raven Rock Guard. Eventually, Gratian returned back to Cyrodiil with his wife and son to explore the ruins of Tamriel under the watch of the East Empire Company. Gratian's exploits throughout Tamriel is left largely unknown, at some point, he garnered an assistance named Millius who documented his findings along with Gratian. Gratian had left Raven Rock before it had become a territory of the Great House Redoran.

During Gratian Caerellius' travels after Raven Rock, he was married and had a child named Rellicus Caerellius, both of whom would travel with Gratian around the world. On the 30th of Rain's Hand in 4E 10, Gratian was given an assignment from the East Empire Company in Raven Rock about their sudden discovery of the Bloodskal Barrow in the Ebony Mines. A month later in Second Seed, Gratian and his group had arrived onto the docks of Raven Rock, which is now under the occupation of the Great House Redoran, much to his surprise. Gratian and Millius had recovered the Caerellius House by it would constantly be covered in Ash. His family would take residence in the Redoran household. On the 9th of Second Seed, the two archaeologists had traversed the Bloodskal Barrow where Gratian learned about the Bloodskal Clan and discover the Bloodskal Blade.

Tempted by the Blade's mystery, Gratian had pulled the Bloodskal Blade from its pedestal, much to the dismay of Millius. The moment he had picked up the blade, a group of Draugr had attacked the two. Millius had fought valiantly but had succumbed the power of the Undead Nords. Gratian was able to fend off the remain Draugr but was mortally wounded in the process. With the Bloodskal Blade in his hands, Gratian died in peace, accepting his fate, hoping that whoever found his journal, would show it to his superiors and to tell his wife that he loves her. He died on the Second Seed of 4E 10.

After safely reaching Mereth and reclaiming Saarthal, the Circle of Captains was assembled. It was decided that every captain and his crew should go their own ways. Unlike most of the bands, Krilot Lok went back to the sea. It is said that they visited Yokuda and encountered Redguards long before they settled on Tamriel.

The crew of Krilot Lok visited many lands along the shores of Tamriel, including the great deserts of Elsweyr and the southern marsh later known by the name of Black Marsh.

entities.name: Grosta
entities.description:
Grosta was an Atmoran warrior during the Merethic Era. She was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

Grosta was one of the war-teacher Adrimk's students. She earned her name as a warrior on Tamriel and was very close to her Shield-Sister Froa. They were said to have thought and spoken as one.

Grosta joined Ysgramor's cause to slay the savage elves who were to blame for the Night of Tears. On the Day of Final Passage she had become a crewmember of the Darumzu, longboat under command of Captain Ylgar. She was joined by her teacher and her students, most of whom haven't had earned their names yet.

During the voyage to the Tamriel, known to Atmorans as Mereth, Darumzu was caught in Storm of Separation and was separated from the rest of the fleet. However, the boat sailed out safely, arriving at Hsaarik Head just a bit late. Unfortunately there are no further records found on what happened to Grosta after landing.

entities.name: Gurilda Sharktooth
entities.description:
Gurilda Sharktooth was an Atmoran warrior and a member of the Five Hundred Companions. She was the Captain of the crew of the Fallowfire.

After avenging their fallen comrades who died during the sack of Saarthal, the Circle of Captains decided that each crews should go their own ways and create their own legends. The crew of the Fallowfire rejoiced and yearned to fight the remaining Mer that had not yet been put to the sword. Captain Gurilda led her crew away from the sea to explore the land of Mereth.

The crew traveled south and fought any Mer they met. No settlement remained unburned in their path. As they ventured deeper into the land, so did the fear of Men began to grow in the elves. The crew found a new region near the mountains, which they called "The Rift." It was a land riven by deep canyons and swift-flowing rivers. In the name of the Fallowfire, of their fallen companions and Yngol, they burned every Mer villages and killed all they encountered.

At last, the Mer met the Atmoran in battle. The Elves had set up in great numbers on top of a rocky hill, daring the Companions led by Gurilda to attack. The Men took the bait and the battle began. Gurilda was pierced by many different weapons but lived until sunset. Her spirit joined that of her companions and ancestors in Sovngarde, knowing her crew was victorious.
entities.short_description: Gurilda Sharktooth was an Atmoran warrior and a member of the Five Hundred Companions. She was the Captain of the crew of the Fallowfire.

Gysilla was the second bride of Emperor Antiochus.

Despite Antiochus' lifestyle, Gysilla gave birth in 3E 104 to a daughter Kintyra, who was named in honor of Antiochus' great-great-great grandaunt. Kintrya became Empress herself after the death of her father.

Upon Emperor Antiochus' death in 3E 120, Potema, the Wolf Queen of Solitude, spread rumors about Gysilla being unfaithful. It was rumored that Kintrya was not the daughter of Antiochus and she could not claim the Imperial throne.

His spearmen were never defeated in their history, until the Battle of Ceyatatar, where they suffered their first defeat at the hands of Pelinal Whitestrake and the Imperial slaves who were rebelling against the rule of the Ayleids. Hadhuul was killed by Whitestrake during the battle in 1E 242. His ghost, however, still remains haunting the ruins in 2E 582.

A plaque dedicated to Harald sits on the left side of the archway that leads to the Palace of the Kings. It reads: ♦ HARALD

13th in the line of Ysgramor and founder of the great Kingdom of Skyrim where he established fair Windhelm as his capital.

entities.name: Hazadir
entities.description:
Hazadir was an Argonian armorer and freedman who hailed from the province of Morrowind. When he was emancipated, he immigrated to Cyrodiil. He was responsible for designing the armor that was used by the Imperial Legion for fighting Argonian forces in Black Marsh.

He ultimately won an armoring challenge against Sirollus Saccus, by designing a set of armor adapted to the terrain of the swampy conditions that the Imperials would be facing, and thus received Imperial commission. His knowledge of Argonian tactics and weaponry were instrumental in the resulting Imperial victory there.

entities.name: Hellena
entities.description:
Hellena was the Queen of Lilmoth, wife of Emperor Magnus Septim, and mother of Emperor Pelagius Septim III. Sometime before 3E 109, she became ruler of the kingdom of Lilmoth following the execution of the Argonian priest-king and represented Imperial interests in Black Marsh.

The Daedric Prince Sheogorath described Hellena as "unique," but "fairly average for a Septim," and claimed that she either "wielded fear like a cleaver" or that she would "wield a cleaver and make people afraid." Sheogorath attributes her son's paranoia to her, saying that "Pelagius learned at a very early age that danger could come from anywhere."

entities.name: Helseth
entities.description:
Hlaalu Helseth was a Dunmer King of Morrowind during the later fourth century of the Third Era, the son of Queen Barenziah and General Symmachus. He was notorious for his cunning character and scheming ways.

Helseth was born to Barenziah and Symmachus in 3E 376

Shortly after arriving at the kingdom of Wayrest in High Rock, Eadwyre married Barenziah and adopted Helseth and Morgiah. In 3E 405, with his adoptive father gaining in years, Prince Helseth had to compete for the throne with Elysana, the daughter of Eadwyre from his previous wife. However, Princess Elysana proved much too cunning, and eventually arose victorious from the power struggle. After the death of Eadwyre she became Queen, banishing Barenziah and Helseth.

After their exile from Wayrest, Barenziah and Helseth fled to Morrowind once again, where they were welcomed by Athyn Llethan, Barenziah's uncle and King at the time. Soon after, King Llethan died, along with his protege Talen Vandas, passing the throne to Helseth. The circumstances surrounding their deaths were considered suspicious, as people that would inconvenience Helseth had been found dead in many occasions throughout the years. However, nothing could point directly to his involvement.

entities.name: Henantier the Outsider
entities.description:
Henantier the Outsider was the first Elven Harbinger of the Companions.

Near the end of the First Era, Henantier arrived at Jorrvaskr to join up with the legendary Companions. At the time, there was much racial prejudice among the Companions and elves were not permitted to be full Companions, and few were even allowed to see the inside of the hall.

Like Cirroc before him, he was initially subject to ridicule upon his arrival, but this did not deter him. Henantier was humble in the daylight hours, performing any task asked of him. At night, he trained fiercely in the outside yard, allowing himself only minutes of sleep before resuming his servant duties the next day.

Henantier outlived several Harbingers but never complained about his lowly position within the guild. Given his long life, he came to be trusted by the new Companions as the one who could teach the ways of honor.
entities.short_description: Henantier the Outsider was the first Elven Harbinger of the Companions.

entities.name: Herbane
entities.description:
Herbane was an adventurer and author who traveled across Skyrim, searching for the most dangerous of creatures and exploring the province. In his writings he mentions his continued search of a challenge worthy of story and ends each book with a boastful statement that he was yet to encounter anything that would make him tremble. He was going to be featured in , but was cut from the game.

He has found, fought, and won over Hagravens, Ice Wraiths, and Animunculi. He has delved deep into Dwemer Ruins, survived frozen, freezing tundras of Skyrim and the wonders and dangers of the Reach.

The following books have been authored by Herbane:

entities.name: Hermeskr
entities.description:
Hermeskr was an Atmoran warrior who lived during the Merethic Era. He was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

On Atmora, Hermeskr was among the students of wise war-teacher Adrimk. He had not yet earned his name as a warrior. When Ysgramor returned from Tamriel, Hermeskr joined the Five Hundred Companions with a group of other war-students and Adrimk herself to slay the savage Snow Elves that were responsible for the infamous Night of Tears. On the Day of Final Passage Hermeskr had become a crew member of Darumzu, a longboat under command of Captain Ylgar. During the voyage to Skyrim, known to Atmorans as Mereth, Darumzu was caught in the Storm of Separation and was separated from the rest of the fleet. However, the boat sailed out safely, arriving at Hsaarik Head only slightly late. Hermeskr finally earned his warrior name, Who Threw His Shield, on Tamriel, however, no further details on how it happened have been recorded.

entities.name: Hero of Dawnstar
entities.description:
The Hero of Dawnstar is the protagonist of , responsible for defending Dawnstar against the Ice Tribes and the Gehenoth Thriceborn around the year 3E 427, as well as rooting out a traitor to the Empire.

At the beginning of , the Governor of Dawnstar sends the Hero to the exile post of Dawnstar with only 50 gold after an attack from the Ice Tribes, and the suspicion that one of his Four Champions had betrayed him and gave the Ice Tribes some sort of advantage. He tasks the Hero with revealing the traitor and defending the city. He tells the Hero that there's 3000 gold in it for him if he succeeds. Before the Hero arrives, the Governor tasks an oracle named Eustacia with aiding the Hero.

Upon arriving in Dawnstar, the Hero sought out Eustacia who used her oracular powers to provide the first clue towards identifying the traitor. The Hero then makes his way through the many surrounding locations to find the exiled Champions. Once found, they are interrogated by the Hero one by one until the Hero believed that he had identified the traitor.

Upon identifying the traitor, the Hero is given a mystical frost named Starfrost as a reward, and just in time for the Ice Tribe's second attack. Using the power of Starfrost and the collective prayers of Dawnstar, the Hero defeated every troll, bandit, and soldier that they threw into the city. Then, after most of their army was killed, they released the Gehenoth Thriceborn upon the city. However, even their greatest ally fell before the Hero. For successfully defending the city, the Governor gave the Hero 3000 gold, as promised.
entities.short_description: The Hero of Dawnstar is the protagonist of , responsible for defending Dawnstar against the Ice Tribes and the Gehenoth Thriceborn around the year 3E 427, as well as rooting out a traitor to the Empire.

entities.name: Hestra
entities.description:
Hestra was the Empress of the Alessian Empire during the early First Era. She is known to have believed that when the Dragon Break of the Middle Dawn occured, Cyrodiil "became an Empire across the stars."

While details regarding the rule of Empress Hestra are scarce, it is known that she invaded the Reach and took a hard stance against piracy along the eastern coastline of the Topal Bay.

Around 1E 1030, ten kings ruled over the then-independent kingdoms of the Reach. The Reachmen were constantly warring with themselves, and not a united force. Empress Hestra invaded from the south. Despite the kings of the Reach standing opposed to the Empress, her legions, which were known as the Alessiaj Legions at the time, proved too much, and one by one the kings either submitted to the Empress, or were slain in battle.

The last major site of battle was at the Sundered Hills, where the Reachmen slew numerous patrols and garrisons though ultimately to no avail as reinforcements came just as fast as they were defeated. Faolon would consort with a Hagraven and over the course of two years, the Reachmen had almost achieved victory. Hestra sent an even larger force north, which ultimately ended up routing after Faolon slew a thousand of their forces,

entities.name: Hidellith
entities.description:
King Hidellith Aldmeri was an Altmeri King of Alinor during the Second Era. He was the father of Ayrenn and Naemon, whom he conceived with his wife, Kinlady Tuinden. Hidellith passed away in 2E 580, and was succeeded by his eldest child, Ayrenn.

In 2E 486, Hidellith ordered much of the Alinori navy to follow a small Maormeri fleet that was spotted off the coast of Alinor. The navy followed the ship into uncharted waters, arriving into an ambush in Pyandonea itself. The navy was destroyed, save for one surviving warship, which provided reports on the landscape of Pyandonea.

Hidellith and Kinlady Tuinden's had their first child, a daughter named Ayrenn, on the 5th of Second Seed in 2E 555. The date of birth and name were some of many decisions that the king based on the precedents laid down in the Scrolls of Praxis; a tradition known as Elven Ceremoniarchy. Hidellith and Tuinden had a son a few years later, named Naemon.

In Evening Star of 2E 563, Hidellith gathered with the royal family in the Crystal Tower to celebrate Ayrenn's matriculation into the Sapiarchs' Labyrinth for the requisite 3,555 days. However, Ayrenn went missing, and disappeared somewhere between the Palace and the Tower.

entities.name: Hierem
entities.description:
Hierem was a greatly influential Nibenese Imperial with ties to several powerful factions, and serves as one of the primary antagonists of and . He served under both Thules the Gibbering and Titus Mede I during the Fourth Era. His physical form was described in 4E 48 as a pudgy man with thick eyebrows and mild blue eyes. He came from an old Nibenese family with a lot of connections.

Hierem was in a leadership position in the Mages Guild before its collapse, and also served as an ambassador to Morrowind before its independence.

During the Stormcrown Interregnum Hierem served as a minister to Thules the Gibbering, before Titus Mede took the throne from him. Hierem was the second most powerful man in the Empire, holding a great deal of influence in the Synod and the Elder Council. He used his heritage as a Nibenese as well as his many connections to make the Elder Council accept Titus Mede as a savior rather than a conqueror.

After the birth of Attrebus Mede in 4E 26, it was the idea of Hierem to the Emperor to turn the crown prince into a hero, and the Emperor complied, as it offered him a form of direction for raising Attrebus. Attrebus became immensely popular among the people as a result.

entities.name: High Priest Uluscant
entities.description:
High Priest Uluscant was an Ayleid priest dedicated to the worship of Hermaeus Mora. He was known to have resided in Bisnensel during the early First Era, where he spread the worship of Mora to much of the city's citizens.

In 1E 453, Uluscant founded the Primeval Seekers, a cult dedicated to the worship of Daedric Prince Hermaeus Mora. He established the congregation in Bisnensel, an Ayleid city founded by King Laloriaran Dynar a number of years prior. The cult began to gain many of the city's learned and influential citizens as members, giving Uluscant a large amount of support in Bisnensel. The Seekers requested that Dynar give Uluscant more of a say in municipal affairs, to which the King denied, remarking that he would not share leadership with an order of scholars.

Disappointed by Dynar's rebuff, the Seekers deposed Dynar as ruler of Bisnensel a few months afterwards. Dynar and his family fled to the Isle of Balfiera, and Uluscant became the new ruler of Bisnensel. It is unknown how long Uluscant ruled, or when the city fell to ruin.

entities.name: Hira
entities.description:
Hira was the last emperor of Yokuda. He persecuted the Ansei, and sent his brigand army of Orcs and war castoffs to wipe them out. He sent one hundred of his personal guards to arrest the famous Divad Hunding. His guards managed to capture him until one of them killed his aging mother, which awoke the spirit of the Way in Divad and led to his escape and subsequent resistance against Hira.

Divad managed to convince his father Frandar to go to war against Hira in the War of the Singers. The Ansei were greatly outnumbered initially, and led Hira's troops from their original invasion point of High Desert to the foot of Mount Hattu. Frandar planned to fight seven battles here, with the Singers growing in power with the Shehai until triumphed over Hira's forces.

Little is known of Hira's life or death, save that he had a consort named Elisa.

Hjalmer was the second known ruler of Skyrim. He was the eldest living son of Harald, the first known ruler of Skyrim. Hjalmer became king of Skyrim in 1E 221, after his father Harald died, when the first ever Moot was convened. He didn't reign long, as he died the following year in 1E 222, of unknown reasons. His younger brother, Vrage, became the next High King.

entities.name: Hoag Merkiller
entities.description:
Hoag Merkiller was a Nord High King of Skyrim in the First Era. He is considered to be one of the greatest war chiefs of his time and instrumental in the formation of the First Empire of the Nords.

Hoag was also known to be a powerful Tongue, as it was shown in his battles against Morrowind's armies during the Skyrim Conquests.

He attended the coronation of Emperor Gorieus on the 23rd of Sun's Dawn in 1E 461, along with his father and High King, Kjoric the White. Kjoric later rebelled against the Emperor, but was killed at the Battle of Sungard in 1E 477 or 1E 478. After this, the Moot named Hoag as the new High King.

His reign was short-lived however, as he was killed at the Battle of Glenumbria Moors 1E 480 or some time between 1E 461 and 1E 477. He was succeeded by Wulfharth.

entities.description:
Hoag Stormcloak, also known as the Great Bear of Eastmarch, was the father of Ulfric Stormcloak and the leader of the Stormcloak Clan. who banned the Argonian population from living within the city walls. He died in 4E 183, while Ulfric was imprisoned due to his involvement in the Markarth Incident. Due to his incarceration, Ulfric was unable to attend the funeral, and had to smuggle his eulogy for his father out of prison in the form of a letter.

entities.name: Horavatha
entities.description:
Horavatha is a character from the book Vernaccus and Bourlor, written by Tavi Dromio.

Horavatha was a Daedra Seducer that consistently taunted Vernaccus. Her constant undermining of Vernaccus only increased his anger, which she delighted in doing, causing him to murder and rampage throughout the Colovian West. Horavatha would eventually attempt to provoke Vernaccus into fighting Bourlor. However, instead of fighting and being shot, Vernaccus fled the confrontation and would become famous, if only temporarily.

Horavatha grew jealous of Vernaccus new found fame, until the day came when one of his shrines came under attack. Horavatha goaded him into intervening, which would ultimately lead to his fall from fame.

entities.name: Hosgunn Crossed-Daggers
entities.description:
Hosgunn Crossed-Daggers was a Fourth Era Jarl of Riften. He was appointed as Jarl in 4E 98 after the death of the previous Jarl during the Void Nights. He ruled for 31 years with an iron fist, taxing his citizens mercilessly. It was not until 4E 129 when the citizens rose up against him. They succeeded, in a short war which left much of Riften in ruins.

Hosgunn was appointed Jarl of Riften in 4E 98 during the Void Nights, following the assassination of his predecessor. Many of The Rift's citizens believed that Hosgunn was responsible for the assassination. He was nevertheless appointed Jarl despite public outcry about this.

Under Hosgunn, protests were broken up by the guard and a curfew was established in Riften. This curfew was ruthlessly enforced — anyone breaking the curfew was jailed without trial, and executed if they were repeat offenders.

He imposed crippling taxes on the city, causing commerce to slowly dry up. He hoarded almost all of the tax money and invested it into creating a wooden palace which was so extravagant, large, and excruciatingly embellished that it took 7 years to build.

Hranvard Frostfinger was a witch of Eastmarch who was said to have sacrificed thirteen innocent people at once to the Daedric Prince Mehrunes Dagon, which briefly opened a portal from the Deadlands to Skyrim. Hranvard was slain quickly afterwords by the witch hunting Direfrost Family. But after she died the sky split apart and engulfed the witch hunters in flame, killing all thirty of the hunters except for the leader, Yllothon. He was spared by what was probably Dagon only so he could agonize over the loss of almost his entire clan.

entities.name: Hrolfdir
entities.description:
Hrolfdir was the Jarl of Markarth during the Markarth Incident in 4E 174. He is the father of Markarth's Jarl Igmund, and brother of his former steward Raerek, who now serves as steward for Jarl Igmund.

While Jarl, the Reachmen, former rulers and natives of The Reach, seized the opportunity to conquer Markarth in a savage uprising, due to the Empire's resources being focused on the Great War. Hrolfdir was ultimately unable to quell this uprising and was deposed by the Reachmen, however he and his family managed to escape the city and sought help to reclaim it.

Hrolfdir made contact with the son of the Jarl of Windhelm, Ulfric Stormcloak, and promised him and his militia free worship of Talos within Markarth in exchange for liberating the city from the control of the Reachmen. Ulfric and his men agreed, and successfully retook the city, captured the Reachmen's king Madanach and drove the remaining hostile Reachmen from the city who then fled into the wilderness and pledged to cut a bloody hole into the Reach until the land was theirs once again, dubbing themselves the Forsworn. After reclaiming Markarth, Hrolfdir was brutal to the Reachmen usurpers and their alleged conspirators. He was said to have executed children of alleged Forsworn sympathizers and unjustly imprisoned those accused of colluding with Forsworn usurpers. However, this might have been under pressure of Ulfric Stormcloak, who allegedly held the city at the time, including the right to decide who could and could not enter the city. Even so, Braig's story and Thonar's Journal seems to imply Hrolfdir had agency on who to execute. Regardless of who did the executions, those of the Forsworn who didn't run were killed, except for Nepos the Nose and a handful of other Forsworn, including Madanach.

Shortly after the city had been liberated, a large group of Thalmor arrived in the city and demanded the arrest of Ulfric and his men. Refusal to obey the Thalmor's demand would have violated one of the terms of the White-Gold Concordat that forbids the worship of Talos. For Hrolfdir the choice was clear, not wanting to risk another war with the Dominion, he agreed to have Ulfric and his men arrested and personally aided the legion in the capture of Ulfric Stormcloak. Ulfric and his men called it "The Markarth Incident;" it was the founding day of the Stormcloaks and can be considered where the Skyrim Civil War originally started.

entities.name: Hrothmund the Red
entities.description:
Hrothmund the Red is the Nordic founder of the Thirsk Mead Hall along with other Skaal Village members who left to found the Hall.

He beheaded Drengr Bronze-Helm and held his head as a trophy in the middle of the hall. This testament of his strength led him to become the first Chieftain of the Mead Hall. This tradition of electing a chieftain by duel, is set as the standard for the Mead Hall. He died fighting Ondjage, the Fell Wolf.

His rule lasted for 21 years. He lived in the third century of the Third Era, contrary to the claims of some saying he lived in the Second Era. His place of burial along with his axe, Hrothmund's Axe, is in Hrothmund's Barrow.

Hrotti Blackblade was an Atmoran warrior and a member of the Five Hundred Companions. She is the ancestor of Aela the Huntress.

Not much is known of Hrotti's background, other than she was part of the Atmorans who fought during the event known as The Return, under Harbinger Ysgramor.

Hrotti's legacy stretches from the Merethic Era to the Fourth Era. Not only with Aela the Huntress but with her mother and grandmother. Aela claims that when she fights, she does so thinking of he lineage.

entities.name: Huna
entities.description:
Huna was a Nedic hoplite who was one of the companions of Pelinal Whitestrake during the Alessian Slave Rebellions in Cyrodiil during the First Era. Originally a slave who collected grain for the Ayleids, who ruled Cyrodiil and had enslaved the Imperials, Huna was eventually freed from their bondage by Pelinal Whitestrake and trained to become a hoplite, or spearman.

Eventually, Whitestrake and Huna developed a relationship, and it was said that Whitestrake loved Huna. In 1E 242, Huna was killed by the arrows of Celethelel the Singer. Huna's death drove Whitestrake to madness, and led to him rampaging across Cyrodiil, destroying many Ayleid cities including Narlemae and Celediil.

entities.name: Iachesis
entities.description:
Iachesis was the Ritemaster of the Psijic Order and magister of the Isle of Artaeum during the First and Second Eras. Iachesis was said to be an extremely powerful wizard in his own right, having led the Order for over three millennia.

Iachesis is known to have been the head of the Psijic Order as early as 1E 20, when the mage Voernet went to the Isle of Artaeum to meet with him. Around that period, the Psijics served as counselors to kings and proponents of "The Elder Way," a "philosophy of meditation and study said to bind the forces of nature to the individual will."

In the early Second Era, a former student of the Order named Heliand brought an 11-year-old boy named Trechtus to Iachesis. He recognized the young boy's potential and welcomed him into the Order, bestowing upon him the new name "Vanus Galerion" and taking him on as a pupil. In 2E 230, Iachesis met with a now older and more accomplished Galerion, along with King Rilis XII of Firsthold, to propose the formation of a new guild called the Mages Guild.

Shortly afterwards, the Isle of Artaeum mysteriously vanished from Nirn, with Iachesis and the rest of the Psijic Order disappearing with it. When Artaeum returned to the world after 500 years in 2E 730, the Order was no longer led by Iachesis. The Psijics would not, or could not, offer an explanation as to where the Isle had gone or what had happened to Iachesis.

entities.name: Ianus Faleria
entities.description:
Ianus Faleria was the second son of Lord Nunex Faleria and Lady Faleria. with a merchant's daughter.

Ianus was born in 1E 386 as the third and final child of Lord and Lady Faleria, with his mother dying in childbirth. His father was an Imperial and his mother was an Ayleid, though Ianus had mostly elven traits. As such, his parents never allowed him to go outside Fort Faleria as the Alessian Empire would banish or execute him due to the First Pogrom.

After becoming an adult, Ianus became discontent with being isolated in his father's underground estate, and managed to find a way to easily get in and out of the fort. He fell in love with a merchant's daughter, and fathered a son with her named Maxivian Faleria. The woman's parents were horrified at Maxivian's elvish traits, and forced her to confess that Ianus was the child's father. In order to keep his family a secret from the Empire, Nunex Faleria hid his grandson with Ianus in the fort.

Within days, the Alessian Army was at the gate of Fort Faleria, seeking to arrest Nunex for his crimes of treason after discovering his elvish children. On the 19th Sun's Dawn, 1E 421, Ianus went with his family to speak to their father, just after he had finished performing a dangerous ritual to wipe out the Alessian Army. Ianus put his hand on his father's shoulder, but it was too late for Lord Faleria to cancel the ritual, and the darkness he summoned inadvertently killed Ianus and Maxivian. Lord Faleria buried him with his sister Lucina on the surface, where he never allowed his children to go, writing "Boundless Eternity Awaits Us" on his epitaph.

entities.name: Ilzheven
entities.description:
Ilzheven is wife to Ezhmaar Sul. She appears as a ghost in the events of .

Her face was formed by delicate curves. Her eyes' color was red, like the last fading of a sunset.

After Vivec disappeared, the Dunmer needed a source of power to hold Baar Dau in the air. The Ingenium was used to keep the Ministry of Truth floating. In order to work properly, the Ingenium needed mortal souls. Firstly, only the souls of criminals and outlaws were used to run the Ingenium. Yet, Vuhon discovered that around twelve 'large' souls could power it for for months.

According to Vuhon, Ilzheven had the right sort of soul, so she was chosen to power the Ingenium. However, Sul claimed that she had been chosen because she loved Sul and not Vuhon. Sul tried to save her, but he ended up destroying the Ingenium. Ilzheven died and Baar Dau fell destroying Vivec City and its surroundings. It is thought that the collision was the direct cause of the eruption of the Red Mountain.

entities.name: Indoril Nerevar
entities.description:
Lord Indoril Nerevar, known formally as Serjo Indoril Nerevar Mora, and alternatively as St. Nerevar the Captain, Nerevar Moon-and-Star, and Godkiller, was a Chimer hero who lived during the First Era. He was a champion of Azura and the first Hortator, or war-leader/champion, of the unified Chimer and Dwemer, following the overthrowing of the Nordic Empire in Resdayn. However, after the discovery that the Dwemer were creating the Numidium, he led his people against them in the War of the First Council. Nerevar died at Red Mountain, though the exact cause is disputed. Later, he became a Saint of the Dunmer's Tribunal Temple.

Nerevar played a crucial role in Morrowind's history. The Ashlanders and an underground offshoot of the Tribunal Temple, known as the Dissident Priests of Vvardenfell, believed that he was reincarnated multiple times as part of the Nerevarine Prophecy. This prophecy was fulfilled by the Nerevarine, the hero of .

Nerevar's early life is shrouded in mystery. Vivec's sermons indicate he was, at one point, a guard for a merchant caravan, but the accuracy of his prose is somewhat debatable. When the War of Succession ravaged the Nordic Empire, Nerevar seized the opportunity to incite a rebellion in Resdayn. Nerevar united the disparate Chimer clans, and was proclaimed as Hortator, whereupon he forged an unlikely alliance with the Dwemer, thanks in part to his burgeoning friendship with the Dwemer king, Dumac. Together, the alliance drove the Nords from Morrowind, attaining the Chimer's independence.

Some time after, Nerevar married Almalexia, and maintained close relationships with several people amidst his retinue, such as his advisors Sotha Sil and Vivec, his shield-bearer Alandro Sul, and Voryn Dagoth the Lord High Councilor of House Dagoth (and, by some accounts, Nerevar's most loyal servant). Centuries later, Dagoth learned that the chief Dwemer scientist, Kagrenac, had discovered the Heart of Lorkhan beneath Red Mountain, and intended to use it for unclear apotheotic purposes, something the Chimer considered blasphemous. For one reason or another, when Nerevar confronted Dumac about Kagrenac's plans, their friendship swiftly crumbled. This resulted in the War of the First Council, culminating with the Battle of Red Mountain, wherein the Dwemer race mysteriously disappeared forever.

entities.name: Inga
entities.description:
Lady Inga was owner of Darkmoor estate, wife of Count Sven. She had a son, Jonni. She was a distant relative to previous Darkmoon Keep inhabitants and had little to none royal blood.

Inga was a large gray-white woman with icy gray-golden hair and bright blue eyes. She was a Nord.

She was the last caretaker of young Barenziah. Upon Barenziah's arrival she burned her favorite toy, Wuffen, and swore to train her. She wasn't too proud of caretaking the Dunmer and shared the disappointment with neighboring ladies, but she received payments from the Imperial Palace for doing so.

She is mentioned in The Real Barenziah, Book I.

Ingjaldr's chronicler, Lokheim, wrote an account of the battle, it was later rewriten in a book, known by the name of "Fall of the Snow Prince."

entities.name: Irthvyd the Impassive
entities.description:
Irthvyd the Impassive was a Jarl and later High King of Skyrim during the First Era.

When in the late-First Era the people of Solitude rose up against High Queen Roleke, Jarl Irthvyd heard of the troubles due to being in the area. He and his warriors marched on Solitude, where upon approaching the gate, Kyne appeared before the Jarl. She told him that the High Queen, as well as her children, had died, leaving the province without an heir to the throne.

With the favor of Kyne, Jarl Irthvyd and his men entered the city. Only mere hours later Jarl Irthvyd was crowned High King. Under his reign, peace returned to the Holds of Skyrim after the years of Roleke's bloody reign. After decades, when King Irthvyd had grown older, he refused to marry or make an heir. His most trusted advisor, Temylda, would eventually be named High King.

Irthvyd was said to be a stoic, calm and collected man, thus earning the nickname The Impassive.

entities.name: Istlod
entities.description:
Istlod served as High King of Skyrim. He also was the father of future High King Torygg.

The exact duration of the reign of Istlod is uncertain. However, it has been stated that he held Skyrim together for almost 25 years following the signing of the White-Gold Concordat. In addition to High King, he also served as the Jarl of Solitude and lived in the Blue Palace, as was the custom.

His vampiric Court Wizard Sybille Stentor served him, caring for his son, and has been with the family ever since. Upon his death, a moot was called to name his heir, Torygg, as the new High King.

entities.name: Jagar Tharn
entities.description:
Jagar Tharn was a powerful Imperial Battlemage and personal advisor to Emperor Uriel Septim VII during his early years as emperor. After months of plotting, Tharn used the Staff of Chaos to trap Septim in Mehrunes Dagon's Plane of Oblivion out of jealousy and desire for the throne, and copied his look by using Illusion magic, marking the beginning of the Imperial Simulacrum.

Tharn usurped the throne as Emperor of the Septim Empire of Tamriel from 3E 389 until his ultimate demise in 3E 399 at the hands of the Eternal Champion, by the unification of the Staff of Chaos and the Jewel of Fire's power.

Tharn's life before Imperial service is near completely ambiguous. Tharn claimed to be born in southern Valenwood to a Bosmer mother, which according to Notes on Racial Phylogeny, would likely make him Bosmer in appearance. According to Symmachus, Tharn was also part Dunmer, part Altmer, and "part the gods only know what." According to The Lost Fort Faleria, even minor physical features can be passed down from the father, likely explaining Tharn's red eyes that are common in most Dunmer. Symmachus also claimed that Human blood was absent from Tharn's ancestry. This, however, is untrue if he is a member by birth of House Tharn whose other members have been notable Nibenese rulers.

Tharn was a mage-priest at the Temple of Sethiete in Camlorn, High Rock. He turned to thievery for a short period of time after leaving the temple's circle, stealing many books of old, powerful, and forgotten spells along with lore and articles about many ancient tools and magical items. Included among these texts was information on the Staff of Chaos, an immensely powerful magical staff said to be made with the land itself. In 3E 376, Tharn had either traveled to Mournhold under one of his alter-egos, an enigmatic bard named "Nightingale," or tasked Drayven Indoril to do so, and stole the Staff of Chaos from its hiding place in the Mournhold mines.

entities.name: Jeek of the River
entities.description:
Jeek of the River was one of the captains of the Five Hundred Companions and a friend of the legendary Ysgramor, and it's said that he and his crew were among Ysgramor's personal favorites. According to the tales, he was a great beast of a man who stood head and shoulders above the tallest men of his crew and possessed of the strength of a bear, the heart of a saber cat and the ferocity of a troll. His weapons of choice were a war axe he inherited from his father called Relkjard, or "Foecrusher," and a silver-edged greatsword of burnished steel he'd forged himself and called Bjarskor, meaning "Fireblade," and he wore a suit of armor fashioned by the finest Atmoran craftsmen from metals of the highest quality.

Jeek commanded a longboat named Jorrvaskr - whose hull is now used as the roof of the Companions' mead hall that also bears its proud name - and its crew of twenty-two warriors.

He lived sometime in the late Merethic Era.

Jeek of the River and his crew split from the rest of the captains after the Circle of Captains was assembled. They went southwards towards the area that was later named Whiterun Hold. It is said that they met many elves, but their numbers never faltered, so shrewd were they in battle, with minds as sharp as their blade.

entities.name: Jiub
entities.description:
Jiub Mothren, also known as Saint Jiub the Eradicator, was a Saint of both the Tribunal Temple and the New Temple. He was named a saint after cleansing Vvardenfell of the Cliff Racer menace. He was later killed in the city of Kvatch by a Dremora during the Oblivion Crisis, and his soul was sent to the Soul Cairn.

Jiub's early life was a dark experience, and a time that he himself deeply regrets. Killing was always high in demand in his homeland of Morrowind, and so he worked as a low-grade killer for hire to support his Skooma addiction. It was a decision that led to his eventual capture and imprisonment.

Jiub was sent to prison after a failed assassination on a high-ranking official of House Redoran. A rival assassin from the legally sanctioned assassin guild known as the Morag Tong reached Jiub's target first and alerted the local guards to cover his tracks. Jiub was later sent to jail in the city of Vivec after being found guilty in his trial.

After his release in 3E 427, he was transported by ship alongside the Nerevarine from the Imperial City to Vvardenfell, Morrowind. It was during this time that he decided to turn his life around to seek redemption for his crimes. He felt obligated to give something back to the people of Morrowind, so he decided to undertake a crusade against the Cliff Racers who plagued his homeland.

Jofrior was a Nord warrior who lived sometime in late Merethic Era or early First Era.

Jofrior fought in the Battle of the Moesring, the final battle between Nords and Snow Elves in a long series of wars and skirmishes between the two races. However, she was killed at the hands of the legendary Snow Prince.

She was the sole parent of young Finna, who was a twelve-year-old squire during the battle. As Jofrior fell in front of her young daughter, Finna threw her mother's sword at the Snow Prince, killing him.

During her reign, a guerrilla group called the Horme committed terrorist attacks throughout Southern Skyrim by hitting places such as Whiterun and Hrothgar in the name of Potema Septim, the Wolf Queen of Solitude. The people of Whiterun blamed Jsashe, but oddly enough, exalted her to her current position. She had effective control over Whiterun Hold, yet here magic was unable to have the region prosper under her.

Jubal appears in and serves as a lead character in C0DA, in which he defeats the Numidium and ends the cycle of Landfall. He does this in order to marry the daughter of High Alma Jaroon, the lord of the Velothiid.

It is believed that Jubal is a New Man and that he or his child with Vivec (who the High Alma's daughter turns out to be) will achieve Amaranth.

entities.name: Justin
entities.description:
Justin was an imaginary playmate of Uriel Septim VII; young Uriel even insisted to set a place for her at every meal. Despite the boyish name, Justin was a girl.

King Symmachus kept up the joke long after she went the way of imaginary childhood friends. He asked about Justin's health every time he met Uriel and the Emperor always replied in as mock-serious a fashion. The Emperor, according to Barenziah, once joked elaborately to Symmachus that she met an adventurous though incorrigible Khajiit youth, married him, and settled down in Lilandril to raise fire fern and mugworts.

During her stay at the Imperial City, Barenziah had a meeting with the Emperor. However, she began suspecting that the Emperor might be a fake. She asked about Justin to confirm her suspicion that Jagar Tharn was in fact posing as Uriel.

entities.name: Kagrenac
entities.description:
Kagrenac, sometimes referred to as Kagrnak, was a brilliant magecrafter and engineer of the Dwemer, having gained many titles such as "High Priest," "High Engineer," and "Chief Tonal Architect." He was most well known for his work within the field of mythopoeic forces and for constructing the first Numidium. His own theories on making a new god are written in the book Divine Metaphysics.

When Dwemer miners discovered the Heart of Lorkhan under the Red Mountain, he began studying ways to tap into its power, in his search for the secrets of immortality. He created three tools to manipulate the divine power of the Heart: the dagger Keening, the hammer Sunder, and the gauntlet Wraithguard.

After peace was established between the Chimer and Dwemer, Kagrenac secretly began working on the Heart of Lorkhan in order to make a new god that they could use to claim Resdayn for their own. However, his schemes were discovered by Dagoth Ur and House Dagoth, which led to The War of the First Council. Some accounts say that Dagoth Ur slayed Kagrenac, while others claim that he used the three tools on the Heart of Lorkhan which caused all the Dwemer to disappear from Tamriel.

Kaladas was a Pirate sea captain who was based in Hammerfell, the homeland of the Redguards. In Hammerfell, Kaladas hired Torradan ap Dugal, who would eventually found the Red Sabre, as his midshipman for a pirating voyage. Kaladas; however, was a notorious drinker and ended up crashing his ship near Anvil in Cyrodiil. Extremely embarrassed by his errors, Kaladas drank himself to death in an Anvil tavern.

entities.name: Kastav
entities.description:
Emperor Kastav (?–1E 2812) was the Emperor of the Reman Empire following the reign of Emperor Reman Cyrodiil I. Kastav was considered to be a poor commander and an incompetent ruler, resulting in his deposition and succession by Reman Cyrodiil II.

With Reman Cyrodiil's death in 1E 2762, Kastav was at some point crowned Emperor. In the year 1E 2801, Kastav ordered the Dragonguard of Skyrim to seize hostages from Markarth and Hroldan to ensure that the Jarls "meet their conscription quotas." The Master of the Dragonguard at that time protested against this but his protest was denied by the Emperor. The hostages were housed and trained. Later, in 1E 2804, Emperor Kastav ordered the Dragonguard to suppress the Winterhold Rebellion but the Master refused to do so. In response, the Kastav ordered for their supplies to be cut off. In 1E 2805, Sky Haven Temple was besieged and the city of Winterhold was sacked by a failed Dragonguard recruit named Kalien.

Having been declared too incompetent to rule the Empire, Kastav was deposed and succeeded by Reman Cyrodiil II.

entities.name: Katariah
entities.description:
Katariah, also known as Katariah Ra'athim, and Katariah Septim, was the thirteenth ruler of the Third Empire of Tamriel.

Katariah was born as a member of House Ra'athim, a prominent clan in Ebonheart.

Katariah was uncomfortable in the Imperial City, and during her reign traveled extensively throughout the Empire. Such a cosmopolitan attitude had not been seen since Tiber Septim's day. She repaired the damage her eccentric husband had caused on the diplomatic front, and she strengthened foreign ties and alliances. She was a very popular monarch; the people came to love her far more than the nobility did.

Katariah died in a minor skirmish in Black Marsh in 3E 200. This event is a favorite source for conspiracy-minded historians. The sage Montalius' discovery of a disenfranchised branch of the Septim family's involvement with the skirmish proved a revelation. She was succeeded by her son Cassynder.
