entities.name: Katisha
entities.description:
Katisha was plump and matronly Nord who lived in Riften in late Second Era.

She was married to a smith, had two teenage children, and was perfectly ordinary and respectable—except that she was very fond of cats (and by logical inference, their humanoid counterparts the Khajiit), had a talent for certain kinds of magic, and cultivated rather odd friends.

She was introduced to Barenziah by Therris. Later Barenziah introduced her to Straw. She taught Barenziah an invisibility spell and schooled her in other forms of stealth and disguise. Katisha mingled magical and non-magical talents freely, using one set to enhance the other. She was not a member of the Thieves Guild, but was fond of Therris in a motherly sort of way. Barenziah warmed to her as she never had toward any woman, and over the next few weeks she told Katisha all about herself.

Barenziah talked to Katisha about her problems with men. Or what she thought of as her problems with men. Katisha shook her head and told her she was looking for love, not sex, that she'd know the right man when she found him, that neither Straw nor Therris was the right one for her.
entities.short_description: Katisha was plump and matronly Nord who lived in Riften in late Second Era.

Keirgo's attempt to keep the alliance together failed and later gave rise to the Mane.

entities.name: Khartag
entities.description:
Khartag was a well-known Orcish warrior that served as an ex-member of the Daggerfall Covenant and the leader of the Ropefish, an abolitionist group that helped slaves escape the Great House Telvanni in Vvardenfell.

Khartag was an ex-member of the Daggerfall Covenant and later the leader of the Ropefish. Khartag created the Ropefish as a way to free slaves from the Dark Elves of House Telvanni in Vvardenfell. The word about the Ropefish Gang began to spread around the plantations of Vvardenfell, many of the slaves had contacted the Ropefish, leading to many successful escapes at the hands of the Ropefish. The group would then get attention for the Camonna Tong, who saw a business opportunity in the form of the Ropefish. Avrusa Duleri had talked with Khartag to discuss business but Khartag had denied the offer but had also told them off, not realizing the repercussions from messing with the Camonna. In retaliation, Duleri had the Camonna Tong raid the Ropefish base, killing the slaves and the abolitionist residing in the area. In the end, Khartag was stabbed by a poisoned dagger, leaving him on the cold ground of the Khartag Cavern. The Camonna Tong was terminated in Khartag Point with the help of the Vestige, a traveler wandering Tamriel.

On his deathbed, Khartag would name his subordinate, Nakhul, the next leader of the Ropefish, continuing their operation throughout Vvardenfell. Unfortunately, the Ropefish Gang had disbanded before 3E 427, while the Camonna Tong still worked throughout Vvardenfell. Even though the Ropefish had died out, Khartag himself would not be forgotten by his people. The area the Ropefish operated out of was renamed to Khartag Point, in his honor. At one point, an Orcish warrior had traveled to Khartag Point and was dared by his peers to jump off the cliff, which led to their demise. As time went on, many Orsimer would make pilgrimages to Khartag Point to pay their respects. A Shrine to Boethiah had sunken in the Inner Sea and a new one needed to be constructed. Duma gro-Lag was an Orcish worshipper of Boethiah and decided to build a new shrine atop of Khartag Point. It has remained there ever since.

She is described as an almost snoutless Khajiit. She was overseeing Colin's initiation into this organization.

Arcus and Khasha were Colin's overseers during his test to become inspector. Arcus and her helped Colin after he had murdered his objective. Arcus complained that the murder had been quite a fracas, and Khasha defended Colin stating it was his first time. She offered the new inspector some robes in order to hide the blood.

entities.name: Khunzar-ri
entities.description:
Khunzar-ri; known as Zar for short as well as The Laughing Lion, Luminous Lion of Elsweyr, Jonelight Jaunter, and Imprisoner of Dragons; was a mythic Khajiit hero and warrior active during the Merethic Era.

There are three conflicting accounts of Khunzar-ri's origins. One story claims Khunzar-ri manifested out of moonlight by Jone and Jode. A second story claims he was found inside a box at a shrine to Khenarthi. A third story claims Sheggorath caused Khunzar-ri's birth when he cheered up a grumpy Alkosh, and from a tear of joy from Alkosh, Khunzar-ri was born.

Many tales speak of Khunzar-ri's adventures and teachings. One tale claims Khunzar-ri outwitted a dozen Ogres, while another claimed he had adopted a lost female Alfiq. This Alfiq would go on to serve as Khunzar-ri's scribe and become enemies with Khunzar-ri's lover, Anequina Sharp-Tongue.

Sometime in the Merethic Era, Kaalgrontiid and his horde of dragons came to dominate the land. Kaalgrontiid hoped to claim the Moon's power and become Akatosh's equal. To stop them, Khunzar-ri recruited four companions, Nurarion the Perfect, Flinthild Demon-Hunter, Anequina Sharp-Tongue, and Cadwell the Betrayer. Following the suggestion of Cadwell, Khunzar-ri presented Jode's Core to the dragons. However, he tricked them into storing their energy within it in the guise that they would combine the lunar power with their own. The dragons were subsequently weakened, and Khunzar-ri managed to seal them away in the Halls of Colossus.

entities.name: King Anumaril
entities.description:
King Anumaril was an Ayleid arch-mage and a king of Abagarlas, a city worshipping Molag Bal. He was the father of Prince Malyon and husband to Queen Palolel. During his reign the city was at war with the city of Delodiil, whose citizens worshipped Meridia. Abagarlas's forces included Molag Bal's Daedra and the undead. Close to the end of the war, Anumaril has made preparations to activate the relic called Mortuum Vivicus which would drain all the life from Delodiil. This plan wasn't implemented as a group of warriors from Delodiil, with the help of Prismatic Weapon imbued with Meridia's power, managed to enter the city and stop the ritual. During the final battle of the war, the entire royal family of Abagarlas was put to the sword and the city itself was destroyed by Meridia.

He is also known as the powerful archmage who created the Staff of Towers, which is said to be able to bend and shape the time itself. It was created by him sometime during or shortly before the Alessian Slave Rebellion. The staff consisted of eight segments, each being a semblance of a Tower in its Dance. Seven fragments were later borne by White-Gold Knights to distant Fold-Places, where they were hidden. The last segment, also known as Segment One, remained with Anumaril.

After the Rebellion Anumaril fled along with other Ayleids to Valenwood. They were welcomed by the Green-Sap's Elves as long as they agreed not to dissonate the greensong and all the Heartland High Elves agreed to this except for Anumaril. He asked the Great Camoran to show him the Green-Sap. Within the great graht he found his desire – Perchance Acorn. He then attempted to convert the region into a new home for the Ayleids by plunging Segment One into the acorn. This resulted in stopping the Elden Tree from moving by turning its perchance acorn into a definite acorn, but it was not enough to convert the tree.

He is then said to use his dentition as tonal instruments, dismantle his bones and build of them a Mundus-machine that mirrored Nirn and its planets. When he had used all his substance in fangling this orrery, he placed the segment-scepter within, hiding it between the Moons. And then he started to wait.

entities.name: King Aphren
entities.description:
King Aphren is a Breton spirit found in his tomb in Stormhaven. In life he was a member of the Gardner Dynasty, and had the original Wayrest Palace built. He conquered Wind Keep and named the stronghold Aphren's Hold.

When first meeting him: "These are sacred grounds. My sacred grounds. They are not meant for the living. Are you the one who disturbs our rest?"

After Princess Mira forgives him: "My sword is again broken, but this time for good, and for good purpose. She has forgiven me. You have healed a wound that was centuries old."

King Aphren: "I would give it all, Mira. The sword, the keep, the kingdom … all of it for you …." Princess Mira: "I… I forgive you father."

Due to the King knowing of a conspiracy against his rule, he didn't act against the Corsair invasion of Wayrest in 4E 188. It is unknown whether the King was killed by the Dark Brotherhood, as a contract demanded, or if he was spared.

entities.description:
King Hurlburt of House Branquette, was the twenty-first ruler of Shornhelm. He ruled from 2E 522 until his death in 2E 546, leading Shornhelm at the significant Battle of Granden Tor. Hurlburt joined the recently established Daggerfall Covenant after the Black Drake's Reachman invasion. At the time, the covenant was only a collection of High Rock's many kingdoms.

Hurlburt would be succeeded by his legitimate son, fourteen-year-old Phylgeon Montclair. His eldest son, however, named Ranser Branquette, was supported by House Branquette and House Tamrith who believed him to be the rightful heir, though he had been born out of wedlock. Ranser would later become king.

entities.name: Kintyra Septim
entities.description:
Kintyra Septim was the third monarch of the Third Era and first Empress to rule Tamriel.

Kintyra succeeded Pelagius Septim, who had no living children; Kintyra was the daughter of Tiber Septim's brother Agnorith. After the death of Pelagius, she gave up her post as Queen of Silvenar. Her reign saw much prosperity and many good harvests. Kintyra herself was an avid patron of the arts, music and dance.

Kintyra died in 3E 48 of natural causes and was succeeded by her son, Uriel I.

entities.name: Kintyra Septim II
entities.description:
Kintyra Septim II was the eighth monarch and second Empress regnant of the Third Empire of Tamriel.

According to the First book of A Brief History of the Empire, the story of Kintyra II, heiress of her father's throne, is one of the "saddest tales in the history of the Septim Dynasty." Ten years after being crowned the Emperor of Tamriel, Antiochus Septim and his wife had a daughter in the year 3E 104, whom he named Kintyra, after the Empress Kintyra Septim. Later, at a young age still, she would become an accomplished mystic and sorceress and the second Empress of the Empire of Tamriel.

After the death of her father, Antiochus Septim in 3E 119, Kintyra inherited the throne the 3rd day of First Seed, in 3E 120, at the age of 15, and was crowned Kintyra II. Her uncles, Kings Cephorus of Gilane and Magnus of Lilmoth, attended the coronation. However, her aunt the Queen of Solitude, Potema, was banished after insulting Kintyra in front of the Elder Council by accusing her of being a bastard child, alluding to the decadence that existed in the Imperial City during her father's reign.

Kintyra's aunt, Potema Septim, was scheming to obtain the throne for herself and her son, Uriel. When Potema's accusations failed to stop Kintyra's coronation, Uriel bought the support of several disgruntled kings of High Rock, Skyrim, and Morrowind, and with Potema's assistance, he coordinated three attacks on the Septim Empire which resulted in a civil war known as the War of the Red Diamond, the name coming from the symbol of the Imperial family. In the early surprise attacks, Skyrim and High Rock were easily defeated by the force of Uriel and Queen Potema.
entities.short_description: Kintyra Septim II was the eighth monarch and second Empress regnant of the Third Empire of Tamriel.

entities.name: Kjoric the White
entities.description:
Kjoric the White was a former High King of Skyrim, during the First Era.

He attained the Crown of Verity (and subsequently the title of High King) from Asurn Ice-Breaker, whom the Crown had previously rejected as High King. Asurn had threatened to kill the other members of the Moot if they did not grant him the title, but Kjoric—who was purportedly a soft-spoken man—stood up to him, defeating him in a duel.

He attended the coronation of the Emperor Gorieus on the 23rd of Sun's Dawn in 1E 461 with his son, Hoag Merkiller. Kjoric later rebelled against the Emperor and his Alessian Army, but was killed at the Battle of Sungard in 1E 477 or 478. The Moot named his son Hoag as the new High King.

entities.name: Kluwe
entities.description:
Kluwe, who went by Loate when hiding his face, was an Atmoran warrior who lived during the Merethic Era. He was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

Kluwe was part of Jorrvaskr's crew, commanded by Jeek of the River.

After reaching Mereth and reclaiming Saarthal, Kluwe and his crew went south to the area that is now known as Whiterun Hold. They settled there, making Kluwe to be among the first people who lived in Whiterun.

The character is a reference to former Minnesota Vikings punter Chris Kluwe, who goes by the online alias Loate.

entities.name: Kyrnil Long-Nose
entities.description:
Kyrnil Long-Nose was Harbinger of the Companions during the late Second Era.

The late Second Era was a dark period of time for the Companions due to a series of dishonorable Harbingers who laid claim to Jorrvaskr. Infuriated, Kyrnil invaded Jorrvaskr and killed the usurpers. This was viewed by many as returning honor through blood, in the old ways. He also began the tradition of trusted advisors called The Circle (named after Ysgramor's council of captains). This would serve as an example to the younger, newer Companions.

entities.name: Lady Arannelya
entities.description:
Lady Arannelya was an Altmer commander for the Third Aldmeri Dominion and for the main force of the Thalmor invasion into Hammerfell during the Great War.

Shortly after Lord Naarifin's attack on southern Cyrodiil, Lady Arannelya's troops made their move into Hammerfell firstly bypassing the West Colovian and the cities of Kvatch and Bravil, eventually moving into Hammerfell to start the attack.

Just after entering Hammerfell, Lady Arannelya's troops attacked the southern coastline. With the civil war going on in Hammerfell, the few scattered legions there provided little defense and were eventually driven into the northern sands of the Alik'r Desert. This event became known as the March of Thirst.

Content to have full power over their gains in Hammerfell, Aldmeri troops stationed there continued to secure the major cities. By 4E 174, all but Hegathe had fallen to the Elven invaders.

entities.name: Lamae Bal
entities.description:
Lamae Bal, also known as Lamae Beolfag, "Mother" Lamae, or the "Blood-Matron," was the first recorded pure-blood vampire in Tamrielic history and one of the last known surviving Nedes.

Lamae Beolfag was a Nedic tribeswoman who was raped by the Daedric Prince of domination and enslavement, Molag Bal.

Lamae was discovered by a tribe of nomads, who took care of her and attempted to heal her wounds. Despite their best efforts, however, she appeared to have died within a fortnight. The tribe then prepared to set her body aflame in a funeral pyre, but as it was still burning she rose up and emerged as the first pure-blood vampire. Enraged, she slaughtered the nomads by ripping out the throats of the tribe's women, eating the eyes of the children, and raping the men in a crazed act of violence.

As she was the first individual granted vampirism directly from Molag Bal himself, she became known as a Daughter of Coldharbour. This developed into a tradition among Molag Bal worshipping cults which dictated that females be offered to him on his summoning day. Few survive the ordeal, but those who do emerge as pure-blooded vampires. Being selected as an offering was considered to be an honor that is not rejected lightly.

entities.description:
Legate Cassia was an Imperial Legate during the Great War between the Third Aldmeri Dominion and the Third Empire. She joined the Forgotten Hero during his quest to aid the Empire, after the Hero had taken down a group of Imperial Deserters. With the company of the Hero and his followers, they went to the Imperial City, posing as Gladiators, to find out the source of Naarifin's power. During the Battle of the Red Ring, Cassia commanded a part of the Imperial forces.

entities.name: Legate Rikke
entities.description:
Legate Rikke was a female Nord legate serving the Imperial Legion in Skyrim during the Skyrim Civil War. She was tasked with the recruitment of soldiers for the legion.

The parents of Legate Rikke were Legionnaires themselves, and Legate Rikke followed in their footsteps.

Legate Rikke fought during the Great War, and was part of the Legions that reclaimed the capital. As she and Galmar were Nords from Skyrim, they presumably marched to Cyrodiil with the armies under the command of General Jonna, who commanded Nord Legions from Skyrim.

During the Skyrim Civil War, Legate Rikke served as the local recruiter of the Legion. Legate Rikke gave advice to the General based on Nord tradition, which often led to discussions between the two. to taking over forts, was directed by the Legate after discussing it with General Tullius.

entities.name: Lieutenant Lein-Barduik
entities.description:
Lieutenant Lein-Barduik was an Akaviri who lived sometime in the First Era.

Lein-Barduik served under the Proconsul Beloren-Kaie as his trusted bodyguard, but when a Morag Tong assassin attacked, he fled the scene, leaving him to die. He then took on the Proconsul's identity and founded the town of Hakoshae. After performing the town's first Proving Festival, Beloren came back and attempted to kill the pretender, but Lein-Barduik being a powerful mage was able to cast him back. He then prevented the Festival from taking place again for fear that Beloren would return, until his descendant Magnate Feina-Darak uncovered the tradition and brought it back. His spirit returned as the "Shade of the Founder" to fight the Vestige.
entities.short_description: Lieutenant Lein-Barduik was an Akaviri who lived sometime in the First Era.

entities.name: Llothis
entities.description:
Llothis, better known as Saint Llothis the Pious, is a saint of the Tribunal Temple and the Patron of Tailors and Dyers. He is the contemporary companion of the Tribunal gods, and the best-loved Alma Rula of the Tribunal Temple, he formulated the central rituals and principles of the New Temple Faith. Saint Llothis is the symbolic mortal bridge between the gods and the faithful, and the archetypal priest.

During the events of the , shrines dedicated to him can be found across Vvardenfell, inside Temples, such as the High Fane in Vivec City, the Ghostgate Temple in the Ashlands, or the Holamayan Monastery in the Azura's Coast region.

entities.name: Lord Naarifin
entities.description:
Lord Naarifin was an Altmer general who commanded an Aldmeri army of the Third Aldmeri Dominion during the Great War.

In 4E 171 Naarifin and his army invaded Cyrodiil from the south, by marching out of their hidden camps near the Elsweyr border, flanking Imperial forces near the border of Valenwood. Shortly after, his army conquered Leyawiin and was already besieging Bravil.

By the end of 4E 172, Lord Naarifin's army had advanced to the walls of the Imperial City, while there were clashes between the Aldmeri Navy and Imperial Navy on Lake Rumare. A year later the Imperial City was surrounded on nearly every side, with only the supply route to Bruma remaining open.

In 4E 174 Lord Naarifin's army, now bolstered by Aldmeri reinforcements, took the Imperial City and started looting the city. Shortly after this, Lord Naarifin would begin working on a dread prophecy to bring about a Dominion victory, The Culling. The Battle of the Red Ring, however, changed the course of action, Naarifin had almost completed the prophecy, but was defeated just in time by the Forgotten Hero to prevent the Culling from being completed. Following his defeat, Naarifin was kept alive for thirty-three days, hanging from the White-Gold Tower. It is rumored that a flying Daedra took his body away on the thirty-fourth day.

entities.name: Lord Nunex Faleria
entities.description:
Lord Nunex Faleria is a spectral Lich found haunting Tribune's Folly. In life, he was an Imperial Lord who had partial rulership of Kvatch during the Alessian Doctrines in the First Era. He hid his Ayleid family within his holding, Fort Faleria, in order to keep them safe from the First Empire. His secret was discovered decades later, and in revenge cast a spell that obliterated the Alessian Army at his gate, along with his fort. He then buried his children on the surface and retreated to the ground, sealing the entrance behind him.

Lord Faleria is seen roaming the inner ruins of Tribune's Folly, in what remains of his fort. After you come close enough to him, he will fade and summon his shadow minions, then later the corrupted Minotaur, Limenauruus. He is guarding the First Era Personal Relic.

In the wake of the Alessian Doctrines, Nunex Faleria ruled as a Lord of the Kvatch Regency Council, made up of a king and two other lords.

As a young man, to the shame of his family, Nunex Faleria fell in love with an Elven scholar who was well versed in the ways of dark magic and necromancy. Seeing the xenophobia towards the Nenalata Ayleids who, despite swearing fealty to the Alessian Empire, remained unwelcome by the Alessian Order supporting society, Faleria and his wife decided to marry in secret. Poring over lost secrets, they hoped to find a way to be together for eternity.

entities.name: Lord Thone
entities.description:
Lord Thone was a trusted war-chief of King Mantiarco.

He is best known for having a secret affair with the first wife of Mantiarco, Queen Amodetha of Solitude. As a result, he and the queen had a son, Prince Bathorgh, who was considered a son of the King himself. However, in 3E 97, during an investigation due to rumors of Thone's treason, Mantiarco found out about the affair.

He henceforth banished Prince Bathorgh from Skyrim, and Thone's post was taken by a loyal servant of Queen Potema, Lord Vhokken. The further fate of Lord Thone is uncertain, as he is not mentioned in any other records.

entities.name: Lord Vhokken
entities.description:
Lord Vhokken was a warlord and lifelong loyal servant of Queen Potema in Solitude in early Third Era.

When in 3E 97, King Mantiarco started to investigate rumors of treason of his previous warchief, Lord Thone, Lord Vhokken temporarily took the post of war-chief in Solitude. After Lord Thone was found guilty, Vhokken most likely kept the post.

The evidence of treason might have been, however, set up by Lord Vhokken himself in tandem with his Queen. The demise of Lord Thone was beneficial for both Lord Vhokken and Queen Potema, whom he worked for.

Lord Vhokken has been continuously recorded working close with Queen Potema in later years. He was, without doubt, loyal and trusted servant of the Queen. He is recorded to be a diplomatic emissary of Queen Potema in 3E 99 and 3E 110.

entities.description:

He hired the Lord Vanech's Building Commission in the year 3E 358 to a contract to improve the road between Gideon and Black Marsh. Xellicles paid their commission a hefty amount of gold ranging in the several million septims. Xellicles wanted the trade routes to be repaired in any way possible to keep his goods from spoiling because of the lengthy trip between the two locations. He died before the Commission was able to complete the contract.

entities.name: Lucien Lachance
entities.description:
Lucien Lachance was a Speaker for the Black Hand during the waning years of the Third Era.

In his youth, Lucien traveled in Skyrim and visited the city of Riften. Once there, he came into possession of the Blade of Woe, and eventually became a Speaker for the infamous underground society known as the Dark Brotherhood, after the previous Speaker died fulfilling a contract. The Hero of Kvatch may have gained entrance into the Dark Brotherhood by committing the murder of an innocent, and sleeping in any isolated room or location that the Dark Brotherhood deems 'safe'. When they awoke, Lucien Lachance confronted the Hero, with the offer of the "honor" of becoming a member of the Dark Brotherhood after completing a test which involved murdering Rufio, who resided at the Inn of Ill Omen, north of the town of Bravil.

Lachance resided at Fort Farragut, an abandoned ruin of a fort located northeast of Cheydinhal. The Hero may have visited the fort in order to find out what Lucien had been planning and to also receive Shadowmere as a reward.

After learning of the deaths of various Black Hand members, Lachance deduced correctly that Ungolim, the Listener of the Black Hand, was the next target, and set out to stop his renegade Silencer from destroying the Dark Brotherhood completely. Lachance arrived in Bravil too late. Ungolim lay dead at the foot of the Lucky Old Lady. Lachance angrily confronted his Silencer, and demanded to know why they had betrayed him and the Brotherhood. After seeing the confusion in the Silencer's eyes however, Lucien realized he was mistaken. The Silencer had been tricked into serving the real traitor, who had not died in the Purification of the Cheydinhal Sanctuary, but continued to wreak havoc on the Brotherhood by replacing Lachance's dead drops. Lachance ordered his Silencer to travel to Anvil at once, and lie in wait for the real traitor.

entities.name: Lucina Faleria
entities.description:
Lucina Faleria was the daughter of Lord Nunex Faleria and Lady Faleria.

Lucina was born in 1E 374 as the first child of Lord and Lady Faleria.

On the 19th Sun's Dawn, 1E 421, Lucina went with her family to speak to their father, just after he had finished performing a dangerous ritual to wipe out the Alessian Army at their gate. It was too late for Lord Faleria to cancel the ritual, and the darkness he summoned inadvertently killed Lucina. Lord Faleria buried her with her brother Ianus on the surface, where he never allowed his children to go, writing "Let the Weeping Cease" on her epitaph.

entities.name: Lymdrenn Telvanni
entities.description:
Lymdrenn Telvanni was once a member of the Great House Telvanni during the Accession War in 4E 06, in the province of Morrowind. Lymdrenn was a casualty of the Accession War, when the Argonians under the command of the An-Xileel, invaded Morrowind and slaughtered House Telvanni.

Lymdrenn Telvanni was a prominent member of the Great House Telvanni, who had a wife on his side. In 4E 5, Lymdrenn had a son named Brandyl Telvanni, whose born on the same year as the Red Year, when Red Mountain erupted, sending an endless flurry of ash across Vvardenfell. When the An-Xileel took over in faraway Black Marsh, they amassed an invasion force onto the weakened Morrowind, attacking various city-states including Tear and Mournhold. The Argonians sought to destroy House Telvanni, and so the various strongholds were destroyed, leaving little to no survivors. Both Lymdrenn and his wife both died at the hands of the Argonians, in agony and pain.

By his request, Lymdrenn had his wet nurse named Hidyra Olen take his child, Brandyl Telvanni far away from the destruction, to the west. Olen and the remaining Telvanni took a ship known as the Pride of Tel Vos, escaping Morrowind. Olen was able to keep Lymdrenn's journal so that Brandyl will know his heritage. Unfortunately, the Pride of Tel Vos crashed onto the shores of Skyrim, specifically along the coast of Winterhold. Hidyra Olen had lost Brandyl amidst the wreckage. Young Brandyl was found by an Argonian Couple, who took him in and returned to Black Marsh, where Brandyl was raised as Brand-Shei. Several years later in 4E 201, Brand-Shei returned to Skyrim after he learned of his background. He was able to learn about his heritage, but it is unknown what he did with this information.

entities.name: Lysandus
entities.description:
King Lysandus, also known as the Dragon of Daggerfall, was a king of Daggerfall during the Third Era. He ascended to the throne after the death of his father Arslan II.

His widow was Mynisera, who was the Dowager Queen of Daggerfall. His son and successor is Gothryd, the current King of Daggerfall. Lysandus' mother is Nulfaga, the so-called Mad Witch. Lysandus was considered a true descendant of Tiber Septim.

In 3E 402, the War of Betony broke out. Sentinel, however, claimed Daggerfall had illegally annexed the island following piracy, threats and invasion, whereas Daggerfall claims Betony asked for protection due to an increase in piracy.

Regardless of which account is true, the ordeal surrounding Betony got the attention of King Camaron of Sentinel. Camaron claimed that by a two hundred year old agreement, Betony rightfully was a vassal of Sentinel. Spurred on by his warlords, he declared war on Daggerfall.

entities.name: M'aiq the Liar
entities.description:
M'aiq the Liar is a recurring source of misinformation in the Elder Scrolls series, featured in , , , and . He was introduced by the game designers as an easter egg to provide commentaries about the Elder Scrolls series.

M'aiq is quite an eccentric character; wherever he is found and interacted with, he loves to share his claims of great knowledge from his travelling and opinions with those he meets on a variety of random topics including children, Colovian Fur Helms, the Companions, crossbows, dragons, fighting with one's feet, fish sticks, nudity, werewolves, dwarves, combining magic, multiplayer, and more. He almost always speaks in the third-person when spoken to, like most Khajiit do.

Due to the often dubious nature of M'aiq's dialogue, and M'aiq as a character, whatever degree of truthfulness or reliability any of the information he may provide is up to one's own discretion or interpretation.

M'aiq's history and circumstances are largely kept a vague mystery. The Skyrim incarnation of him claims to not remember his childhood. It is believed that if he was ever directly asked about his past, M'aiq would simply lie in his answer, leaving his true nature unclear.

entities.description:
Macalla was the Queen of Dawnstar during the waning years of the Third Era, sometime around the Oblivion Crisis. Macalla was the leader of the Kingdom of Dawnstar during the Oblivion Crisis and was involved in a political marriage with King Thian of Solitude. The city-states of Dawnstar and Solitude were one of the more influential cities in Skyrim and had control all across the northern coast from Haafingar to Eastmarch. Thian and Macalla sought to expand their territory beyond the northern coast by taking Imperial fiefdoms in the Sea of Ghosts such as Roscrea and Bleakrock Isle. As of now, their progress is unknown. It was likely interfered by the abrupt Oblivion Crisis that ravaged Tamriel.

entities.name: Magnus Septim
entities.description:
Magnus Septim was the eleventh ruler of the Empire of Tamriel. He was the youngest son of Emperor Pelagius Septim II and Empress Quintilla. That made him half-brother of Antiochus Septim, brother to infamous Potema Septim and Cephorus Septim.

Prior to his becoming Emperor, he lived in Almalexia, where he had been a Councillor to the Royal court, being too young to hold a more formal office.

At some point, Magnus married either Hellena, Queen of Lilmoth or Utheilla of the Direnni Clan. With one of these women he had a son named Pelagius as well as a daughter named Jolethe.

At the time of the War of the Red Diamond Magnus was either of King of Lilmoth or Wayrest. and after her death continued to fight the forces of Uriel III. In the year 3E 127, Magnus led an army of Argonians through friendly Morrowind and occupied Kogmenthist Castle. His army would be driven back by Potema Septim, but his brother, Cephorus would defeat Uriel's forces at the Battle of Ichidag. Magnus would later breach the walls of Solitude during the Siege of Solitude, ending the war.

entities.name: Malur Omayn
entities.description:
Malur Omayn is a member of the Dissident Priests mentioned in the book The Battle of Red Mountain.

As stated in the preface of The Battle of Red Mountain, the account of the Battle of Red Mountain was given to Malur Omayn after he confronted the god Vivec with Ashlander traditions about the battle, which are collected in the book Nerevar at Red Mountain, and with prophecies about the Nerevarine.

As a member of the Dissident Priests Malur Omayn would have been in danger of persecution anyway, as the group is outlawed and known members imprisoned. Malur Omayn must have known that confronting one of the gods of the Tribunal Temple, who is behind this persecution, with the Dissident Priest's accusations would cost him his freedom. It is known through conversations with citizens in Morrowind, that Malur Omayn was imprisoned within the Ministry of Truth.

entities.name: Mane
entities.description:
The Mane is the formal title given to the nonpartisan spiritual leader and ruler of Elsweyr and the Khajiit people. Sometimes, they are successful in bringing temporary peace to the province; however, this does not last very long. Historically, the Mane has been known to reside in the city-state of Torval, where he is protected by his Warrior Guard.

Khajiit tradition holds that only one Mane can be alive at any one time and that there is only one Mane, who is simply reborn in different bodies.

A Mane can be born only under a rare alignment of the moons Masser and Secunda when, according to legend, a third moon appears in the sky. In ancient times, the Khajiit would shave off their own manes in deference to the Mane, braiding them into locks that he would incorporate into his own, gigantic mane. Over time, as the population of the region grew, this ritual became impractical.

Now, while all Khajiit still remove their manes, they do so largely as a symbolic sacrifice. The current Mane still wears the hair-locks and braids of his own tribe as well as those of his Warrior Guard, which encompasses hundreds of Khajiit. He is so weighted down by the hair of his kinsmen that he cannot move without aid, and often travels about the countryside by means of a palanquin.

entities.name: Mansel Sesnit
entities.description:
Mansel Sesnit, also known as the Elden Yokeda, was a Redguard Yokeda. He is one of the most notorious Yokedas due to the fact that he almost conquered the Yokudan Empire in the year 2245 of the Yokudan Calendar (1E 609) after eight years of conquest. He was assassinated in the Yokudan year 2253 (1E 617), whereupon the empire fell in control under Randic Torn.

entities.name: Mantiarco
entities.description:
King Mantiarco was King of Solitude in early Third Era. He was also husband of the infamous Wolf Queen Potema Septim.

King Mantiarco's first wife was Queen Amodetha, who was beloved by the people of Solitude. From this marriage Mantiarco's first son was born. He was named Bathorgh. After growing up Prince Bathorgh became one of the mightiest warriors of Solitude. Unfortunately, Queen Amodetha died and left the King widowed.

As a sign of peace between Solitude and the Septim Dynasty, King Mantiarco and Emperor Uriel Septim II signed a Promise of Marriage. Galana Septim was to marry the old king. During his ambassadors visit in 3E 80, the Promise was stolen and hidden from the Hall of Records by the young Potema Septim. By doing this she accidentally became the promised bride herself.

One year later in 3E 81, the 14-year-old Potema married King Mantiarco. Despite the nature of the marriage and the vast age difference, Mantiarco truly loved Potema and allowed her to do whatever she wished. Surprisingly, 15 years later in 3E 97 Queen Potema gave birth to Mantiarco's second son. The old king wanted to name the boy in his own honor, Mantiarco the Second. Potema, however, had far greater plans for her son, thus he was named Uriel Septim III.
entities.short_description: King Mantiarco was King of Solitude in early Third Era. He was also husband of the infamous Wolf Queen Potema Septim.

entities.name: Manwe
entities.description:
Manwe was a Atmoran warrior and craftsman. He was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

He was an accomplished craftsman on Atmora, prior to the Day of Final Passage. He worked in the massive shipyards of Jylkurfyk. He and Menro were the ones that constructed one of the Five Hundred longboats, Jorrvaskr.

During the Day of Final Passage Manwe was part of Jorrvaskr's crew and was under command of its captain, Jeek of the River. It is said that Menro and Manwe took Atmoran timbers with them.

After arriving at Mereth and retaking Saarthal, Manwe as well as the rest of the crew went south to the area that was later known as Whiterun. According to book series Songs of the Return, Menro and Manwe were the ones who founded the city of Whiterun.
entities.short_description: Manwe was a Atmoran warrior and craftsman. He was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

entities.name: Marukh
entities.description:
Marukh, sometimes spelt Maruhk, and also referred to as the Monkey Prophet or Prophet-Most-Simian, was an Imga prophet of the early First Era who was credited with founding the Alessian Order, a once popular monotheistic religion. He is commemorated every 9th of Second Seed on Marukh's Day, in which people remember his solemnity. Perhaps his most influential credo is seen in a famous quote of his "All are guilty until they have proven themselves innocent," a concept still based heavily in the legal system of modern Tamriel. Despite being an Imga, Marukh did not look up to elves the way his fellow Imga did; in fact Marukh and his Alessian Order despised elves to an extremity. While Marukh did play an important part in organizing the modern Cyrodiilic Pantheon, he is often criticized for the severity of some of his principles. Marukh's teachings were sometimes referred to as the "Monkey Truth." After Marukh's death a fanatical sect of the Alessian Order, known as the Marukhati Selective, revived Marukh's teachings sometime in the Middle-First Era in response to perceived heresies of Aldmeri origin.

Marukh was an Imga native to the then-jungled western Colovian coast, an area that is now known as the Gold Coast. After looking at the stars that made the Tower constellation in a state of near-death, Marukh was supposedly visited by the ghost of the Empress Alessia who spoke to him and questioned the validity of Elven rule in Tamriel. Marukh recorded Alessia's words and out of them, formulated the Seventy-Seven Inflexible Doctrines on a scarp with his own blood. These doctrines would later be evolved into the Alessian Doctrines, After his conversation with Alessia, it became apparent to Marukh that death was an illusion, and that through "Proper-Life and Ehlnofic Annulment," one can conquer death itself.

Marukh's Seventy-Seven doctrines eventually gathered a following, thus the Alessian Order was born, which may have originally been known as the Brothers of Marukh. In order to gain more supporters the Alessian Order incorporated many polytheistic elements into their monotheistic religion, adding aspects of various cultures' gods into the Alessian canon as saints and spirits. The Alessian Order quickly spread across Tamriel, Whether or not Marukh lived to see his religion flourish is not known; it is implied in The Illusion of Death that he may have died while writing his doctrines.

entities.name: Masser
entities.description:
Masser, also known as Jode or Mara's Tear, is the larger of the two moons of Nirn, and is red in color.

Among the Khajiit, Masser, as well as Secunda, are revered because their lunar phase helps determine the forms Khajiit take at birth.

Lorkhan, "The Missing God", was sundered into two halves during his destruction, becoming both Masser and Secunda. The two moons symbolize his duality, reminding his man-creations of his struggle, which is most likely another reason for the Khajiit's worship. The Khajiit also refer to Masser as Jode.

Masser vanished together with Secunda between 4E 98 and 4E 100 during what was known as the Void Nights.

entities.name: Mathieu Bellamont's Mother
entities.description:
Mathieu Bellamont's mother was a Breton who was murdered by Lucien Lachance, an assassin of the Dark Brotherhood, when her son, Mathieu Bellamont, was a child. The sight of his mother's severed head drove Mathieu insane and he vowed revenge on the Dark Brotherhood, devising a complex and structured plan to bring it down, partly succeeding.

After his mother's death, Mathieu killed his father who had prayed to the Night Mother for the death of his wife. Lachance took interest in him and invited him into the Brotherhood.

Bellamont carried his mother's head with him throughout the course of his plan, until he took up residence in the Anvil Lighthouse basement, where he set up a small shrine with candles and the head in the middle. It was in this same recluse that he brought the dead bodies of murdered Brotherhood members to be burnt.

The existence of the head and Mathieu's obsession with it was a secret that he only revealed to one person: an assassin named Maria. When Maria expressed disgust over it, Mathieu promptly killed her.

entities.name: Mats
entities.description:
Mats was a Nord member of Moraelyn's Companions sometime during the First Era. Mats, also known informally as "Moraelyn's Slave," was a former slave freed by Moraelyn. Upon killing his former master, Moraelyn gave him some coins and told him that he was "free to go wherever he wished," but chose to travel with him instead.

Before joining Moraelyn's Companions, Mats was a slave to a master located in Reich Parkeep, a village in Morrowind. According to Mats, his sister and he himself were sold so their father could win when gambling too much. For a long time, Mats believed that he was sold for disobedience or because he was useless. One day, his master beat him near death until Mith and Moraelyn stopped him. The master claimed that Mats was a runaway slave and that he could do as he liked with him. Moraelyn and Mits gave the master all the gold they had, giving him the option to take the gold and leave, or be killed by Moraelyn. The master chose the latter and died at the Dunmer's hand.

Moraelyn suggested to Mats that he could take the gold and go where ever he liked but he chose to leave with them. They buried the gold with the master and Mats' been with the group ever since.

entities.name: Maxevian
entities.description:
King Maxevian was a King of Daggerfall during the Second Era. He is known for issuing military orders to the Pale Watch following the destruction of Orsinium and the subjugation of the Orcs in Wrothgar.

In 2E 434, King Maxevian issued a set of military orders to the knights stationed at Watcher's Hold in Wrothgar. In these orders, he commended the knights for their service in vanquishing the Orcs, destroying their capital, and subjugating their lands. He warned that the Orcs would eventually return to their homeland and attempt to rebuild their kingdom, and commanded the knights to maintain an eternal vigil in Wrothgar to strike them down should they return.

He promised that the knights would serve at Watcher's Hold for no longer than five years, after which they would be relieved by new knights and allowed to return home to Daggerfall. The letter was dated the 10th of Hearth Fire, 2E 434.

By 2E 458, however, the promised relief had not arrived. Captain Orrent Retene wrote a desperate a letter to King Maxevian, begging the king to relieve them of their duty. In the letter, Captain Retene stated that he had served faithfully at Watcher's Hold for twenty-four years, and that morale and supplies were dwindling.
entities.short_description: King Maxevian was a King of Daggerfall during the Second Era. He is known for issuing military orders to the Pale Watch following the destruction of Orsinium and the subjugation of the Orcs in Wrothgar.

entities.name: Maxivian Faleria
entities.description:
Maxivian Faleria was the son of Ianus Faleria and a merchant's daughter. He was the paternal grandson of Lord Nunex Faleria and Lady Faleria, though his maternal grandparents were horrified of his elvish features.

Maxivian was the son of Ayleid-Imperial Ianus Faleria and a human merchant's daughter living in the Gold Coast, whom Ianus visited in secret. He was born in 1E 420, though his mother's family were horrified of his elvish traits. They forced her to confess that Maxivian's father was Ianus, Lord Nunex Faleria's son. Lord Faleria took his grandson and hid him with the rest of his Ayleid family, as the Alessian Empire would banish or execute him due to the First Pogrom.

Within days, the Alessian Army was at the gate of Fort Faleria, seeking to arrest Nunex for his crimes of treason after discovering his elvish children. On the 19th Sun's Dawn, 1E 421, Maxivian went with his family to his grandfather, just after he had finished performing a dangerous ritual to wipe out the Alessian Army. Ianus put his hand on his Nunex's shoulder, but it was too late for Lord Faleria to cancel the ritual, and the darkness he summoned inadvertently killed Maxivian and Ianus. Lord Faleria buried him with his uncle Neransi on the surface, where he never allowed his children to go, writing "You are the Light in My Darkness" on his epitaph.

entities.description:
Meksim the Walker was a Atmoran warrior who lived during the Merethic Era. He was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

Meksim was part of the Jorrvaskr crew, commanded by Jeek of the River.

After reaching Mereth and reclaiming Saarthal, Meksim and his crew went south to the area that is now known as Whiterun Hold. They settled there, making Meksim one of the first people who lived in Whiterun.

entities.name: Menro
entities.description:
Menro was a Atmoran warrior and craftsman who lived during the Merethic Era. He was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

He was an accomplished craftsman on Atmora, prior to the Day of Final Passage. He was working in the massive shipyards of Jylkurfyk. He and Manwe were the ones that worked on one of the Five Hundred longboats, Jorrvaskr.

During the Day of Final Passage, Menro was part of Jorrvaskr's crew and was under command of its captain, Jeek of the River. It is said that Menro and Manwe took Atmorian timbers with them.

After arriving at Mereth and retaking Saarthal, Menro as well as the rest of the crew went south to the area that is later known as Whiterun Hold. According to book series Songs of the Return, Menro and Manwe were the ones who started the city of Whiterun.

entities.name: Mentin
entities.description:
Mentin was Duke of Glenpoint in 3E 121. During the War of the Red Diamond he was bought by Potema Septim.

In the late autumn, early winter of 3E 121 Empress Kintyra II led her troops to aid Mentin against Potema, who's army was sighted in the area. However upon the arrival of the Imperial Army Potema's location was unknown. During the same night Kintyra's force was silently assassinated and Empress herself was captured. This led to downfall and eventually death of Kintyra II. Uriel Septim III, Potema's son, took the Imperial throne afterwards.

entities.name: Meris
entities.description:
Meris, also known as Saint Meris the Peacemaker, is a saint of the Tribunal Temple and the Patron of Farmers and Laborers. As a little girl, Saint Meris showed healing gifts, and trained as a healer. She ended a long and bloody House war, intervening on the battlefield in her white robe to heal warriors and spellcrafters without regard to faction. The troops of all the Houses adopted white robes as their standards, and refused to shed the blood of their brethren.

The Swords of St. Meris are five legendary artifacts that will bring despair to the undead. If they are used in war against the Redoran or Indoril, it would be considered a sacrilege.

During the events of , shrines dedicated to her can be found across Vvardenfell, inside Temples, such as the High Fane in Vivec City, the Ghostgate Temple in the Ashlands, or the Holamayan Monastery in the Azura's Coast region.

entities.name: Merkyllian Ramth
entities.description:
Merkyllian Ramth was an Atmoran warrior who lived during the Merethic Era. He was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

On Atmora, Ramth was among the students of wise war-teacher Adrimk. He had not earned his name as a warrior yet.

Along with Adrimk herself and other war-students, Ramth joined Ysgramor's cause to slay the savage elves who were to blame for the Night of Tears. On the Day of Final Passage he had become a crewmember of Darumzu, longboat under command of Captain Ylgar.

During the voyage to the Tamriel (known to Nedes as Mereth), Darumzu was caught in the Storm of Separation and was separated from the rest of the fleet. His boat sailed out safely, however, arriving at Hsaarik Head just a bit late. Ramth finally earned his warrior name on Tamriel; no further details on how it happened have been recorded.

entities.description:
Mhorus Larich was a former King of Skingrad during the fifth century of the First Era. In 1E 478 a terrible plague swept across Cyrodiil killing him and his entire family except for two of his sons, Rislav and Dorald.

entities.name: Mhuvnak
entities.description:
Mhuvnak was a Dwemer architect known for constructing the Vault of Mhuvnak, better known as Frostvault, to contain and protect the Wrathstone. Mhuvnak constructed the Vault with the intention of keeping the Wrathstone safe from invading Nords, Ayleids, and other Dwemer clans.

Sometime, under unknown circumstances, the Wrathstone from the Halls of Colossus in Elsweyr was in the possession of the Dwemer of Mzulft in Skyrim. Due to numerous attacks against the city circa 1E 243 by Nords, Ayleids, and other Dwemer clans, speculated to be attempts to recover the Wrathstone, Mhuvnak took the tablet and fled to the nearby Dwemer city of Kagrenzel, although the prevailing theory is that he simply died in one of the attacks. According to an unknown adventurer searching for the Wrathstone and follwoing Mhuvnak's trail, Mhuvnak was not confident that Kagrenzel could withstand an attack if other were to discover the new location of the Wrathstone. To better protect it, Mhuvnak build his eponymous vault near the city, filled with numerous traps and animunculi. Mhuvnak's ultimate fate is unknown.

Before the reclamation of Mzulft by the Dwemer from the attacking Nords, the location of Frostvault was lost. The Dwemer of Mzulft attempted to find the vault using an Oculory, but there is no indication that they were successful. and the other was given to the Ayleids of Garlas Malatar in Cyrodiil by Meridia.

entities.name: Minglumire
entities.description:
Thane Minglumire was Duke of Vengheto and a member of the Elder Council. He resided in the Imperial City in 3E 153. After Katariah I took the Throne, he commonly served as opposition to her, confronting her at every decision she made. He took a particular delight in pointing out her lack of practical knowledge and experience.

When Emperor Pelagius Septim III was removed from the throne in 3E 153, Katariah I assumed regency the same year. She faced a lot of opposition from the Elder Council, mostly from the Duke and Thane Minglumire, who took great pleasure in exposing her lack of experience.

When Katariah and the Council were discussing the massacre of Imperial soldiers in the village of Armanias, Katariah, pointing out the sweltering climate and sodden swampland, said that if the troops wore their usual armor, they would be in danger. She added that she knew a clever armorer for the job, a former Argonian slave named Hazadir that she met in Vivec City. Minglumire laughed at her, saying that she wants a slave to design the armor; he added that Sirollus Saccus was the best armorer in the city and that he should be armoring the troops. When Hazadir ultimately received the commission, he gave knowledge of Argonian tactics, leading to Armanias's revolt being put down; Katariah won not only the respect of the Elder Council, but even that of Thane Minglemire.

entities.name: Mirtil Angoth
entities.description:
Mirtil Angoth was a Snow Elf who lived during the Merethic Era. A survivor of the Nordic-Falmer War, it is unknown if she suffered the same fate as her other Snow Elf brethren.

During the war, she wrote a journal about her survival, and what the Snow Elves were trying to do to escape the genocide and brutality that the Nords were committing.

entities.name: Mith
entities.description:
Mith was a Nord/Chimer member of Moraelyn's Companions sometime during the First Era. He appears in the King Edward book series. Mith grew up in Blacklight as a stable boy before leaving with Moraelyn.

When younger, Mith was a stable boy for the King of Blacklight. He used to dream and talk alot, which got him beaten by his father. To prevent this from happening, Mith learned to be quick with the broom.

Mith met Moraelyn when his brother was King of Ebonheart. During those times, the king came to visit and brought Moraelyn along, to keep him out of trouble. When Moraelyn looked at Mith, it was out of disgust.

The king told Moraelyn to go clean his knife and told Mith to go with him. Moraelyn, displeased answered that he did not need an escort but Mith was ordered to follow him anyways. After walking in the city, Mith wanted to give directions to the prince but he pushed him right of the piers into the water below. Everyone laughed at him but the elf did not mind them. He made his way to the store and waited for the prince. When Moraelyn came, Mith stole his pouch without him noticing. The prince inside the store and gave the dagger. When he couldn’t pay, he told the smith that he was King of Ebonheart, to which the smith answered that he wa ma the Archmagister. The guard was called and three of them came to arrest the prince. The young boy was so fast that he lost them quickly and got away. Mith however managed to catch him and while he planned to take the money and leave, he told the prince that he might not have been born rich, but he was proud. The prince started laughing. Thats when Mith started to take a liking to him.
entities.short_description: Mith was a Nord/Chimer member of Moraelyn's Companions sometime during the First Era. He appears in the King Edward book series. Mith grew up in Blacklight as a stable boy before leaving with Moraelyn.

entities.name: Mithas
entities.description:
Mithas was greatest of the Dwemer blacksmiths who created the eponymous Anvil of Mithas. It is said that the anvil, together with the Hammer of Gharen, could produce the finest armor and weapons and that only the hammer was strong enough not to shatter upon the mighty enchanted anvil. When used together, they would also reveal the entrance to the dwarven mines beneath Dagoth-Ur. The Anvil had come into possession of King Casik of Ebontheart who tasked the Eternal Champion with retrieving the hammer in exchange for the mountains location, which housed the eighth and final piece of the Staff of Chaos.

entities.name: Modellus
entities.description:
Modellus, sometimes referred to as Lord Modellus, was a member of the Elder Council in 3E 120.

Modellus' first appearance was in 3E 120. He is mentioned in the The Wolf Queen, Book V. It is said that Modellus was already a member of the Elder Council. Modellus' and the then-Princess Kintyra's relationship is also revealed. By the time Modellus and Kintrya II was already engaged.

Second Modellus' appearance dates only year after, 3E 121. He is mentioned in the The Wolf Queen, Book VI. During Empress Kintrya's rule during the War of the Red Diamond Modellus led one of Imperial Armies. He was stationed in the Imperial City, but got tricked by Potema. She sent Modellus a false letter from Kintrya and asked for reinforcements in Glenpoint. The exact date of it is unknown, but Modellus' army was ambushed and defeated in Dragontail Mountains.

Kintrya's letter to Modellus reveals that they wanted to marry in the summer of 3E 121 in the Blue Palace. However, the war got between them. Kintrya was captured in Glenpoint and Modellus himself was defeated in an ambush. They never got married.

entities.description:
Morachellis Hag-Husband was a bard at the famous Bards College in Solitude during the Second Era. Today, many graduates still follow in his footsteps, along with those of Callisos, another famous bard. He was also a scholar whose fields of knowledge included The Towers, Ayleids and Aurbis. Two of his known speculations include that the Doomcrag was an attempt to create a Tower and that a troll's third eye was used to view, not the mundane world, but the overworld of spirits coterminous with it. However, some of his statements were highly dubious as Morachellis also believed that horkers grew into mammoths, and that fire could be classed as a beverage.

entities.name: Moraelyn
entities.description:
Moraelyn, also known as The Witch-King, was a Chimer king of Ebonheart in the First Era. He approached the king of Wayrest seeking a trade deal that would allow him to mine for ebony in the Wrothgarian Mountains. Eventually, he left with the queen of Wayrest, Aliera. Moraelyn was the father of Edward. So far, he has appeared in fifteen books in the series King Edward.

Moraelyn was born into the Chimer House Ra'athim as the son of King Kronin of Ebonheart. His elder brother, Cruethys, was the heir to the throne and would later become King of Ebonheart. He also had another "brother," S'ephen, who was later revealed to be illegitimate. It is also said that Kronin, Cruethys, and Moraelyn were driven from Ebonheart by the Nordic Empire. Following their exile, the three waged relentless raiding campaigns and employed guerrilla warfare in an effort to reclaim their homeland.

As such, he would often visit Blacklight with his brother to meet with the capital's King. It was during those times the elf met the first member of his future band of companions, Mith. When meeting the young man, Moraelyn had nothing but disdain for him and paid him no mind.

During one of those visits, Moraelyn was asked by his brother to go fetch his dagger at a store. Mith was to escort and show him the way. When the young Nord tried to tell Moraelyn where the store was, the young prince pushed him off a pier and took off. While Mith could levitate, he was taken by surprise and fell into the water. While everyone laughed at him, the young man got up and went to wait for the prince at the store. When the prince arrived, Mith stole his purse. The Dark Elf then went to the store and had nothing to pay with. He said he was the Prince of Ebonhart but the owner did not believe him and called the guards. Moraelyn ran away and lost them quickly. Mith managed to catch up and told the prince that he might no have been born rich, but he was born proud. Moraelyn stared at him and laughed innocently. The two have been together ever since.

entities.description:
Morgiah is a Dark Elf Princess of Wayrest, in . As a result of the game's events, she likely became Queen of Firsthold. Her parents were Tiber Septim's General Symmachus and Mournhold's Queen Barenziah.

Morgiah is the second child of Queen Barenziah and King Symmachus. After the chaos that occurred in Mournhold, Barenziah traveled to the Imperial City, where she met with an old family friend, King Eadwyre. He convinced her to move to Wayrest, later becoming the queen of the High Rock city, and in the process, making Morgiah the princess.

Morgiah was born in 3E 384, eight years after Helseth, and was named after her paternal grandmother.

Much later in life, Morgiah marries King Reman Karoodil of Firsthold,

entities.name: Morian Zenas
entities.description:
Morian Zenas was a member of the Mages Guild. He wrote the book On Oblivion, and is considered a well-respected source of information about the many planes of Oblivion. He was a master of Conjuration, as was his apprentice, Seif-ij Hidja Morian is also a master of many different subjects of magic.

He made it his life's ambition to find a way in to the realm of Oblivion. During experimentation with portals, his mind became interconnected with that of his apprentice. He then met with the Dunmer wizard Divayth Fyr, who taught him a method through exploiting a series of portals to various realms created by a Telvanni wizard long missing and now presumed dead. He used this method to then cross over to the realm of Oblivion and Seif-ij was able to document it, with their telepathic connection.

Morian Zenas traveled through Ashpit, Coldharbour, Moonshadow, Quagmire, and Apocrypha. After finally reaching Apocrypha his lust of knowledge takes over, until his thoughts become nothing more than unintelligble whispers. Zenas eventually was lured into the world of research and study, and is believed to have gone back to Apocrypha, or may have lost his sanity and fell into the stacks of Madness in the Shivering Isles.

Zenas published a book or pamphlet called "Commentaries on Beredalmo," referring to Beredalmo the Signifier, in which he stated, "As for the Osseous Orrery: can anyone really claim to comprehend the full intentions of Anumaril in his metamorphosis to instrumentality? Do we even know how many axes of circumpenetration its arms rotate through?"

entities.name: Moricar
entities.description:
Moricar, also known as Moricar the Middling, was the Emperor of Cyrodiil during the Interregnum, following his father's death in 2E 542. He was part of the Longhouse Emperors bloodline, was the son of Emperor Durcorach, and father of Prince Leovic. He had noticeably large pectoral muscles.

After his father Durcorach the Black Drake's death during the invasion of High Rock in 2E 542, Moricar became the second of the Longhouse Emperors of Cyrodiil. He tried to subjugate Solitude at some point, but was driven back. Emperor Moricar sent his son, Prince Leovic, to deal with raiders on the borders of the empire. After the success of the campaign, Moricar let his son choose his reward. Leovic requested to be wed to Clivia Tharn, daughter of Abnur Tharn. Sometime between the 2E 560 and 2E 564, Moricar passed the throne to his son, Leovic, who became the third Longhouse Emperor.

entities.name: Morihatha Septim
entities.description:
Morihatha Septim was the nineteenth ruler of the Third Empire of Tamriel.

Daughter of Uriel Septim V, and the sister of Uriel Septim VI, Morihatha reigned over Tamriel for nineteen years, having ascended to the Throne in 3E 317 upon the death of her half-brother Uriel VI. She continued her brother's work of taking control of the Elder Council, through bribing and bullying the last few members of the Council her brother had not yet reached.

She is responsible for bringing the Archmagister of Skyrim to the Imperial City, and creating the second ever Imperial Battlemage position since Tiber Septim's rule. The state of the Empire had been growing discordant, with many open wars and rebellions running unchecked since the time of her grandfather, Cephorus II. Through calculated strategy, she slowly won back the rebellious vassals, always ensuring never to overextend herself.

Her military campaign was extremely decorated and successful, although their slow pace often frustrated the Elder Council. Thusly, she was supposedly assassinated in 3E 339 in a plot conceived by Argonian Elder Council member Thoricles Romus, who was furious at her refusal to send troops to the rebellious Black Marsh. She was succeeded by her nephew Pelagius Septim IV.

entities.name: Moth Priest
entities.description:
Moth Priests are members of the Cult of the Ancestor Moth, who normally reside in either the Temple of the Ancestor Moths or in the libraries of the White-Gold Tower.

Moth Priests believe it is their sacred duty to study the Elder Scrolls. The priests study and discern the Scrolls in order to divine the future and use the knowledge to aid the Emperor. They also guard the deeper parts of the Temple of the Ancestor Moths where they reside. In combat they typically wield an Akaviri Katana or Dai-Katana. Sometimes, the priests may venture out into the world to search for more scrolls for the library in the White-Gold Tower.

Moth Priests eventually become blind as a result of continuous reading of the Elder Scrolls. Typically, this occurs due to a combined result of both decades of studying the scrolls and old age. However, Dexion Evicus became blind early in his life due to a lack of proper preparation before reading from an Elder Scroll.

entities.name: Mryfwiil the Withdrawn
entities.description:
Mryfwiil the Withdrawn was the Harbinger of the Companions several hundred years after the death of Ysgramor.

Up until this point, the Companions had evolved into a group of soldiers for hire. Typically, their services would be purchased to fight wars, even if it meant they faced each other on the field of battle.

Mryfwiil the Withdrawn foresaw that this path would lead to their eventual destruction and decreed that the Companions would no longer be party to any war or political conflict of any kind.

The decreed was upheld and the Companions today are known as impartial arbiters of honor, in addition to their glories on the field of battle.

Her skill is comparable to that of Cherim.

entities.name: Mynisera
entities.description:
Mynisera was the Dowager Queen of Daggerfall. Mynisera is the widow of King Lysandus of Daggerfall and is the mother of the current King, Gothryd. She was a trusted friend of Uriel Septim VII.

In 3E 403 Uriel VII sent a letter telling her that the Numidium had resurfaced, and that the Totem of Tiber Septim was in the possession of Lord Woodborne of Wayrest. The Emperor asked her to persuade Woodborne to give the Totem of Tiber Septim to the Blades.

However, the War for Betony ruins the Emperor's plan. The letter is indeed delivered to the Queen of Daggerfall, but now the Queen is Aubk'i. Mynisera was then the Dowager Queen, as her husband, King Lysandus had died during the war. Lysandus' son, King Gothryd, now ruled Daggerfall.

In the end the letter ends up in the hands of Gortwog, the leader of the Orcs of Orsinium. The agent that Uriel Septim VII sent, eventually recovered the letter, unfortunately the news of the Totem of Tiber Septim had been spread widely around the Iliac Bay.

entities.description:
Naenra Waerr was an ancient witch who enchanted the infamous sword Umbra for the sole purpose to entrap souls. She was eventually executed for her creation, but not before she was able to hide the sword. Some people speculate that Naenra Waerr was in fact Sheogorath in disguise.

Clavicus Vile wanted a weapon that would send him souls. He could not find a smith who could craft such sword, but Vile eventually came across Naenra Waerr. Naenra crafted the sword, but it was unstable. She told the Prince that he had to imbue the sword with part of his own power so that it could be whole and communicate with it on the mortal plane. Vile agreed to do what the witch asked, but she tricked him. The sword would possess its owner over time. The sword ended up being independent from Vile, a sentient being.

entities.name: Nafaalilargus
entities.description:
Nafaalilargus, also spelled Nafalilargus, N'falilaargus or N'falilaargas, and referred to additionally as Nahfahlaar Nafaalilargus was considered to be not as noble or intelligent as the rest of his race, and it has been said that greed was his downfall.

The Atlas of Dragons refers to a "Nahfahlaar" as having been last seen in 2E 369. The source notes that Nahfahlaar had repeatedly relied on mortals for protection, his last known protector being the King Casimir II of Wayrest, who was apparently "ended" by the Dragonguard in that year. However, Nahfahlaar was able to escape execution himself.

In 2E 582, during the main quest of , the Vestige allies with "Nahfahlaar," who is referred to in promotional content as "a powerful and famous ally from Elder Scrolls lore." Claiming the rewards for the Dragon Rise event will also return ten offerings called "Nafaalilargus' Offering."

In 2E 864, after signing a pact with the loyal Forebears of Hammerfell, Emperor Tiber Septim sent Lord Amiel Richton, his greatest commander, to capture the Crowns headquarters at Stros M'kai. Knowing that the Crown's navy was powerful, Richton assigned Nafaalilargus the task of defeating the navy in order to destroy Prince A'Tor and the Redguard resistance, an event which would later be known as the Battle of Hunding Bay. After A'tor was hit by a poisoned arrow, Nafaalilargus destroyed his ship with a single fiery breath. The loss of A'tor and Stros M'kai brought about the surrender of the Crowns and the Province of Hammerfell to fall under the dominion of Tiber Septim.

entities.name: Nandor Beraid
entities.description:
Nandor Beraid was a fighter of renowned prowess and power elected by the Elder Council to try the armor of Hazadir and be his champion.

After the massacre of Imperial troops outside the village of Armanias in Black Marsh, Empress Katariah I and the Elder Council decided to change the armor of the soldiers engaging the revolt so that they could have better chances of survival in the Marsh's harsh climate and swamps. Katariah suggested they hire an Argonian named Hazadir that she knew to create this new armor; however, councilor Minglumire opposed her suggestion, saying that Sirollus Saccus was the finest armorer in the Imperial City.

Both men were then invited to challenge each other in creating the most efficient armor, with the armorer with better results after seven days being the one chosen by the Empress and the Council to equipping the army on, giving them a delay of seven days. Nandor Beraid and Raphalas Eul were sought out as champions to fight in the soon-to-be created armors; Nandor Beraid would be equipped by the Argonian Hazadir, while the other champion, Raphalas Eul, would be equipped by Saccus. At the end of the seven-day delay, both Eul and Beraid were brought into the Council's arena and fought; Nandor won the fight, leading to Hazadir getting the commission to equip the Imperial troops.

Carved depictions of Narimaya are found in Al-Danobia's Tomb in Hew's Bane.

entities.name: Naryu Virian
entities.description:
Naryu Virian is a well-known member of the Morag Tong, being active during the Interregnum. Naryu's exploits have inadvertently saved countless lives throughout the provinces, such as ending the Llodos Plague in Deshaan and the reign of the Sweetroll Killer in the Gold Coast.

Dark Elf women are often known to be flirtatious and promiscuous, Naryu included; she is known as the "the Beautiful Darkness." Naryu Virian is an agent of the Morag Tong, and uses her soft-spoken feminine voice to coerce people into spilling information or into doing her bidding. However, she is also a ruthless and cunning assassin with a reputation larger than her guild, and completes every writ by any means possible. Naryu also has a free-will attitude and a dark sense of humor, appreciating even the creepiest and foreboding of things. However, she still has a softer side in regard to close friends and allies.

Naryu Virian was born in the province of Morrowind, to Mjahlar Virian, a well-respected member of the Morag Tong. At one point, Mjahlar took in an orphaned child named Odral Quintayn. As time went on, Mjahlar sponsored both Naryu and Odral in the Morag Tong, who trained with each other throughout the years. Naryu trained under the tutelage of Varon Davel, a senior member of the guild. Her father retired soon after, leaving for Vounoura in the Sea of Ghosts. Her time in the Morag Tong had garnered the attention of several of their assassins, including Ashur of the Quiet Blade, who was one of the few who sought to train her, though past it to Davel. During her training, she was observed by the young nobles of House Redoran, Veya Releth and Ulran Releth, both of whom have grown to admire her. As time went on, Naryu rose through the ranks of the Morag Tong, completing writs with relative ease. She had also begun to experiment in her killing methods, using the usual knife and garrote in addition to items in arms-reach like stew pots and even a copy of the Twenty-Fourth Sermon of Vivec's Lessons. She is incredibly resourceful and takes an opportunity that comes her way. Her reputation had eventually surpassed Morrowind, bringing attention to the Eyes of the Queen, specifically Razum-dar. The two eventually came together but were eventually estranged.

entities.name: Nchunak
entities.description:
Nchunak was a notable Dwemer. Nchunak believed in the theories of Kagrenac, that the Dwemer race should have the power of immortality by the use of the Heart of Lorkhan and the Numidium. He traveled among the many colonies of the Dwemer empire to teach the theories of Kagrenac.

At unknown time, Nchunak traveled to the city of Kherakah. The city of Kherakah "taught the precepts" of Kagrenac, where the people believed in the teachings and ideas of Kagrenac and the Tonal Architects. When Nchunak was at Kherakah, he learned that the people were still studying the concepts of Kagrenac, yet interested in learning them. He also learned that he was the only one who could teach the ideas of Kagrenac and lead the people to enlightenment. He took this as a great compliment, and gave thanks and left with an infinity of bows.

entities.name: Neloth
entities.description:
Neloth, also preferred as Master Neloth, is a powerful wizard lord and Councilor of House Telvanni. In 3E 427, he served as Master of Sadrith Mora and lived in the tower of Tel Naga, where his Mouth was Arara Uvulas. He kept a collection of rare treasures that at one point included Mehrunes' Razor, although such items were often stolen by other Telvanni. A talented enchanter, he studied and gathered staves crafted by Azra Nightwielder and was known to enjoy canis root tea. Along with the other Telvanni councilors, he recognized the Nerevarine as Hortator.

During his time in Sadrith Mora, several Telvanni councilors were believed to have been assassinated at the command of Trebonius Artorius, the Arch-Mage of the Mages Guild.

During the late Third Era, Neloth lived in Tel Naga, a Telvanni tower located in Sadrith Mora, Vvardenfell.

During this time he served as a clan leader in House Telvanni. Several of his fellow Telvanni councilors were assassinated if the Nerevarine joined the Mages Guild. Neloth managed to survive and went on to become the most powerful wizard of House Telvanni. Some even consider him to be the most powerful wizard in all of Morrowind.

entities.description:
Neransi Faleria was the first son of Lord Nunex Faleria and Lady Faleria.

Neransi was born in 1E 383 as the second child of Lord and Lady Faleria.

On the 19th Sun's Dawn, 1E 421, Neransi went with his family to speak to their father, just after he had finished performing a dangerous ritual to wipe out the Alessian Army at their gate. It was too late for Lord Faleria to cancel the ritual, and the darkness he summoned inadvertently killed Neransi. Lord Faleria buried him with his nephew Maxivian on the surface, where he never allowed his children to go, writing "May My Actions Bring You Peace" on his epitaph.

His province made a treaty with the Second Aldmeri Dominion, and a number of skirmishes with the empire in 2E 861 were reported during his reign. He is depicted wearing the hair-locks of his entire tribe. It is unknown if he was still Mane after Septim conquered Elsweyr.

entities.name: Nienolas Ulwarth
entities.description:
Nienolas Ulwarth, also known as Nienolas Ulwarth the Mighty, was an Argonian hailing from Blackrose. He was a great Axe-warrior, and is said to be the only person with a greater proficiency at this weapon than Ellabeth, the "Queen of the Axe."

However, Nienolas stated that he loved more "his ax handle and shaft," for there was another woman that he loved, Lorinthyrae. As revenge, Ellabeth then captured Nienolas, and gave Lorinthyrae three doors to which she had to open one of three doors. She was told that behind one of the doors was her love, behind another, a great demon, and behind the third, freedom. However, Nienolas was already deceased, as Ellabeth had already killed him.

entities.name: Night Mother
entities.description:
The Night Mother, also known as the Unholy Matron, the Shrouded Lady, Blood Flower the Lady Death, and the Mistress of the Void, is the bride of Sithis, the Dread Father of the Dark Brotherhood. Those who wish to have someone assassinated pray to the Night Mother by performing the Black Sacrament, and she extends their requests to her Listener, who in turn passes the task on to the Speakers. It is debatable whether she was a single person, a title passed down through the eras, or an immortal spirit.

According to Dark Brotherhood beliefs, she is wife of Sithis, but was told by Sithis to kill her five young children in his name. After the deed was done, Sithis gave her the honor of being his wife and being the head of the Dark Brotherhood.

The Night Mother is likely to have lived during the Second Era, as indicated in the in-game book The Brothers of Darkness. In , her tomb is located underneath the Lucky Old Lady statue in Bravil. There are skeletal remains of one adult and five children in her tomb. This takes into account her children in Dark Brotherhood beliefs. The Night Mother might also be the same person as the Lucky Old Lady.

One indication of this is that the Lucky Old Lady is surrounded by five children. However, the woman depicted by the statue was said to have lived in the First Era. The Night Mother has also been credited as an incarnation of Daedric Prince Mephala, whereas she is also identified as Severa Magia in Morrowind during the Third Era. Before this, in , the Night Mother is identified simply as an immortal spirit with the likeness of either a Redguard or a Khajiit woman.

entities.name: Nilara Ienth
entities.description:
Nilara Ienth is a Dunmer and sister to Milore Ienth. She along with her lover Athras left Solstheim and returned to Morrowind were they own a manor in Mournhold. Nilara mentions in her letter that they haven't visited the old manor for fifty years now, but says that nothing has really changed to the place.

Later on she tells her sister that Athras have returned to work as a jewelcrafter in the city. Nilara says that he brings in a lot of coin to the manor, and at the rate things are going for them now, she looks forward to see the manor in its full glory in the future.
