entities.name: Nocturnal
entities.description:
Nocturnal (in Daedric script, ) is the Daedric Prince whose sphere is the night, darkness and mystery. She is also known as the Night Mistress and Lady Luck. The Cyrodiilic Thieves Guild leader, the Gray Fox, has the Gray Cowl of Nocturnal, which truly represents the sphere's darkness quality; it permanently removes the wearer's specific identity from all history. Regardless, the Cyrodiilic Thieves Guild venerates Nocturnal by ending talks with the saying "Shadow hide you." The summoning date of Nocturnal is 3rd of Hearthfire.

Nocturnal and Azura have been referred to as sisters, though whether in the literal or the metaphorical sense is unknown. referencing her claim as part of the original Void She is thought to be the "eldest and most powerful of the Daedric Princes."

Although Nocturnal has arguably one of the largest followings of all the Daedric Princes, she has no form of organized clergy. There are a few who call themselves priests of Nocturnal, though the Night Mistress does not herself seem to show them any particular favor. Indeed, Nocturnal seems to have no real interest in worship. A temple of Nocturnal does exist called the Twilight Sepulcher, located in Skyrim, though this was built around the portal known as the Ebonmere, the portal to Nocturnal's plane of Oblivion known as Evergloam. Supposedly, Nocturnal is the source of a thief's luck, which flows from the Ebonmere and plays a heavy role in the lives of any who use the shadows to do their work, though none know what price is paid in return.

Nocturnal has at least one cult dedicated to her, the Whispering Shadows. They operated throughout the Clockwork City in the Second Era. In Summerset she has only one known human follower, known as Earl Tundilwen.

entities.name: Nulfaga
entities.description:
Nulfaga, called the Mad Witch, was a Dowager Queen of Daggerfall. Nulfaga was the grandmother of the current King of Daggerfall and is married to Arslan II. She was a powerful mystic and necromancer. She had a dragon familiar named Skakmat.

When Sentinel declared War on Daggerfall, due to the submission of the Isle of Betony to Daggerfall, Nulfaga and Medora Direnni urged King Lysandus not to enter the war. Both sorceresses foretold doom to King Lysandus, but Lysandus insisted on his decision to fight against Sentinel. Nulfaga retired to Shedungent in the Wrothgarian Mountains and left Skakmat behind to report to her.

Although Skakmat, with his unnatural fog, tried to avoid the Battle of Cryngaine Field, eventually as foretold, Lysandus was killed by a Sentinel arrow. Upon learning of this, Nulfaga descended into madness and remained within Shedungent, spending the entirety of her time in magical studies.

Nulfaga was misled into believing that the murderer of her son, Lysandus, was in an unmarked ship travelling from the Imperial City to Daggerfall. The ship was, in fact, the ship of the mysterious agent sent by Uriel Septim VII. She summoned a storm to swallow and destroy the ship and its passengers, though the agent survived.

entities.name: Nurarion the Perfect
entities.description:
Nurarion the Perfect, also known as Nurarion the Voiceless, was a Merethic Era Altmer hero and member of Khunzar-ri's kra'jun – his company of heroes – who fought against the dragons of Elsweyr. Prior to his adventures in Elsweyr, he fought against the magic of the Maormer king Orgnum in Sunhold, and was the brother of Sunhold's king.

During the Merethic Era, the city of Sunhold in the Summerset Isles was under the constant sufferance of storms conjured by the king of the Maormer, Orgnum. To combat the storms, Nurarion led Sunholds mages in performing a counter-spell to ward off the storms. To ensure his success, Nurarion made a deal with the Daedric Prince Clavicus Vile to give him a voice that could call forth "a doom greater than any called by Orgnum." Characteristic for bargains made with Clavicus Vile, Nurarions newfound power came with a heavy toll: although he was able to end the storm, the power of his voice was so strong that he could not speak without posing a great risk to those around him. His voice was said to "cut lightning bolts in half and turn mountains to rubble," and that only his foes ever heard him speak, and even then, only in whispers. in Wormroot Depths.

Nurarion was found in exile by the Khajiit hero Khunzar-ri, and was the first member of Khunzar-ri's kra'jun formed to combat the dragons that raged across Elsweyr. Knowing that they could not defeat the dragons in direct combat, the kra'jun, consisting also of Anequina Sharp-Tongue, Cadwell, and Flinthild Demon-Hunter, resolved to trap the dragons where they could do no harm. After the group tricked the dragons into having their strength sapped into Jode's Core, Nurarion suggested trapping them in the Halls of Colossus, which they successfully accomplished.

After the disbandment of the kra'jun following Khunzar-ri's death, Nurarion used his voice to scream years of range and sorrow into a gem in an unknown cave, said to be only the second time he ever screamed, the first time being to save Sunhold. The power of his voice caused the cave around him to collapse, resulting in his death, although the gem is said to remain undiscovered along with echoes of his power. It has been claimed that the leftover echoes will sunder Anequina from Pellitine, or level Rimmen in the blink of an eye.

entities.name: Nuulion
entities.description:
Nuulion was a master smith from Summerset Isles who lived during the Second Era. He is known for having kept the Dunmer Ulvul Llaren as a slave and for guarding the secrets of crafting Elven armour from moonstone and quicksilver.

Nuulion was a renowned craftsman specialising in the forging of Elven armour. He resided on the homeland of the High Elves, Summerset Isles, where he was celebrated for his skill. He was active from the fifth through the seventh century of the Second Era. In his service was a Dunmer named Ulvul Llaren, who worked for Nuulion for three centuries, operating the bellows in his forge. Over that time, Ulvul learned all the nuances of the process: the use of moonstone, the addition of quicksilver for gilding, and the special method of quenching in salt water.

Nuulion is described as a cruel master. Eventually, Ulvul managed to escape and, driven by revenge, revealed to the world the secrets of Elven armour that had previously been known only to the Altmer. As a result, the knowledge of crafting Elven armour spread beyond Summerset.

Nuulion's subsequent fate is unknown; he may have died before or after Ulvul's escape, but no definite records exist.

entities.name: Obeth Arnesian
entities.description:
Obeth Arnesian is an unseen character mentioned in Sinderion's Field Journal.

According to the journal, Obeth was a treasure-hunter who had been exploring Blackreach, when he came upon what he had assumed was just a "noisy red weed." Being unsuccessful in finding anything else of value, he took the weed, hoping to find someone who would find it of value. After much searching, he tracked down Sinderion, a Nirnroot enthusiast in Skingrad, Cyrodiil. Sinderion paid Obeth 1,000 septims, and they never crossed paths again.

entities.name: Ocato of Firsthold
entities.description:
Ocato of Firsthold was a pivotal Altmer mage in the Third Empire of Tamriel in the latter years of the Third Era, and the beginning of the Fourth. Ocato was once a long-standing member of the Elder Council, and the defeat of Jagar Tharn at the hands of Uriel Septim VII's Eternal Champion promoted Ocato to being one of the few known Imperial Battlemages of the Empire. This position he served during the Nerevarine Prophecy, and during the Oblivion Crisis.

In the Crisis' conclusion, the Septim Dynasty became extinct. Ocato was then appointed as Potentate of the Empire, leading in an emperor's stead until one could be found; a position that would cost him his life, leaving Ocato assassinated in 4E 14. Without Ocato as a unifying force, the Empire descended into a chaotic period known as the Stormcrown Interregnum.

Much is unknown about Ocato's early life. The only strongly-implied information is him being an Altmer with his chosen name being "Of Firsthold;" meaning he comes from the ancient city of Firsthold, in the Summurset Isles.

In unknown circumstances, Ocato became involved with the Elder Council. By 3E 405, when encountered by Uriel Septim VII's Agent in his affairs with the Kingdom of Daggerfall, the Agent noted that Ocato was "long" of the Council.

entities.name: Olms
entities.description:
Olms, also known as Saint Olms the Just, is a saint of the Tribunal Temple and the Patron of chandlers and clerks.

Saint Olms is known to have founded the Ordinators, and also conceived and articulated the fundamental principles of testing, ordeal, and repentance, in the Ministry of Truth.

Olms was considered important enough to have a Canton in Vivec City named after him. According to Guide to Vivec, St. Delyn Canton and St. Olms Canton are residence cantons for commoners and paupers. The Temple charges very reasonable rents for comfortable workshops, shops, and apartments, and most of Vvardenfell's crafts and light industry are housed in these cantons. The Abbey of St. Delyn the Wise is on the top tier of St. Delyn, and Hlaalu Councilor Yngling Half-Troll has a top-tier manor on St. Olms.

During the events of , shrines dedicated to him can be found across Vvardenfell, inside Temples, such as the High Fane in Vivec City, the Ghostgate Temple in the Ashlands, or the Holamayan Monastery in the Azura's Coast region.

entities.description:
Oreyn Bearclaw was a legendary Dunmer hero, known for slaying the Glenhwyfaunva of the Elven wood, protecting his clan in the process.

According to the Daedric Prince Malacath, however, the legend of Oreyn Bearclaw was a false story, with most of Bearclaw's legendary deeds being accomplished by his Orcish companion: Kharag gro-Khar.

In Oreyn Bearclaw's Helm can be obtained by summoning Malacath at his shrine in Assurdirapal. In his Helm can be given to the player by Farvyn Oreyn's descendant, Modryn Oreyn. In , the Helm of Oreyn Bearclaw can also be acquired as part of "Dreams of the Dead" in the Gallows Hall Creation Club content.

entities.name: Orgnum
entities.description:
Orgnum (also spelled Orghum) is the Maormer King of the island kingdom of Pyandonea.

According to legend, Orgnum was a phenomenally wealthy nobleman, who used his finances to launch a rebellion against the powers of the land. He and his followers were banished for this to a place separated from Aldmeris by an impenetrable mist, Pyandonea, "Veil of Mist." This boundary proved so effective that the followers of Orgnum never again disturbed their former countrymen in Aldmeris.

According to the historical fiction dramatization of Potema Septim's life The Wolf Queen, he is described as having white limpid jelly-like skin and bald white eyes.

Three months before the War of the Isle in 3E 110, King Orgnum met with Potema Septim in Solitude to make an agreement that when the Maormer took over Tamriel, she would be Empress of the continent. In turn Potema promised that she would lead an insurrection against her brother, Emperor Antiochus Septim. On the night of their first meeting, Potema shared her bed with Orgnum, as she deemed it to be the polite and diplomatic thing to do.

entities.name: Paarthurnax
entities.description:
Paarthurnax (Dragon Language: Paar–Thur–Nax, "Ambition–Overlord–Cruelty"), sometimes referred to as the Old One, is an ancient dragon who resides in Skyrim. He serves as the leader of the Greybeards, noted as surpassing all the others in his mastery of the Way of the Voice.

While few details are known regarding Paarthurnax as a supporter of the Dragon Cult during the Dragon War, the Dragonguard considered him a legendary lieutenant of Alduin, At some point during the war, Paarthurnax, along with a few other dragons, switched sides and taught the rebels the Voice. Their leaders Gormlaith Golden-Hilt, Hakon One-Eye, and Felldir the Old were all taught personally by Paarthurnax, who was the first dragon to defect to the rebels, becoming the first Tongues. It is said that Kyne called upon Paarthurnax, as Paarthurnax pitied Man, to teach them the Voice.

Late during the Dragon War, the leaders of the rebellion used an Elder Scroll to cast Alduin adrift into time atop the Throat of the World. Paarthurnax was not present during the fight but felt when Alduin was defeated, like the other dragons.

During the 373rd year of the Second Era, the Dragonguard noted that Paarthurnax was already under the protection of the Greybeards of High Hrothgar, refusing to act until they had an opportunity to strike against him.

entities.name: Pelagius Septim
entities.description:
Pelagius Septim was the second ruler of the Septim Empire, and Tiber Septim's grandson. He ruled Tamriel for less than three years; however, he was still seen to be as strong of a ruler as his grandfather had been. It is said that, had he not been killed, the rule of Pelagius could have continued the Golden Age of Tamriel.

In 3E 41, Pelagius was the first of the Third Era Emperors to be assassinated, as an unknown enemy of the Septims hired assassins. He was killed by the Dark Brotherhood while praying at the Temple of the One in the Imperial City. His reign lasted less than three years. Because he had no children he was succeeded by his first cousin, Kintyra Septim.

Amaund Motierre claimed that the death of Pelagius Septim caused a necessary change in Imperial policy. For a similar reason, Motierre and his supporters desired the assassination of Titus Mede II in the Fourth Era.

Pelagius Septim II was the sixth ruler of the third Empire of Tamriel.

In 3E 63, eleven year a widower with a young son named Antiochus, Prince Pelagius traveled to the High Rock city state of Camlorn to impress the Princess Quintilla. However, upon arriving, he learned of a demon Werewolf terrorizing the city. Instead of wooing, the Princess and Pelagius, using his sword and her magic, went out to save the kingdom. They slayed the beast and with the powers of mysticism, Quintilla tied the beast's soul to a gem. Pelagius had the gem made into a ring and married the Princess. The prince stayed in the Kingdom until the birth of their child, Potema.

Pelagius Septim II ascended to the throne when his father, Uriel II, died in 3E 82. Pelagius Septim II inherited a host of debts due to his father's poor financial and judicial management. To cope with this, he dismissed all of the Elder Council, allowing only those members willing to pay a large sum of money to re-join. He encouraged similar actions of other Kings and rulers throughout the then un-united Tamriel.

entities.name: Pelagius Septim III
entities.description:
Pelagius Septim III, born as Thoriz Pelagius Septim, and the Mad Emperor, was the Jarl of Solitude, and the twelfth Emperor of Tamriel and a member of the Septim Dynasty. When Pelagius was just over a year old, Emperor Antiochus Septim died and his daughter, Kintyra, assumed the throne to the acclaim of all. Kintyra II was Pelagius' cousin and an accomplished mystic and sorceress. Kintyra II's reign was usurped by her and Pelagius' cousin Uriel, by the power of his mother, Potema, the so-called "Wolf Queen of Solitude", during the War of the Red Diamond.

After his accession as High King of Skyrim, Pelagius married a Dunmer woman named Katariah I, and become Emperor of Tamriel after the death of his father Magnus Septim in 3E 145, and lasted almost two years until he was removed and put into a asylum and his wife Katariah, later succeeded him to the throne as both Empress regent-dowager and Empress regnant, until their son Cassynder was old enough to rule.

Pelagius was born in 3E 119 (or 3E 125) as Thoriz Pelagius Septim, to Magnus Septim, King of Lilmoth and his wife Hellena or Utheilla Direnni in the city of Wayrest in High Rock at the end of his uncle Antiochus I's glorious reign. He had a sister named Jolethe, and presumably had another brother and sister. At a young age, Pelagius's mother instilled in him that danger could come from anywhere, which made him paranoid and suffered night terrors.

The conflict and civil war, which became known as the War of the Red Diamond broke out, splitting the Empire in half. The civil war was known as some of bloodiest battles in the Septim bloodline. Pelagius' father, Magnus Septim allied himself with his brother then the King of Gilane and future Emperor Cephorus, against the Usurper, and had brought the wrath of Uriel III and Queen Potema at Wayrest. During the civil war between the Septims, Pelagius, along with his brothers, sisters, and his mother Utheilla Direnni fled to the Isle of Balfiera, in the center of the Iliac Bay.

entities.name: Pelagius Septim IV
entities.description:
Pelagius Septim IV was the twentieth Emperor of Tamriel. He succeeded his aunt, the Empress Morihatha, who was assassinated in 3E 339. Pelagius' mother, Eloisa, had died four years prior to his ascension, thus making the 25-year-old Pelagius the first in line for the Septim throne.

Pelagius Septim IV's rule was one of integration throughout Tamriel, continuing on the work of Morihatha Septim; but, despite his beneficial traits and patience, the progress he made was slow. This is largely because the kingdoms had been free of constraint for so long, even a benign influence was seen as odious. The eastern province of Morrowind still remained relatively alienated from the Empire, its customs differing strongly from the Empire's, and its rulers being largely unreceptive of the Empire's diplomacy. Closer to home, however, small kingdoms were gradually integrating further with the Empire and its culture. After Pelagius' 29-year reign, the Empire was more united than it had been for hundreds of years. Scholars agreed that the Empire had not seen such unity since the reign of Uriel Septim I.

Pelagius died in 3E 368, at the age of 54, of internal problems. He was succeeded by his son, Uriel Septim VII, who swore on his father's deathbed to continue the work Pelagius had begun to unite all the provinces across Tamriel.

Pelladil allegedly summoned an army of Stone Atronachs to build Blackrose Prison from the ruins of various nearby Lilmothiit ruins, under orders from Potentate Versidue Shaie.

entities.name: Pentarch Khorb
entities.description:
Pentarch Khorb is a Nord Vampire and a member of the Gray Host who appears in The Elder Scrolls Online: Greymoor. He is an assassin who, on the orders of the Ashen Lord, Rada al-Saran, assassinated Queen Gerhyld of Solitude. He is identifiable by his eyepatch, and a bloody trail follows him from Solitude to Blackreach.

Khorb was a Nightblade who served as a Pentarch of the Gray Host. He was tasked by the Ashen Lord with the assassination of Queen Gerhyld. After committing the murder, he fled the capital, leaving a trail of blood that led into the depths of Blackreach.

He was eventually tracked to the Dwemer ruins of Kagnthamz, where he took refuge in a chamber filled with comatose or dead commoners, whom he was draining to heal himself.

After Old Mjolen performs a divination on an amulet that Khorb lost during his flight from the palace, the Vestige and Fennorian are able to track him magically. The trail leads them to an unfortunate hunter's camp, and then to the Chillwind Depths cavern.

entities.name: Peryite
entities.description:
Peryite (Daedric script: ) is the Daedric Prince of pestilence and plague. Among mortals, he is considered the most affable of the Princes and among those with the worst reputations. Among the Daedra, he is charged with ordering the lower planes of Oblivion.

Peryite can be summoned in his shrine by offering him a silver ingot, a deathbell flower, vampire dust and a flawless ruby.

Indirectly, Peryite has influenced the lives of nearly every mortal inhabitant of Nirn throughout history; he is the Lord of Pestilence, the cause of many plagues and pandemic diseases. He is typically listed along with princes such as Molag Bal and Vaermina as one of the few truly evil Daedric Lords, in the mortal Man and Mer’s sense of the word.

It is said that the goddess Kyne gives Peryite the souls of skeevers when they die.

entities.description:
Pierric was the Breton lord of Cumberland and the father of High King Emeric.

In Pierric's hall of business in Wayrest, Emeric learned of the tracking of shipments, the balancing of accounts, and the fluctuation of currencies. Discontent with his son only learning the ways of peace and trade, for two months every summer he had Emeric spar with the Cumberland Master of Arms each morning. Unlike his son, Pierric was not a member of the royal family of Wayrest, as Emeric was persuaded to assume the throne after the entire royal family was killed by the Knahaten Flu, which also took Pierric himself.

entities.name: Porcia Loran
entities.description:
Porcia Loran was a Breton spymaster of the Imperial Legion during the Fourth Era.

Porcia was the mentor of spies serving the Legion. Sometime during the Fourth Era a former spy by the name of Talym Rend had struck a deal with Sheogorath which demanded Porcia be turned mad. During this time, Porcia was actively serving with Breton Legionnaires in Skyrim, who were engaging with Reachmen invaders at Bthardamz.

In order to turn Porcia mad, Talym had ambushed a Reachman courier, and planted fake intel in Bthardamz for Porcia to discover, however, while doing so, Talym had also activated a number of traps in the ruin, putting the Reachmen on high alert, and resulting in the capture of Porcia. As such, Talym had to save his former mentor. The Spymaster did, however, find the fake intel, and assumed it was legitimate. The intel pointed towards a nearby Grove of Mara, where a sacred flower grew which was required to combat the Reachman poison, according to the intel.

When the Legionnaires arrived at the grove and demanded the sacred flowers, the priests of Mara refused. As such, Poria ordered her men to attack the grove, resulting in the deaths of numerous priests and the Legion obtaining the flowers. Imperial alchemists refined the flowers into a gas, but due to the low quantity of the gas, Porcia ordered it only to be used when the Reachmen poison would be used on the bulk of the Imperial force. The fighting took place in a passage leading to Bthardamz, and when the combat between the Reachmen and the Legion became heavy, the Reachmen unleashed the poison. In response, Porcia unleashed her antidote.

entities.name: Potema Septim
entities.description:
Potema Septim, also known as Potena, and the Wolf Queen, was a Queen of Solitude in Skyrim's hold of Haafingar during the Third Era. She was the daughter of Pelagius Septim II and Quintilla. Her efforts to claim the Ruby Throne resulted in the War of the Red Diamond, a lengthy and horrible war that devastated the Empire, turning it into a "land of death." Most of her Imperial family was killed, famines were widespread, and the war ended with the death of her and her lineage. Her actions during the war cemented her reputation as one of the most notable necromancers in Skyrim's history. She is also one of the few historic figures to have been viewed by scholars as "unambiguously evil."

Four years prior to her birth, Potema's father, Prince (and future Emperor) Pelagius Septim II had been a widower for eleven years, and already had a son named Antiochus, Potema's half-brother, with whom he traveled to the city-state of Camlorn in High Rock. He then tried to impress Princess Quintilla, however Camlorn had been terrorized by a great demon werewolf. Pelagius and Quintilla, using his sword and her magic, defeated the beast. Quintilla using her magic to chain the beast's soul into a gem, which would be later be made into a ring on their wedding. Pelagius stayed in the city-state until Potema's birth.

Potema was born in 3E 67 to Emperor Pelagius Septim II, a member of the powerful Septim Dynasty, and upon seeing her as a newborn, her grandfather, Emperor Uriel Septim II, is famously said to have declared that she looked like "a she-wolf ready to pounce," a chillingly accurate omen of her future nature and legacy. Raised in the Imperial City, her upbringing was marked by emotional neglect, with distant parents and an elder brother, Antiochus, a decadent noble sixteen years her senior who was more interested in his own pleasures than in his sister.

By the age of fourteen, Potema was celebrated across Tamriel for her beauty and attracted numerous suitors. However, her marriage was ultimately a political one. She was wed to Mantiarco, the aging King of Solitude, likely following her interference in a marriage contract originally intended for her aunt Galana, a document she is said to have stolen and hidden.

entities.name: Prince Bathorgh
entities.description:
Prince Bathorgh, known as The Man Who Cannot Be Hit, was son of beloved Queen Amodetha of Solitude and Lord Thone, Warchief of Solitude. He was considered to be the firstborn son of King Mantiarco, but according to The Wolf Queen, Book II, in 3E 97 Mantiarco found out about an affair of his deceased wife Amodetha and his trusted warchief Lord Thone. As a result, Bathorgh was stripped of his rights to the throne of Solitude and banished from Skyrim. His place as an heir was taken by Mantiarco's and Potema's son Uriel Septim III. Bathorgh was a renowned and skilled fighter, annual champion of Tournament of Stamina in Solitude.

"It's the Tournament of Stamina today, you know the Prince would never miss that. The fellow invents new strategies of self-defense every year to show off during the games. Don't you recall last year, where he entered the ring unarmored and after twenty minutes of fending off six bladesmen, left the games without a scratch? He dedicated tha't bout to his late mother, Queen Amodetha'." - Lord Vhokken in Year 3E 97

"He's no friend to me or you, your highness, but you must give the man his due respect. He moves like lightning. You wouldn't think it of him, but he always seems to use his awkwardness to his advantage, to throw his opponents off. Some say he learned the style from the Orcs to the south. They say he learned from them how to anticipate a foe's attack by some sort of supernatural power." - Lord Vhokken in Year 3E 97

"His highness Prince Bathorgh has finished the tournament and awaits you to present his award. He has successfully withstood attacks by nine archers and the giant scorpion we brought in from Hammerfell. The crowd is roaring his name. They are calling him The Man Who Cannot Be Hit." - Lord Vhokken in Year 3E 97

entities.name: Prince Hubalajad
entities.description:
Prince Hubalajad, or Prince Hew was a Yokudan nobleman, who tried to colonize Hew's Bane.

Prince Hew attempted to colonize a peninsula in southern Khefrem, Hammerfell, which he named "Khefrem's Boot." When he arrived, he found a barren land hostile to most life, land bad for crops due to brackish water and heat. Hew attempted regardless and failed in almost every endeavor. In the end though, he successfully founded the city of Abah's Landing, located in a naturally protected harbor on the east coast of the peninsula.

Within the city Hubalajad built a lavish palace, from which his heirs would rule for generations. He also forged, to the south, the No Shira Citadel, which was abandoned due to the seasonal flooding undermining defensive capabilities. To connect Hew's Bane with the other Ra Gada holdings, he built the Princes Gate, therefore connecting all Ra Gada held land in Hammerfell.

Purilla Falen was a Dunmer war hero of Great House Hlaalu who fought in the Great House War of 2E 559. Purilla was assigned to guard the construction of a trading outpost in the disputed territory fought over by House Hlaalu and House Dres. Purilla's forces were attacked by an army of Dres mercenaries that outnumbered them five to one, but despite being highly outnumbered she held off the attack until reinforcements arrived through a portal connected to the city of Narsis.

Though the forces of house Hlaalu successfully defended the outpost, Purilla and most of her soldiers died in the fight.

Pyokos is a Sload who serves as an agent to Morgiah, going undercover as a double agent in the Order of the Black Worm. A misshapen creature, fat and warty, its mouth seemingly too big for the Cyrodilic it spoke. Morgiah met this sload years ago off the coast of Hammerfell. She knew he could be trusted, so she sent him as a spy to Thras to learn what he could. Pyokos told her that the Thrassians believed Mannimarco to be sleeping, but the higher priests believed, secretly, that he was dead or ascended and no longer concerned with mortal affairs following the Warp in the West.

entities.description:
Queen Bianki was a Redguard Queen of Gilane. She was also Cephorus Septim's bride.

First records of Queen Bianki date to 3E 98. She is mentioned in the The Wolf Queen, Book III. By that time she was already the Queen of Gilane and the bride of then 21-year-old Cephorus. She was visiting the Imperial Palace after the death of Emperor Pelagius Septim.

Bianki's second appearance dates 3E 109. She is mentioned in the The Wolf Queen, Book IV. She already had several healthy children with Cephorus, though the exact number of children is unknown.

In 3E 127, after Emperor Uriel's death, Cephorus took his place and Bianki became Empress.

entities.name: Quintilla
entities.description:
Quintilla, also referred as Quizara in Biography of the Wolf Queen, was daughter of King Vulstaed of Camlorn. She was believed to be one of the most beautiful Princess in Tamriel, and was skilled in all maidenly skills as well as being an accomplished sorceress.

In 3E 63, the widowed Prince Pelagius Septim II arrived at the court of Camlorn. During his visit, the city-state was terrorized by a great demon Werewolf. According to The Wolf Queen, Book I, Quintilla and Pelagius defeated the beast and its soul was bound to a gem. Pelagius made this gem into a ring and used it to marry Quintilla.

It is said that the soul of the great wolf remained in the gem until the birth of couple's first child, Potema Septim, who later became known by the name of Wolf Queen of Solitude. Quintilla had two other, much younger children - Cephorus and Magnus, both of whom became Emperors in their lifetimes. She was also step-mother to Pelagius's first son Antiochus, but they were never close. He was already fourteen when Quintilla and Pelagius met.

Quintilla is once again mentioned in the The Wolf Queen, Book III. She is said to have visited Potema in the Blue Palace in 3E 99, shortly after death of Pelagius. In the book, she admits that she is not happy with Antiochus becoming the Emperor, and that it is unfortunate that she will not live to see Potema's son Uriel take the throne of Solitude. She gives Potema a necklace with a single yellow gem—the one with werewolf's soul—as a gift to Uriel. The necklace is enchanted with an Illusion spell that makes the wearer able to Charm whosoever he chooses, a worthy skill for both king and emperor. She also correctly predicts that Potema's husband, King Mantiarco, already over 80 years old, will die very soon.

entities.name: Ramth the Greater
entities.description:
Ramth the Greater was a Atmoran warrior who lived during the Merethic Era. He was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

On Atmora Ramth was among the students of wise war-teacher Adrimk. He had not earned his name as a warrior yet.

Along with Adrimk and other war-students Ramth joined Ysgramor's cause to slay the savage elves who were to blame for the Night of Tears. On the Day of Final Passage he had become a crewmember of Darumzu, longboat under command of Captain Ylgar.

During the voyage to the Skyrim, known to Atmorans as "Mereth," Darumzu was caught in Storm of Separation and was separated from the rest of the fleet. However, the boat sailed out safely, arriving at Hsaarik Head just a bit late. Ramth finally earned his warrior name, Ramth the Greater, on Tamriel; however, no further details on how it happened have been recorded.

When Harald conquered Skyrim, Randagulf was defeated. So respectful of this great hero was Harald, that he took his gauntlets as his own. These gauntlets, worn by both mighty warriors, are believed to give the wearer additional strength.

entities.name: Raphalas Eul
entities.description:
Raphalas Eul was a fighter of renowned prowess and power elected by the Elder Council to try the armor of Sirollus Saccus.

After the massacre of Imperial troops outside the village of Armanias in Black Marsh, Empress Katariah I and the Council decided to change the armor of the soldiers so they could have better chances of survival in the Marsh's different climate and swamps. Katariah suggested they hire someone she knew, an Argonian named Hazadir, to create this new armor. However, councilor Minglumire opposed her suggestion, saying that Sirollus Saccus was the finest armorer in the Imperial City.

Both men were then invited to challenge each other in creating the most efficient armor, the goal being to allow the Empress and the Council to determine on who's shoulders to put the responsibility of equipping the army; each armorer was given a period of seven days to do so. Raphalas Eul and Nandor Beraid were sought out as champions to fight in the soon-to-be created armors, with Eul being Sirollus Saccus's champion while Beraid would get equipped by Hazadir. At the end of the delay, both Eul and Beraid were brought in the Council's arena and fought. Raphalas Eul lost the fight, thus Hazadir took the commission to equip the Imperial troops.
entities.short_description: Raphalas Eul was a fighter of renowned prowess and power elected by the Elder Council to try the armor of Sirollus Saccus.

entities.name: Rasha
entities.description:
Rasha was a Khajiit Speaker of the Black Hand, and leader of the Cheydinhal Sanctuary at the time of the Great War.

He, along with Listener Alisanne Dupre, spoke of reinstating training for Shadowscales born in the Black Marsh to help revive the Dark Brotherhood. They eventually deemed this as too great a cost of resources. After Alisanne fell defending the Night Mother's Crypt, and a new Listener was not revealed, Rasha claimed to be the Listener himself. His treachery was unmasked when he failed to speak the Binding Words, and he was thus killed by his brother Garnag at Cicero's insistence.

entities.name: Ravate
entities.description:
Ravate is a wizard who took part in a "contest of wills" with the Daedric Prince of Madness, Sheogorath.

Ravate sought out Sheogorath, "the most capricious of the Daedric Princes," in order to win his favor. When he finally met the Prince, he spoke humbly and offered to drive a thousand men mad in exchange for greater magical power. Sheogorath was in an agreeable mood. He proposed a counteroffer, or as he called it, a "game," during which Ravate must maintain his sanity for three days while Sheogorath does his best to drive the wizard insane. If Ravate survived, Sheogorath would grant him his wish.

Though Sheogorath found the idea of the game fun, Ravate felt less so. When he attempted to flee, Sheogorath denied him and trapped the wizard within his realm, the Shivering Isles, blocking off all exits. Ravate had no choice but to wander the realm, spending each moment looking over his shoulder and jumping at every noise. Each moment brought new terror as he waited for Sheogorath to begin.

After three days, Sheogorath appeared to Ravate. By then, he was convinced every creature was out to get him at the whims of Sheogorath. Sheogorath, however, revealed he had, in fact, done nothing, and that Ravate had driven himself mad with his delusions. Therefore, Sheogorath had won. From that day forward, Ravate served Sheogorath and warned daring travelers who tried to approach Sheogorath of their inevitable defeat.

entities.name: Raven Direnni
entities.description:
Raven Direnni was a female Altmer and a prominent member of the Direnni Bloodline.

Raven Direnni was an enchantress whose magic helped secure the final victory over the Alessians at Battle of Glenumbria Moors, she was one of the earliest occupants of Castle Daggerfall.

Before the Psijics of Artaeum, it is said that she created the art of Enchanting, learning how to bind a soul into a gem and use that to ensorcel all manners of weaponry.

The last King of the Ayleids, Laloriaran Dynar, met with Raven at some point between 1E 461 and 1E 477.

entities.name: Ravius Terinus
entities.description:
Ravius Terinus was a renowned thief in the city of Sutch, Hammerfell. Ravius was supposedly in the Thieves Guild by his own admission, however this is unlikely; at the time, the last-known Guild in the region had perished some 450 years prior. He is detailed in the book Thief of Virtue.

Ravius Terinus was a thief of high skills in the city of Sutch, Hammerfell. The ruler of the city was a Baron with a fascination for rare coins; Ravius believed that the Baron should "share his wealth" with the people, especially with Terinus himself. He thus endeavored to break into the Baron's vault and acquire the coins for himself.

One night, Ravius entered the baron's castle to steal the rare coins, avoiding the guards and unlocking not only the door with only nine lockpicks but also disabling the seven traps guarding the treasures. Right about to make his escape, the Baron discovered the thief's illegal presence in the castle and sent his guards after him, blocking the only way out. Ravius made his way even deeper into the castle and entered the Baroness Veronique's room. Though she initially assumed that he would force himself on her, Ravius had no such desire, though he soon realized that seducing her might be the only way out. Thus, the thief made the choice of leaving the money but keeping his life, successfully seducing the Baroness thanks to her poor relationship with her husband. By the time the guards came into the room, Veronique had hidden Ravius within her chambers; she handed over the coins to the captain of the guard, saying that Terinus had left it behind after escaping through a window. Ravius slept with her until dawn, leaving exhausted, but sated.

Ravius was an arrogant, yet witty and intelligent man; his arrogant nature could, however, be backed up by his skills as a thief, and he was additionally known for his "handsome looks." To penetrate the baron's castle, he cleverly used an arrow of penetration and It only took him nine lockpicks to unlock the building's doors; with nothing but a fork, a bit of string, and a wineskin, he disabled the seven traps placed to guard the Baron's treasure. Ravius also proved his intelligence by his ability to assess situations quickly, such as when he saw that the only out of the castle was to seduce the Baroness Veronique and sleep with her so she would hide him from the guards. He did call this a "double sacrifice" when he realized he would lose the coins, perhaps alluding to the Baronesses "plainness"; however, he also willingly slept with her the entire night and was "sated," suggesting he was just referring to how he would have to lay out his dignity to get what he wanted.

entities.description:
Rayelle was the Breton Princess of Shornhelm during the 6th century of the Second Era. She was daughter to King Ranser of Shornhelm who started a civil war against High Rock and Hammerfell after High King Emeric married Maraya, a Redguard noblewoman, instead of his daughter.

Rayelle was Emeric's first choice of wedlock but before the marriage papers were signed, he married Maraya, Redguard princess of Sentinel which subsequently strengthened the Wayrest-Sentinel alliances and turned out to be a prosperous agreement. However, this angered Rayelle's father, King Ranser, who waged the so-called Ranser's War on High Rock and Hammerfell.

entities.name: Red Bramman
entities.description:
Red Bramman was an Argonian pirate who operated in the Imperial province of Black Marsh during the First Era. His raids along the coast of Topal Bay eventually attracted the attention of Empress Hestra, who ordered the Imperial Navy to hunt him down.

Unable to capture him through battle in Topal Bay, the Imperial Navy followed Bramman down a river whose entrance had been disguised by thickets of mangroves near Soulrest. The navy followed him deep into the heart of Black Marsh, cornering him and his bandits near what would become Blackrose. Upon his capture, the Imperial Navy executed Bramman and brought his head to Empress Hestra.

Reglius was let go from Lord Vanech's comission and like Decumus Scotti, he had traveled to Falinesti (Valenwood) after being invited for work by Liodes Jurus. After meeting Scotti, Reglius falsely informed the Cyrodiil that Liodes Jurus was dead. During a Khajiit attack on a Bosmer village where they had found refuge, Reglius and Decumus Scotti tried to escape by climbing a large tree and jumping to a cliff, however a coin dropped out of Scotti's bag and alerted the Khajiit to their presence. As a Khajiit warrior started climbing the tree after them, Reglius panicked and attempted to jump to the cliff, falling and breaking his neck upon impact with the ground.

He is a character mentioned in the A Dance in Fire series.

entities.name: Regulus Sardecus
entities.description:
Regulus Sardecus, also known as General Sardecus or Sardecus the Rock, was an Imperial general, who led the Fourth Legion during the Blackwater War, after their first campaign, led by Augurius Bucco, had failed. Sardecus was a near-legendary figure, having fought in countless campaigns, and had distinguished himself as both a soldier as well as a general. He was everything that Bucco was not. He was stout, humorless, had hawk-like features, and walked with a limp (a lingering injury from the Battle of Argonia). He spoke in short, gravely sentences that commanded obedience. He deliberately avoided using all formal dress and regalia, preferring to wear a simple centurion's panoply with a white crest to signify his station.

By 1E 2823, Sardecus and his Legion had regained all the territory that Bucco had lost when he had retreated.

Disease accounted for roughly half of all fatalities in the first campaign, followed closely by mysterious disappearances. By Sardecus' estimation, Argonian raids had taken a distant third. With these facts in mind, he created a new war doctrine and disseminated it to all of his officers. The crux of the strategy was simple: the only way to conquer Black Marsh was to destroy it. Sardecus deployed entire cohorts of engineers and sappers to the front lines. While legionnaires launched raids on border villages, the supporting troops drained swamps, salted rice paddies, and felled hundreds of trees. The most well-known event of this portion of the war was the "Great Burn" of 1E 2828. Records indicate that in early Rain's Hand 1E 2828, Elissia Mallicius (one of Sardecus' most-trusted legates) ordered a unit of sappers to set fire to a peat bog outside of Stormhold. The sappers followed the orders, not knowing that the bog was just one part of a massive underground network. Months passed before legionnaires started reporting random fires, some as far away as Soulrest and Gideon. It took several more months before the Legion realized that the entire region was on fire. An inferno of burning peat and detritus raged underfoot for more than three years. The already deadly marsh became so dangerous that the Legion was forced to give ground for the first time in the better part of a decade. Hundreds of soldiers were lost to "swamp lung" and gas explosions before they escaped the scalding heat of the fire. It was a devastating blow to both the Legion and the Argonians. This marked the end of the second campaign, and the end of Sardecus' tenure as general.

Soon after the legion's retreat, Sardecus fell ill and died before reaching the Imperial City. The official diagnosis was a severe infection from a wound he had sustained on the way out of the marsh. However, the true circumstances of Sardecus' death are still a matter of historical debate. The author of the book The Blackwater War believes that the Shadowscales played some role in his death, as Sardecus was a high-ranking general, and had died shortly after the Great Burn.

entities.name: Reman Cyrodiil II
entities.description:
Emperor Reman Cyrodiil II was the third ruler of Reman Empire, after Emperor Kastav Cyrodiil and before Emperor Reman Cyrodiil III.

Reman II was born in 1E 2794 and his reign began in 1E 2812 although other sources say he was crowned circa 1E 2806 following Kastav's deposition. Reman's first move as Emperor was to put an end to the Winterhold Rebellion that his predecessor had recklessly started, and did so using swift negotiation tactics.

Reman quickly revealed that he was a skilled tactician and politician and always showed respect to his own men and to his enemies. Whenever he conquered new territory he did so with a careful hand, as to not disrupt local culture and traditions, but mostly to establish good trade. He gathered many advisors from the conquered territories to help him figure out how to rule it correctly. Reman was known as the Emperor who focused on his people more than any other. Under his rule, Necromancy and Daedra Worship was abolished and the Second Empire thrived. However, Reman desired more.

Around the 2830s he ordered the Legions of the Empire to launch a full-scale offensive into Argonia, an event known as the Blackwater War. The campaign proved to be very difficult with many casualties and losses. Only the northeastern parts of the province were captured resulting in Reman declaring an end to the offensive in 1E 2837.
entities.short_description: Emperor Reman Cyrodiil II was the third ruler of Reman Empire, after Emperor Kastav Cyrodiil and before Emperor Reman Cyrodiil III.

entities.name: Reman Cyrodiil III
entities.description:
Reman Cyrodiil III was the last ruler of the Reman Empire after Emperor Reman Cyrodiil II. It was his death, and the death of his son, Juilek Cyrodiil, that sparked the end of the First Era and the introduction of the Second Era.

During his life he married Empress Tavia, whom he later imprisoned in Black Marsh and fought in the Four Score War of Morrowind. He had a mistress called Rijja in 1E 2920, whom he later had imprisoned. On the 6th of Sun's Height, 2920, Rijja attacked the Emperor causing a loss of his right eye. It is possible that some sort of regent or potentate ruled over the Empire during the gap between the death of Reman Cyrodiil II and the ascension of Reman Cyrodiil III.

entities.name: Rhorlak
entities.description:
Rhorlak was one of captains of the Five Hundred Companions. It is said that he was the most battle-hardened and unflinching of all captains. Rhorlak was in command of Chrion and its crew.

After crossing the Sea of Ghosts and reclaiming Saarthal, the Circle of Captains was assembled. It was decided that every captain and his crew should go their own path. Rhorlak and his crew went to the far east, to "the eastern lands near the Red Mountain".

There Rhorlak made a camp and slaughtered any elves to approach. He strongly believed in Ysgramor's tales and considered all of Mer liars. That led to merciless killing without any second thoughts. It is where the long lasting conflict between the Nords of Skyrim and the Dunmer of Morrowind originated.

After Rhorlak received news of Ysgramor's death, he put down his axe, in grief and swore never to pick it up again.

entities.name: Ria Silmane
entities.description:
Ria Silmane was one of the few known Imperial Battlemages of the Elder Council, and a former apprentice to ex-Imperial Battlemage Jagar Tharn. Appointed to the Council following Tharn's resignation, Ria is the deuteragonist in the events of .

Murdered by her former master in 3E 389, Ria's assumed death and the kidnapping of Emperor Uriel Septim VII marked the beginning of the Imperial Simulacrum. As a spirit, Ria was the guiding figure of the Eternal Champion, divining all locations of the eight pieces of the Staff of Chaos. She preserved her spirit form for nearly ten years as an exceptionally talented sorceress. She finally passed in 3E 399, by using the last remainder of her magic to help the Champion infiltrate the Imperial Palace.

At an indeterminate time, Silmane became the apprentice to Imperial Battlemage Jagar Tharn, then head of the ruling body of Tamriel: the Elder Council. After the End of Harvest festival that year, Tharn resigned from his duties on the Council claiming that he wished to study other circles of magic; a cover story for his plan to kidnap Emperor Uriel Septim VII. He then advocated for his apprentice, Ria Silmane, to resume his duties as Imperial Battlemage of the Empire, and head of the Elder Council. The council fully approved.

Soon after, Tharn returned with the Staff of Chaos and usurped the Emperor's power in 3E 389. Silmane attempted to warn the Elder Council of his treachery, however, Tharn found her first, and used the Staff of Chaos to destroy her corporeal form.

entities.name: Rid-Thar-ri'Datta
entities.description:
Rid-Thar-ri'Datta (sometimes spelled Rid-T'har-ri'Datta) was the first Mane of the Khajiiti people. He restored peace to the Khajiit during the rebellions against the Elsweyr Confederacy, granting equal power between the masses.

He encountered several times in his spiritual form across the Reaper's March's questline, where he grants his council to the Lunar Champions Khali and Shazah while they are on their way to become the next Mane.

Rid-Thar-ri'Datta was born sometime during the Second Era under the rare alignment of the two Moons, thus becoming the First Mane.

After Keirgo of Anequina and Eshita of Pelletine combined their kingdoms to form the province of Elsweyr in 2E 309, a class struggle had surfaced, with many feeling the ruling class had betrayed them. Keirgo petitioned the Second Empire for help, but they had just lost their Potentate Versidue Shaie, and were unable to help. The cities of Anequina were under constant attack, and after the old capital Ne Quin-al fell to the rebels, it seemed as though Elsweyr would fall under the weight of its union.

He was supposed to meet Decumus Scotti, a senior clerk for Lord Vanech's Building Commission, to discuss plans for the trade routes in Black Marsh, but never got to because Scotti was robbed by highwaymen and left for dead. His business operated out of Black Marsh during the Third Era.

entities.name: Rijja
entities.description:
Rijja was the Redguard mistress to Emperor Reman III in 1E 2920. One of his most trusted councils, she was framed for treason by Versidue-Shaie and imprisoned in the Thurzo Fortress. Despite this, the Emperor would continue to visit her regularly, and even agreed to free her for extradition to Hammerfell. However, after he offhandedly mentioned his intention to make her sister Corda his new consort, she clawed at his face in a fit of rage, leaving him without his right eye. She was executed two months later. Ironically, it was this act that ultimately pushed Corda to later assassinate the Emperor for the Night Mother, with Versidue taking Reman's place as Potentate and officially ending the First Era.

entities.name: Rislav Larich
entities.description:
Rislav Larich, also known as Rislav the Righteous, was a former King of Skingrad and was the eighth child of King Mhorus of Skingrad.

After the death of his father, Rislav's older brother, Dorald Larich, became the King of Skingrad. When Dorald became king he immediately swore fealty to the Alessian Empire, which angered and shocked many of the nobles in the Colovian Estates. Rislav, who was enraged by Dorald's actions, killed his older brother and took the throne for himself during the Coup at Skingrad. After this a war broke out between the Alessian Empire and the allied kingdoms of Skingrad and Kvatch.

Though Rislav had no previous experience in warfare he managed to defeat the much larger Alessian army by use of guerilla tactics.

entities.name: Roeth
entities.description:
Roeth was an Atmoran warrior. He was one of the Five Hundred Companions. He had a war-wife, Britte, who were both part of the Krilot Lok crew.

After safely reaching Mereth and reclaiming Saarthal, the Circle of Captains was assembled. It was decided that every captain and his crew should go their own ways. Unlike most of the bands, Krilot Lok went back to the sea. It is said that they visited Yokuda and saw Redguards long before they settled on Tamriel.

The crew of Krilot Lok visited many lands along the shores of Tamriel, including the great deserts of Elsweyr and southern marsh later known by the name of Black Marsh. Roeth fell while battling Argonians in Black Marsh.

entities.description:
Roleke was a High Queen of Skyrim, residing from the city of Solitude. She is also sometimes referred to as "Head-Rolling" Roleke.

In the late-First Era, Roleke served Skyrim as its High Queen. Roleke was personally performed over twenty executions for people who had rebelled against her. Her reign was considered to be long and bloody.

Not long after the executions, the people of Solitude rose up against their Queen, and besieged the Blue Palace. Roleke was later said to have been killed by her own children, who had also died from their wounds in the aftermath.

Roris, also known as Saint Roris the Martyr, is a saint of the Tribunal Temple and the Patron of Furnishers and Caravaners. Roris was captured by Argonians just before the Arnesian War, Roris proudly refused to renounce the Tribunal faith, and withstood the cruel tortures of Argonian sorcerers. Vengeance and justice for the martyred Saint Roris was the rallying cry of the Arnesian War.

Roris was able to help the faithful Dunmer Baranat during his battles with the Coribael Brothers. Baranat beseeched him for help against Horis Coribael, and in return Roris made him "as unyielding as the heart of Oblivion.

During the events of , shrines dedicated to him can be found across Vvardenfell, inside Temples, such as the High Fane in Vivec City, the Ghostgate Temple in the Ashlands, or the Holamayan Monastery in the Azura's Coast region.

He was one of the few that survived the collapse of Crystal Tower, and his heroic deeds saved many Altmer during the Oblivion Crisis. Lathenil of Sunhold later followed in his footsteps.

entities.description:
Saeel was Lu'ah Al-Skaven's deceased husband whom she wanted to raise from the dead.

Saeel died as an Imperial soldier in battle twenty-five years prior to the events of , helping the Empire retake the Imperial City from the Aldmeri Dominion during the Great War. His body was burned before Lu'ah could attempt to resurrect him.

entities.name: Saint Kaladas
entities.description:
Saint Kaladas was a saint and craftsman who lived around two centuries after the death of Pelinal Whitestrake.

Kaladas built the Chapel of Zenithar in Leyawiin. He built the chapel in memory of the story of how after the death of Pelinal, a messenger took his Mace to the settlement of Leyawiin.

Years later, Kaladas passed on and was laid to rest in the under-croft of the Chapel of Zenithar. Not long after, people began saying that while they prayed at his tomb they saw visions of the Mace at the other end of a large chasm.

During the Third Era, a Knight of the Nine named Sir Ralvas went the Chapel in the hopes of recovering the mace and saving his dying order. He spent months with little food and rest praying at the altar and trying to reach the mace with no success. He noted that while he felt like everything in the Chasm was real, the priest said he never moved. Soon Ralvas gave up and left the Chapel broken and in despair. His body was later found by Sir Amiel and Sir Juncan who took his body to be laid to rest at their Priory.

entities.name: Saradin the Lost Love
entities.description:
Saradin the Lost Love is a wispmother and optional boss in . She is found in the watery depths of Skyreach Catacombs.

She was the last princess of Skyreach, and daughter of High King Durac. She planned to marry her friend and her father advisor's Virmaril, but her father married her off to King Kestic. As the Ra Gada advanced on the Nedic kingdom, Virmaril appeared before Durac and his council, in the guise of helping them. Instead he slaughtered them and ascended into lichdom. Saradin was apparently killed or transformed in the process.

She is the author of Saradin's Diary, which can be found near her.

entities.name: Savirien Chorak
entities.description:
Savirien-Chorak (?E ??? – 2E 430 or 431) was a Tsaesci who served as Potentate, the de facto leader of the Empire of Reman Cyrodiil in its final days. He is the son of the Potentate Versidue-Shaie. He was one of two leaders of Cyrodiil hailing from Akavir, following the war fought between Akavir and Cyrodiil. Not much is known of him, except that he and his father were responsible for the end of the 'Reman' Line, and the convenient placement of them as the sovereign leaders of Cyrodiil. He succeeded his father upon his assassination in 2E 324, but in Sun's Dawn in 2E 430, he and every one of his heirs were assassinated by the Dark Brotherhood. His palace, as his father's, was not in the Province of Cyrodiil itself. As a result of his death, Orsinium lost its status as an Imperial province, and was sacked by Breton and Redguard forces in 2E 431.

entities.name: Secunda
entities.description:
Secunda, also known as Jone or Shandar's Sorrow, is the smaller of the two moons in orbit of Nirn, the other being Masser. The moons can easily be seen in the night sky throughout Tamriel. These two moons do not contribute anything to gameplay outside of scenery in games, except for the fact that Secunda becomes the Bloodmoon in expansion of .

Among the Khajiit, Secunda, as well as Masser, are revered because their lunar phase helps determine the forms Khajiit take at birth.

Lorkhan, "The Missing God," was sundered into two halves during his destruction, becoming both Masser and Secunda. The two moons symbolize his duality, reminding his man-creations of his struggle.

Secunda vanished together with Masser between 4E 98 and 4E 100 during what was known as the Void Nights.

During his rule, Senecus Goddkey helped administer the Forebears ideals in place of Volag, who had disappeared. Sentinel soon became an exotic retreat for the nobles of High Rock, coming from places such as Daggerfall and Wayrest.

entities.name: Seryn
entities.description:
Seryn, also known as Saint Seryn the Merciful, is a saint of the Tribunal Temple and the Patron of Brewers, Bakers and Distillers. She was a pure virgin of modest aspect, who could cure all diseases at the price of taking the disease upon herself. Tough-minded and fearless, she took on the burdens of others, and bore those burdens to an honored old age.

During the events of , shrines dedicated to her can be found across Vvardenfell, inside Temples, such as the High Fane in Vivec City, the Ghostgate Temple in the Ashlands, or the Holamayan Monastery in the Azura's Coast region.

entities.name: Shalidor
entities.description:
Arch-Mage Shalidor, sometimes referred to as Archmagus Shalidor, was a famous Nord Archmage and powerful wizard who lived during the First Era. He created the Labyrinthian in Skyrim, the mage sanctuary of Eyevea, and his personal compound of the Fortress of Ice, near Winterhold. Shalidor was said to have a vast knowledge of the workings of Magicka that few could ever compare to.

Shalidor once fought the Dwemer of the Rourken Clan.

The Archmage Shalidor was well known for his spell Shalidor's Mirror, which was a ward capable of reflecting offensive spells back at the caster. It is speculated that Shalidor created the spell after his battle with the Rourken Clan, trying his best to emulate the effect of the Dwemer shield, Spell Breaker. Shalidor was also known to put a large amount of effort into researching the dragons that once roamed Skyrim. Shalidor also performed rituals that extended his life so he could continue his work.

Most of the research and writings that Shalidor wrote while in Labyrinthian were lost to the ages, but some of what he wrote is still out there. During the Fourth Era, the College of Winterhold attempted to seek out more of Shalidor's writings to expand The Arcanaeum, improve the arcane skills of the members there and to help the college expand and improve as a whole.

entities.name: Shezarrine
entities.description:
The Shezarrine is an influential and sometimes god-like figure who is believed to be a mortal incarnation of the Missing God, Lorkhan. The term "Shezarrine" itself is derived from "Shezarr," the Cyrodilic understanding of what is essentially the Missing God, and was first used in reference to Pelinal Whitestrake in the Song of Pelinal. in a similar light to how many old myths portray the roles of Shor and Shezarr.

The Shezarrine is believed to have found its origins after the defeat of Lorkhan, at the ending of the Dawn Era. Auri-El and Trinimac, who, according to Elven legend, were unable to destroy Lorkhan's Heart, instead decided to hide it where they thought it could never be found. The Heart was launched to Nirn from Auriel's Bow, and where it landed Vvardenfell was formed. Though Lorkhan's body was all but destroyed, his soul could not be extinguished due to his living, yet sundered, divine center, and so was doomed to wander the creation of the Et'Ada. For this reason, it is believed that whenever the Shezarrine appears, Lorkhan is in some sense physically walking Nirn. This is indicated through various Khajiiti and Yokudan myths regarding Lorkhan's demise stating "We curse you, noisy Lorkhaj, to walk Nirni for many phases," and "Sep could only slink around in a dead skin, or swim about in the sky." According to Mankar Camoran, the Tower is the conduit through which gods can revert themselves into mortal forms.

Elven chronicles of the late Merethic Era and onward record varying accounts of a legendary and immortal human personage wandering Tamriel, gathering armies, conquering kingdoms, ruling them, then leaving to wander again. This strange occurrence may find some clarity in Elven myth, where Lorkhan is stated to be "more of a limit than a nature, so he could never last long anywhere".

Pelinal Whitestrake was the great hero of the Alessian Slave Revolt that occurred during the early years of the First Era, and may have been the Shezarrine.

entities.name: Shrike
entities.description:
Shrike was the baron of Lainlyn during the Warp in the West, and he was the leader of the regional knightly order, the Host of the Horn. Baron Shrike was described as a tyrannical ruler, and many members of the court wanted a change from this dictatorship. Among these people are Lord Kain, one of the leaders of the knightly order, and Shrike's younger brother. Lord Kain created a new knightly order called the Knights of the True Horn and he organized a coup d'état to fight Shrike's rule. The coup ended in failure, and members of the True Horn dispersed across Western Tamriel. Baron Shrike would remain the leader of Lainlyn into the Warp in the West. Shrike's Lainlyn would become a part of the Kingdom of Sentinel along with other regions in the Iliac Bay.

entities.name: Sinmur
entities.description:
Sinmur was a Giant killed by Ysgramor with his axe Wuuthrad. Ysgramor and his Five Hundred Companions were at war against Sinmur and his clan, hundreds were slain, Companion and giant alike. Eventually, Sinmur was cornered in his barrow and killed. It is said that Sinmur's Club was shattered by Wuuthrad before Ysgramor took Sinmur to his knees as Wuuthrad was buried deep into his skull.He was buried in Shor's Stone Mine, in the Rift of southeastern Skyrim.

Sinmur is known to have killed two Companions, Valdur and Hakra.

entities.name: Sir Amiel Lannus
entities.description:
Sir Amiel Lannus, also known as just Sir Amiel, is an Imperial knight ghost. When he was alive, he was the head of the Knights of the Nine, before the order fell apart. His ring unlocks the Priory of the Nine's secret underbelly.

Sir Amiel founded The Knights of the Nine in 3E 111, following his heroic return from the War of the Isle, with the purpose of recovering the Crusader's Relics, the weapons and armor of Pelinal Whitestrake, which had been lost for thousands of years.

He led the Knights against the Wyrm of Elynglenn to recover the Cuirass of the Crusader, which had not been seen since the First Era. This established the Knights' fame early on.

In 3E 121 when the War of the Red Diamond began, Sir Amiel was unable to keep his knights out of the war, due to the fame which the Knights were built on. The Knights of the Nine were officially dissolved, by Imperial decree, in 3E 131.

entities.name: Sir Berich Vlindrel
entities.description:
Sir Berich Vlindrel (or simply referred to as Sir Berich) was a member of the old Knights of the Nine.

After the founding of the Knights of the Nine, many great and respected knights joined the order, its fame peaked near the time Berich joined and found two of the lost relics.

However, the War of the Red Diamond started in 3E 121, drawing many of the knights into the war, despite the best efforts of Sir Amiel.

Sir Berich decided to leave for the war, and take the Sword of the Crusader and Greaves of the Crusader with him. While leaving he was stopped by Sir Caius who argued with Amiel about not taking the sword into battle. Berich then baited Caius knowing he would draw his weapon, when he did Berich cut him down on the Priory steps. He then left for the war and became a darker person.

entities.description:
Sir Byric of the Flame was a noble knight that served the Duke of Alcaire Castle in 2E 542 and was an honored member of the Knights of the Flame, the regional militia owned by the Duke. In 2E 542, Sir Byric defended the city of Alcaire from the Reachmen of the Reach by burning the fields surrounding the castle, resulting in the end of the army. The Alcaire Knights were renamed to to the Knights of the Flame for Byric's risky move. A statue was erected in his honor in Alcaire.

entities.name: Sir Caius
entities.description:
Sir Caius was a member of the old Knights of the Nine. He was killed by Sir Berich while trying to stop him from leaving to go fight in the War of the Red Diamond and take the Sword and Greaves of the Crusader.

Caius blames himself for Berich becoming what he turned into, saying that if he hadn't drawn his weapon and fought his friend none of it would have happened. Despite this, he had hoped to reconcile with his friend in the after life, something that has yet to happen as his spirit never arrived to guard the last relic.

Sir Caius is first encountered by the Hero while they are searching the Priory of the Nine for the Cuirass of the Crusader. Sir Caius, as well the rest of the knights' spirits (excluding Berich) are in the under-croft guarding there only remaining relic they have. Sir Caius and the rest of the knights will each fight the Hero to see if they are worthy to take the Cuirass and be told where to find the rest of the relics.

After hearing about the massacre at the Chapel of Dibella, in Anvil, the Hero has set forth to find the Relics of the Crusader and stop the attacks lead by Umaril the Unfeathered.

entities.name: Sir Casimir
entities.description:
Sir Casimir was a member of the old Knights of the Nine. Casimir left the order during the War of the Red Diamond, taking the Gauntlets of the Crusader with him. When he returned from the war he was changed, no longer having pity for the weak and helpless. He hoped to return to the services of the Nine and went to the Chapel of Stendarr.

While there, a beggar began pestering him daily and soon Casimir let his temper get the best of him. He struck the beggar out of anger and killed him, right in the Chapel of the God of Mercy. He was cursed by Stendarr and the Gauntlets fell off of his hands and became impossible to move. The curse left Casimir tired and weak, a curse that has followed his family to this day.

The Hero has accepted the call for a divine crusader and has been sent to locate the lost Relics of the Crusader. After finding the lost Priory of the Nine and the ghost of its former members, the Hero has discovered the whereabouts of the relics. They have traveled to Chorrol to recover the lost Gauntlets of the Crusader.

After hearing about the massacre at the Chapel of Dibella, in Anvil, the Hero has set forth to find the Relics of the Crusader and stop the attacks led by Umaril the Unfeathered.

entities.name: Sir Henrik
entities.description:
Sir Henrik was a member of the old Knights of the Nine. He was one of the members of the knights, most had either left for the War of Red Diamond, or had left what they saw was a dying order. While many of the relics where taken into war, Henrik found the Shield of the Crusader and decided it was best to guard the shield and make sure it never entered the wrong hands.

With the help of some of his most trusted friends, he set off to Fort Bulwark with the plan on turning it into a safe haven for the Shield. Henrik and his comrades built many traps and puzzles to slow down and kill any invaders. However, Henrik died during a raid and never got to see the his work completed.

His spirit and first encountered by the Hero in the under-croft of the Priory of the Nine, guarding the Cuirass of the Crusader along with the rest of the great knights of his time. Henrik will tell the hero how to find the fort but will also warn him that the fort was made to defend the Shield for all time and will still contain many traps.

After hearing about the massacre at the Chapel of Dibella in Anvil, the Hero has set forth to find the Relics of the Crusader and stop the attacks led by Umaril the Unfeathered.

entities.name: Sir Juncan
entities.description:
Sir Juncan was a member of the Knights of the Nine. He was one of the knights that found the body of Sir Ralvas after he failed to recover the Mace of the Crusader, a quest he refused to help in while he looked for the Boots of the Crusader. He later discovered that the Boots were needed to get the Mace, and he blamed himself for the death of his friend. Juncan died of unknown causes while searching for the Boots.

Sir Juncan was able to stay out of the War of the Red Diamond, and believed that it was the knights getting into the wars of man that destroyed them.

His spirit is first encountered by the Hero while searching for the Cuirass of the Crusader in the undercroft of the Priory of the Nine. If the Hero succeeds in his fight against Juncan and the other Knights, he will assist the Hero in finding the Relics, in particular the Boots. He will then point the Hero to a Shrine of Kynareth, where the Boots are.

While searching for the Boots, the Knight Commander must speak to the worshipers at the shrine, who will lead the Knight to the Kynareth's Grotto outside the cave Kynareth's Grotto. If the trial is failed, they must be spoken to again to try again.

entities.name: Sir Ralvas
entities.description:
Sir Ralvas is a Dunmer ghost, and one of the original Knights of the Nine.

After the betrayal of Sir Berich, Sir Ralvas began questing for the Mace of the Crusader hoping that its recovery would save the order and reunite its members. He traveled to the Chapel of Zenithar in Leyawiin where the mace was believed to be located. The legends said that after the death of Pelinal Whitestrake, a messenger brought the mace to Leyawiin.

Years later Saint Kaladas built the Chapel to honor the story. After Kaladas died and was laid to rest, people who prayed at his tomb began to see a vision of the Mace on the other side of a long Chasm. Sir Ralvas tried countless times but was unable to reach the mace. He asked the other knights for help but none came to his aid. At last, after months of failing, Ralvas gave up and left the chapel broken and empty. His body was found by Sir Amiel and Sir Juncan, who took his body to the Priory to be laid to rest.

The Hero has answered the call and has set forth to find the remaining Relics of the Crusader. At the Priory of the Nine, they have discovered from Sir Ralvas, that the Mace of the Crusader can be found in the Chapel of Zenithar in Leyawiin.

entities.name: Sir Roderic
entities.description:
Sir Roderic is a balding knight from High Rock taking up the holy Pilgrimage as directed by the Prophet.

Before meeting the Prophet, Roderic was a sword for hire that had served on countless battles, and was a war hero in the War of Bend'r-Mahk.

After seeing the murders of the priest and priestess of the Chapel of Dibella in Anvil, he heard the Prophet saying that a Hero was needed to rally the faithful and save them. He accepted this and began his Pilgrimage, along with his squire, Lathon.

Both Sir Roderic and Lathon can be found riding together along the main roads of Cyrodiil, making their ways to the Shrines to the Nine Divines. If they encounter the Hero, Roderic will offer to let them join their journey, The Hero can take them up on their offer, or continue along their way.

entities.name: Sir Torolf
entities.description:
Sir Torolf was a Knight of the old Knights of the Nine. He was one of the original knights, happy to serve the will of the Nine Divines, but this ended when he joined the War of the Red Diamond and was killed in battle.

His soul now protects the Cuirass of the Crusader in the undercroft of the Priory of the Nine.

After hearing about the massacre at the Chapel of Dibella, in Anvil, the Hero has set forth to find the Relics of the Crusader and stop the attacks led by Umaril the Unfeathered.

After receiving the Blessing of Talos and the promoting of Knights, it is time to face Umaril the Unfeathered at Garlas Malatar. The Prophet has marked the keep where he is hiding.

entities.name: Skorm Snow-Strider
entities.description:
Skorm Snow-Strider was a Nord commander of a legion of Lord Harald's soldiers in 1E 139. Around this time he was leading a campaign in the region near Lake Honrich, to drive the Snow Elves north to the main host of his forces.

During his campaign, he inadvertently discovered a hidden stronghold of Dragon Cultists in the secluded monastery of Forelhost high in the Jerall Mountains. This surprised Skorm, as it was believed that they were all wiped out during the Dragon War. Deciding it was too big a threat to ignore, Skorm and his men attempted a preemptive strike to deal with the cult quickly, but it failed and a siege ensued for several weeks. To make matters worse, a blizzard struck, massively slowing down their advance.

With the help of a voice master, the main gate was breached, though the voice master was killed in the process. The cultists retreated into the interior of the monastery and collapsed the main stairway to block access to the refectory. Eventually, Skorm and his men took the fortress, but discovered the cultists had committed mass suicide, either by poison or slitting their wrists.

Within the catacombs they discovered a well, with several buckets already filled. Several thirsty soldiers drank the water, not knowing that it had been poisoned by the cultists, and died. Demoralized and now at half their original strength, Skorm abandoned the search for any cultist survivors and left the monastery to push his forces north the next day. He did, however, leave his journal behind in the hopes that eventually, someone would make sure that the cultists were eliminated for good.

entities.name: Snow Prince
entities.description:
The Snow Prince was a powerful Snow Elf warrior who lived on the island of Solstheim during the late Merethic Era. He was a much respected and loved ruler by his people but was killed in battle against the ancient Nords.

Towards the end of the Merethic Era, the Snow Elves had been hunted to near extinction by the invading armies of Ysgramor. Mereth had already been purged of Snow Elves, so the ancient Nords turned their attention to Solstheim where a great number of skirmishes were said to have taken place.

The Battle of the Moesring is considered to be the final stand between the Nord and Snow Elf armies. Initially, the ancient Nords cut great swaths through the enemy ranks with their superior weapons, and it was said that the slopes of the Moesring "ran red with Elf blood"

The tide turned when during the battle, The Snow Prince rode in on a "brilliant steed of pallid white." It was said that his spear and armor bore the radiant glow of unknown magicka. The Snow Prince inspired great hope and inspiration to the last remaining army of Snow Elves.

entities.name: Souls
entities.description:
Souls, also known as the Soul or the Animus, are a feature of living entities believed to be closely tied to their consciousness and the bodies they inhabit, encompassing both spiritual and physical aspects. All living beings on Nirn appear to possess a soul, although the souls of more intelligent and powerful creatures are generally considered to be "larger" and possess greater strength. Under normal circumstances, the mind and soul of a mortal are deeply intertwined.

Souls provide power to the various sentient races of Tamriel, the races of Men, Mer, and Beastfolk, and the creatures of Tamriel and Oblivion. The souls of the sentient races are considered "Black Souls", and can only be soul trapped in Black Soul Gems. If a Soul Gem is not filled with a soul of its respective size, the caster's soul can leak into the Soul Gem while touching it. White Souls are considered safer for use than Black Souls. It is said that when one begins working on the art of necromancy, their soul gets corrupted. When a soul has departed, it is possible, through the use of magic, to make the soul control an object, such as what happened with the soul of A'Tor, which powered the Soul Sword. It is said that Argonians get their soul from the Hist shortly after birth, and that upon death, their soul returns to the Hist.

The Daedra do not have a "soul" in the direct manner. Rather, when a Daedra is slain, its vestige returns to its realm of Oblivion to be reformed into a new body, following which they live again. The Daedra are born in Azure Plasm, a lightblue liquid found in the realms of Oblivion. Conjured Dremora can free themselves from their master by soul trapping them. During the Planemeld, Molag Bal held Soul Shriven in Coldharbour. After Varen Aquilarios attempted to become a Dragonborn, the Soulburst took place. The Soulburst resulted in the souls which originally meant to go to the Soul Cairn went to Coldharbour instead. Soul Shriven have strong feelings of emptiness, hunger, and desire. Soul Shriven also had great endurance, being capable of doing tasks for far longer, and sustain more injury, than a mortal could. When a Soul Shriven died, its body was entirely annihilated, which in turn, gave power to Molag Bal.
